sundar.36.cau1: Over there, ever since Hanumān burnt Laṅkā and went away, the demons have lived in dread. In their homes they all think: there is no saving the race of demons. ॥1॥
sundar.36.cau2: When he whose messenger's strength is beyond description comes himself, what good can come to the city? Hearing the townspeople's talk from her messengers, Mandodarī grew all the more distressed. ॥2॥
sundar.36.cau3: In private, with joined palms, she fell at her husband's feet and spoke words steeped in wise counsel: My husband, give up your hostility to Śrī Hari; take to heart what I say, for it is greatly for your good. ॥3॥
sundar.36.cau4: His messenger's deeds, when they so much as think of them, make the demons' wives miscarry. Call your minister and send his wife back in the minister's care, my husband, if you wish for your own good. ॥4॥
sundar.36.cau5: To the lotus-forest of your race Sītā has come like a winter night, bringing it grief. Listen, my lord: unless you give Sītā back, not even Śiva and Brahmā can do you any good. ॥5॥
sundar.36.do36: The arrows of Śrī Rāma are like a host of snakes, and the throng of demons like frogs. Before they swallow them up, give up your obstinacy and make some effort. ॥36॥
sundar.37.cau1: The wicked one heard her words, and he, notorious throughout the world for his arrogance, laughed: Truly, a woman's nature is timid; even in good times she is afraid; her heart is very faint. ॥1॥
sundar.37.cau2: If the monkey army comes, the poor demons will have something to eat and live on. That the wife of one in terror of whom the guardians of the worlds tremble should be afraid is a great joke. ॥2॥
sundar.37.cau3: With these words he laughed, clasped her to his breast and, showing her still greater affection, went off to the assembly. Mandodarī was anxious at heart, thinking that fate had turned against her husband. ॥3॥
sundar.37.cau4: As he sat in the assembly, news reached him that the whole army had come to the far shore of the ocean. He asked his ministers: Tell me what course is right. They all laughed: Simply stay silent and at ease. ॥4॥
sundar.37.cau5: When you conquered gods and demons it cost you no effort; what do men and monkeys count for? ॥5॥
sundar.37.do37: If minister, physician and guru, these three, speak pleasing words out of fear or hope, then kingdom, dharma and body, these three, soon perish. ॥37॥
sundar.38.cau1: That very state of things had come about for Rāvaṇa: his ministers praise him, making sure he hears it. Seeing his opportunity, Vibhīṣaṇa came and laid his head at the feet of his brother. ॥1॥
sundar.38.cau2: Then, with another bow, he sat down in his own seat and, once given leave, spoke: Gracious one, since you have asked me for my counsel, I speak for your good, dear brother, as far as my understanding allows. ॥2॥
sundar.38.cau3: One who wishes for his own welfare, good fame, good sense, a happy destiny and joys of many kinds, he should turn away, my lord, from the forehead of another man's wife, as one turns away from the moon of the fourth day. ॥3॥
sundar.38.cau4: Though one be sole lord of the fourteen worlds, he does not last if he is at enmity with living beings. A man may be an ocean of virtues and accomplished, yet if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good. ॥4॥
sundar.38.do38: Desire, anger, pride and greed are all, my lord, paths to hell. Give them all up and worship Śrī Rāma, whom the saints worship. ॥38॥
sundar.39.cau1: Dear brother, Śrī Rāma is not merely a king of men: he is lord of all the worlds, the Death even of Death. He is Brahman, the Lord, free from all ills and unborn, all-pervading, unconquerable, without beginning and without end. ॥1॥
sundar.39.cau2: The ocean of mercy, who works for the good of the earth, the brāhmaṇas, the cows and the gods, has taken a human body. He delights his devotees, destroys the hosts of the wicked and guards the Vedas and dharma. Listen, brother. ॥2॥
sundar.39.cau3: Give up your enmity and bow your head to him; Śrī Rāma ends the suffering of all who bow to him. My lord, give Sītā back to the Lord, and worship Śrī Rāma, who loves without any motive. ॥3॥
sundar.39.cau4: The Lord does not cast off even one who carries the sin of having wronged the whole world, once he goes to him for refuge. The very Lord whose name ends the three afflictions has appeared; understand this in your heart, Rāvaṇa. ॥4॥
sundar.39.do39क: Rāvaṇa, I fall at your feet over and over and entreat you: cast off pride, delusion and arrogance, and worship the Lord of Kosala. ॥39 (क)॥
sundar.39.do39ख: The sage Pulastya sent this message by way of his own disciple. Dear brother, finding a good moment, I have told it straight away to you, my lord. ॥39 (ख)॥
sundar.40.cau1: Mālyavān was a minister of great wisdom. He was much pleased to hear these words, and said: Dear one, your younger brother is an ornament of good counsel; take to heart what Vibhīṣaṇa is saying. ॥1॥
sundar.40.cau2: Rāvaṇa said: These two fools are praising the enemy. Will no one take them away? Is anyone there? Mālyavān then went home, and Vibhīṣaṇa, joining his palms, spoke again: ॥2॥
sundar.40.cau3: Good sense and ill sense dwell in every heart, my lord; so say the Purāṇas and the Vedas. Where there is good sense, there is prosperity of every kind; where there is ill sense, calamity comes in the end. ॥3॥
sundar.40.cau4: A perverse ill sense has settled in your heart, so you take a well-wisher for a foe and an enemy for a friend. Sītā is the night of doom for the race of demons, and it is she whom you love so greatly. ॥4॥
sundar.40.do40: Dear brother, I clasp your feet and ask you: grant this for love of me. Give Sītā to Śrī Rāma, so that no harm comes to you. ॥40॥
sundar.41.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa spoke words of right counsel, in agreement with the wise, the Purāṇas and the Vedas. On hearing them, Rāvaṇa rose in fury and said: Wretch, your death is now close at hand. ॥1॥
sundar.41.cau2: Fool, you have always lived because I let you live, and yet, simpleton, you favour the enemy's side. Tell me, wretch: who is there in the world whom I have not conquered by the strength of my arms? ॥2॥
sundar.41.cau3: You live in my city and love those ascetics. Fool, go and join them, and preach your counsel to them. With these words he kicked him, and his younger brother clasped his feet again and again. ॥3॥
sundar.41.cau4: Umā, this is the greatness of a saint: he does good even to one who does him harm. Vibhīṣaṇa said: You stand in a father's place for me; you were right to strike me. But it is in worshipping Śrī Rāma that your good lies, my lord. ॥4॥
sundar.41.cau5: With his ministers, Vibhīṣaṇa rose into the sky and went off, saying this for all to hear: ॥5॥
sundar.41.do41: Śrī Rāma is the Lord whose resolve always comes true, and your court is in the grip of death. I go now to take refuge with Śrī Rāma; do not lay the blame on me. ॥41॥
sundar.42.cau1: As soon as Vibhīṣaṇa set off, saying this, all of them were doomed to die. Pārvatī, scorn shown to a holy man at once destroys every good. ॥1॥
sundar.42.cau2: The moment Rāvaṇa cast Vibhīṣaṇa off, the luckless king lost all his splendour. Vibhīṣaṇa set out joyfully for Śrī Rāma, cherishing many hopes in his heart. ॥2॥
sundar.42.cau3: I shall go and see those lotus feet, rosy and soft, that bring joy to his servants: the feet whose touch saved the sage's wife, Ahalyā, and which made the Daṇḍaka forest holy. ॥3॥
sundar.42.cau4: The feet that Sītā, Janaka's daughter, holds to her heart, that ran over the ground after the deceitful deer, that bloom as lotuses in the lake that is Śiva's heart: what good fortune! I shall see those very feet. ॥4॥
sundar.42.do42: The feet on whose sandals Bharata has set his mind: today I shall go and behold those feet with these eyes of mine. ॥42॥
sundar.43.cau1: Thinking such loving thoughts, Vibhīṣaṇa soon reached this shore of the ocean. The monkeys saw him approaching and thought he must be an important envoy of the enemy. ॥1॥
sundar.43.cau2: Keeping him there, they went to the king of the monkeys and reported everything to him. Sugrīva said: O Lord of the Raghus, hear this: Rāvaṇa's brother is here to meet you. ॥2॥
sundar.43.cau3: The Lord said: Friend, what do you make of it? The king of the monkeys said: Listen, O king of men: no one can see through the wiles of the demons. Who knows why this shape-changer has come? ॥3॥
sundar.43.cau4: The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should keep him in bonds. The Lord said: Friend, you have weighed the policy well, but I am pledged to remove the fear of whoever comes to me for refuge. ॥4॥
sundar.43.cau5: Hanumān rejoiced at the Lord's words: the Lord is loving to those who seek his refuge. ॥5॥
sundar.43.do43: Those who abandon one who has come to them for refuge, judging that he may do them harm, they are base and full of sin; there is harm in even looking at them. ॥43॥
sundar.44.cau1: Even one who bears the guilt of killing millions of brāhmaṇas I do not abandon once he comes to me for refuge. The moment a soul turns to face me, the sins of millions of births are destroyed. ॥1॥
sundar.44.cau2: It is the very nature of a sinner that worship of me never pleases him. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me? ॥2॥
sundar.44.cau3: Only one whose mind is pure finds me; deceit, cunning and fault-finding do not please me. Should Rāvaṇa have sent him here to learn our secrets, still, king of the monkeys, we have nothing to fear and nothing to lose. ॥3॥
sundar.44.cau4: Friend, Lakṣmaṇa can kill in the blink of an eye every demon there is in the world. And if he has come to me for refuge out of fear, I will guard him as I guard my own life. ॥4॥
sundar.44.do44: The abode of mercy said with a smile: Bring him in either case. Crying victory to the compassionate Lord, Sugrīva set off, taking Aṅgada and Hanumān with him. ॥44॥
sundar.45.cau1: Respectfully placing him in front, the monkeys went to where Śrī Rāma, the mine of compassion, was. From far off Vibhīṣaṇa saw the two brothers, who give the gift of joy to the eyes. ॥1॥
sundar.45.cau2: Then, as he looked upon Śrī Rāma, abode of all beauty, he stood rooted, gazing unblinking, his eyelids held still. The Lord's arms were long, his eyes like red lotuses, his body dark, freeing from fear those who bow to him. ॥2॥
sundar.45.cau3: His shoulders were like a lion's and his broad chest shone; his face would charm the hearts of countless gods of love. Vibhīṣaṇa's eyes filled with tears and his whole body thrilled; steadying his mind, he spoke gently: ॥3॥
sundar.45.cau4: My Lord, I am the brother of Rāvaṇa, and was born in the race of demons, O protector of the gods. By nature I am fond of sin, and my body is of the dark quality (tamas), as the owl loves the darkness. ॥4॥
sundar.45.do45: I have come, Lord, having heard with my ears your fair fame, that you destroy the distress of worldly existence. Save me, save me, remover of suffering, giver of joy to those who seek refuge, O hero of the Raghus. ॥45॥
sundar.46.cau1: Seeing him prostrate himself after these words, the Lord rose at once, full of joy. The humble words pleased the Lord's heart; he gathered him in his mighty arms and held him to his heart. ॥1॥
sundar.46.cau2: Meeting him together with his younger brother, he seated him close by, and the Lord, who takes away his devotees' fear, said: Tell me, Lord of Laṅkā, how you and your family are; you live in an evil place. ॥2॥
sundar.46.cau3: You dwell day and night among a company of the wicked; how do you keep to dharma, friend? Your ways are all known to me: you are deeply versed in right conduct, and wrong does not please you. ॥3॥
sundar.46.cau4: Even a dwelling in hell is better, dear one; may the Creator never grant the company of the wicked. Vibhīṣaṇa said: O Lord of the Raghus, now that I have seen your feet I am well, for you have shown me mercy, knowing me as your servant. ॥4॥
sundar.46.do46: A soul knows no well-being, and its mind no rest even in a dream, until it gives up desire, the home of sorrow, and worships Śrī Rāma. ॥46॥
sundar.47.cau1: Many wicked ones, greed, delusion, envy, pride and vanity, dwell in the heart for as long as Śrī Rāma, holding his bow and arrows, with a quiver at his waist, does not dwell there. ॥1॥
sundar.47.cau2: Attachment is a pitch-dark night at its height, which delights the owls of craving and aversion. It lives in a soul's mind only until the Lord's majesty rises there like the sun. ॥2॥
sundar.47.cau3: Now I am well and my great fears are gone, O Rāma, for my eyes have seen your lotus feet. O compassionate Lord, the one to whom you are gracious is never touched by the three kinds of worldly pain. ॥3॥
sundar.47.cau4: I am a demon of very base nature and have never done a good deed. Yet the Lord, whose form does not come even into the meditation of sages, has joyfully clasped me to his heart. ॥4॥
sundar.47.do47: What good fortune is mine, boundless beyond measure, O Rāma, mass of grace and joy: with my own eyes I have seen the pair of lotus feet that Brahmā and Śiva serve. ॥47॥
sundar.48.cau1: Listen, friend: I tell you my own nature, which Kākabhuśuṇḍi, Śiva and Pārvatī know. If a man who is the enemy of all creation, moving and unmoving, comes in fear, looking to me for refuge, ॥1॥
sundar.48.cau2: and leaves behind pride, delusion, deceit and guile of every kind, I make him at once like a saint. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, house, friends and family: ॥2॥
sundar.48.cau3: one who gathers up the threads of attachment to all of these, twists them into a cord and with it ties his mind to my feet; who sees all with an equal eye, wants nothing at all, and whose mind holds no joy, grief or fear — ॥3॥
sundar.48.cau4: such a good man lives in my heart just as wealth lives in the heart of the greedy. Saints like you are dear to me; it is for no one else's sake that I take on a body. ॥4॥
sundar.48.do48: Those who worship God with form and attributes, who are intent on the good of others and firm in right conduct and in their observances: such men, who love the feet of brāhmaṇas, are as dear to me as my own life. ॥48॥
sundar.49.cau1: Listen, lord of Laṅkā: all these virtues are yours, and so you are exceedingly dear to me. Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, all the troops of monkeys cry: Glory to the sum of all mercy! ॥1॥
sundar.49.cau2: As Vibhīṣaṇa listens to the Lord's words he cannot have enough of them, knowing them to be nectar to the ears. Again and again he clasps the Lord's lotus feet; the boundless love in his heart cannot be held within it. ॥2॥
sundar.49.cau3: Listen, my Lord, master of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow before you, you who know every heart from within: at first there was some desire in my heart, but it has been carried away by the river of love for the Lord's feet. ॥3॥
sundar.49.cau4: Now, compassionate Lord, give me devotion to you, which makes one pure and is ever dear to Śiva's mind. The Lord, unshaken in battle, said: So be it, and at once called for water from the ocean. ॥4॥
sundar.49.cau5: Friend, though you have no desire, the sight of me never fails to bear fruit in this world. With these words Śrī Rāma anointed him with the tilaka, and a boundless shower of flowers fell from the sky. ॥5॥
sundar.49.do49क: Vibhīṣaṇa was burning in the fire of Rāvaṇa's anger, which the fierce wind of his own breath had fanned; Śrī Rāma saved him and gave him a kingdom that would never be broken. ॥49 (क)॥
sundar.49.do49ख: The wealth that Śiva gave Rāvaṇa when he offered up his ten heads, that same wealth Śrī Rāma gave to Vibhīṣaṇa, and gave it with diffidence. ॥49 (ख)॥
sundar.50.cau1: Those who leave such a Lord and worship another are beasts without tail or horns. Knowing Vibhīṣaṇa for his own devotee, the Lord took him as his own; and the Lord's nature delighted the whole monkey race. ॥1॥
sundar.50.cau2: Then the Lord, who knows all and dwells in every heart, who is every form and yet free of all and detached, the upholder of right counsel, who for a purpose became a man and destroys the race of demons, spoke these words: ॥2॥
sundar.50.cau3: Listen, heroes, king of the monkeys and lord of Laṅkā: how is this deep ocean to be crossed? It teems with crocodiles, serpents and fish of every kind; it is fathomless, and hard to cross in every way. ॥3॥
sundar.50.cau4: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen. Your arrow could dry up ten million oceans. Even so, policy teaches that one should go to the Ocean and make a humble request. ॥4॥
sundar.50.do50: My Lord, the Ocean is a revered elder of your line. He will think it over and tell you a way, and the entire army of bears and monkeys will get across the ocean without effort. ॥50॥
sundar.51.cau1: Friend, the way you have told me is a good one; let it be tried, if fate is on our side. This counsel did not please Lakṣmaṇa; hearing Śrī Rāma's words, he was deeply troubled. ॥1॥
sundar.51.cau2: My Lord, what reliance can be placed on fate? Dry up the ocean; let your mind be roused to anger. Fate is the one prop of a coward's mind; it is the idle who keep crying out, Fate, fate. ॥2॥
sundar.51.cau3: On hearing this Śrī Rāma laughed and said: That is just what I shall do; keep your mind steady. With these words the Lord reassured his younger brother and went down to the ocean. ॥3॥
sundar.51.cau4: First he bowed his head in salutation; then he spread kuśa grass on the shore and sat down. When Vibhīṣaṇa came to the Lord, Rāvaṇa had sent spies after him. ॥4॥
sundar.51.do51: Disguised in the bodies of monkeys, they watched all that took place, and in their hearts they praised the virtues of the Lord and the love he bears for one who comes to him for refuge. ॥51॥
sundar.52.cau1: They began to praise Śrī Rāma's nature openly, and in their great love they forgot to keep up their disguise. Then the monkeys knew them for the enemy's spies, tied them all up and took them before Sugrīva, king of the monkeys. ॥1॥
sundar.52.cau2: Sugrīva said: Listen, all you monkeys: mutilate these demons and send them back. At Sugrīva's words the monkeys rushed at them, bound them and led them round the whole camp. ॥2॥
sundar.52.cau3: The monkeys began to beat them in many ways; though they cried out piteously, still the monkeys would not release them. Then they cried: Whoever cuts off our noses and ears, we charge him by the Lord of Kosala. ॥3॥
sundar.52.cau4: Hearing this, Lakṣmaṇa called them all to him. He was moved to pity, and with a laugh had them set free at once, and said: Put this letter into Rāvaṇa's hand and tell him: Read Lakṣmaṇa's words, you destroyer of your own race. ॥4॥
sundar.52.do52: And give that fool my generous message by word of mouth: Hand Sītā back and come and meet Śrī Rāma, or else your death has come. ॥52॥
sundar.53.cau1: At once the spies bowed their heads at Lakṣmaṇa's feet and set out, recounting a tale of virtues. Telling of Śrī Rāma's glory all the way, they came to Laṅkā and bowed their heads at Rāvaṇa's feet. ॥1॥
sundar.53.cau2: Rāvaṇa laughed and asked: Śuka, why don't you tell me how you are? Then give me news of Vibhīṣaṇa, whose death has drawn very near. ॥2॥
sundar.53.cau3: The fool gave up Laṅkā, where he lived in royal state; now the wretch will be crushed like a weevil in the barley. Then tell me about the army of bears and monkeys: cruel death has impelled it to march here. ॥3॥
sundar.53.cau4: That poor soft-hearted Ocean has become the guardian of their lives. And then tell me about those ascetics, whose hearts are full of dread of me. ॥4॥
sundar.53.do53: Have you met them, or did they turn back as soon as my fair fame reached their ears? Why don't you tell me of the might and splendour of the enemy's army? Your mind seems utterly dazed. ॥53॥
sundar.54.cau1: My lord, as graciously as you have asked, so accept what I tell you, setting your anger aside. When your younger brother went over to them, Rāma anointed him with the tilaka the moment he arrived. ॥1॥
sundar.54.cau2: As soon as the monkeys heard we were spies sent by Rāvaṇa, they tied us up and made us suffer in many ways. They started cutting off our ears and noses, and only when we bound them by an oath in Rāma's name did they let us go. ॥2॥
sundar.54.cau3: You asked about Rāma's army, my lord: a thousand million mouths could not describe it. Its bears and monkeys are of many colours, with fearsome faces, huge and terrifying. ॥3॥
sundar.54.cau4: He who burned the city and killed your son has the least strength of all those monkeys. There are warriors of countless names, tough and terrible, huge and mighty, with the strength of countless elephants. ॥4॥
sundar.54.do54: Among them are Dvivida and Mainda, Nīla and Nala, Aṅgada and Gada, Vikaṭāsya and Dadhimukha, Kesarī, Niśaṭha and Śaṭha, and Jāmbavān — every one of them a mountain of strength. ॥54॥
sundar.55.cau1: All these monkeys are equal to Sugrīva, and there are millions like them; who could count so many? By Rāma's grace their strength is beyond compare; they think of the three worlds as no more than a blade of grass. ॥1॥
sundar.55.cau2: This I have heard with my own ears, Rāvaṇa: the monkey troop-leaders number eighteen padmas (a padma being an immense number). In that army, my lord, there is no monkey who would not defeat you in battle. ॥2॥
sundar.55.cau3: In utter fury they all wring their hands, but Rāma gives them no order. They will dry up the ocean, fish, serpents and all, or else fill it in with great mountains, ॥3॥
sundar.55.cau4: and crush Rāvaṇa and grind him into the dust: such are the words all the monkeys speak. Fearless by nature, they roar and threaten, as though they longed to swallow Laṅkā whole. ॥4॥
sundar.55.do55: The monkeys and bears are all heroes by nature, and over their heads besides is the Lord Rāma. Rāvaṇa, they could conquer ten million Deaths in battle. ॥55॥
sundar.56.cau1: The splendour, strength and wisdom of Rāma are so vast that a hundred thousand Śeṣas (the thousand-headed serpent) could not sing of them. He can dry up a hundred oceans with a single arrow, yet, skilled in policy as he is, he asked your brother's counsel. ॥1॥
sundar.56.cau2: On his advice he is asking the Ocean for a way across, with mercy in his heart. Hearing this, Rāvaṇa laughed: With wits like these, no wonder he has made monkeys his allies. ॥2॥
sundar.56.cau3: Relying on the word of a born coward, he has taken to sulking and pestering the Ocean like a spoilt child. Fool, why do you sing false praises? I have taken the measure of my enemy's strength and wit. ॥3॥
sundar.56.cau4: Where in the world can victory and glory be found for one whose counsellor is the timid Vibhīṣaṇa? At these words of the wicked one the spy grew angrier, and judging the moment right, he drew out the letter. ॥4॥
sundar.56.cau5: Rāma's younger brother gave me this letter. My lord, have it read out and let it cool your breast. Rāvaṇa laughed and took it in his left hand, and the fool called his minister and had him begin to read it. ॥5॥
sundar.56.do56क: Fool, do not humour your mind with mere talk and so bring your race to ruin. Opposing Śrī Rāma, you will find no escape, even if you take refuge with Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva. ॥56 (क)॥
sundar.56.do56ख: Either give up your pride and, like your younger brother, become a bee at the Lord's lotus feet, or else, wicked one, become a moth with all your race in the flame of Śrī Rāma's arrows. ॥56 (ख)॥
sundar.57.cau1: Hearing the letter, Rāvaṇa was afraid at heart, but with a smile on his face he said for all to hear: Like someone lying flat on the ground reaching up to seize the sky: such is the big talk of the younger ascetic. ॥1॥
sundar.57.cau2: Śuka said: My lord, every word of it is true; set aside your proud nature and understand it. Put away your anger and hear what I say: my lord, give up your enmity with Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
sundar.57.cau3: Śrī Rāma's nature is very gentle, though he is king of all the worlds. The moment you meet him the Lord will show you grace; he will not keep a single offence of yours in his heart. ॥3॥
sundar.57.cau4: Hand Sītā over to Śrī Rāma; my lord, do this much that I ask. When Śuka spoke of giving Sītā back, the wicked Rāvaṇa kicked him. ॥4॥
sundar.57.cau5: Śuka bowed his head to Rāvaṇa's feet and went to where Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, was. He bowed to him and told his story, and by Śrī Rāma's grace he regained his own true state. ॥5॥
sundar.57.cau6: Pārvatī, by the curse of the sage Agastya he had become a demon; before that he had been a wise sage. Bowing again and again at Śrī Rāma's feet, the sage went back to his hermitage. ॥6॥
sundar.57.do57: The dull Ocean would not heed the entreaty, and three days went by. Then Śrī Rāma said in anger: Without fear there is no love. ॥57॥
sundar.58.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa, bring the bow and arrows; let me dry up the ocean with the fire of an arrow. Entreaty to the wicked, love for the crooked, fine counsel to one who is a miser by nature, ॥1॥
sundar.58.cau2: talk of wisdom to one wrapped up in attachment, praise of dispassion to the very greedy, talk of calm to the wrathful and the story of Śrī Hari to the lustful: all these bear the same fruit as seed sown in barren ground. ॥2॥
sundar.58.cau3: With these words Śrī Rāma strung his bow, and this view pleased Lakṣmaṇa. The Lord fitted a terrible arrow, and flames rose within the ocean's heart. ॥3॥
sundar.58.cau4: Crocodiles, serpents and shoals of fish were thrown into distress. When the Ocean knew that the creatures were burning, he filled a golden platter with gems of many kinds and, setting aside his pride, came in the form of a brāhmaṇa. ॥4॥
sundar.58.do58: However much one waters it, with endless care, a banana plant bears fruit only when it is cut. Listen, Garuḍa: the base do not heed a humble request; they bend only when rebuked. ॥58॥
sundar.59.cau1: The Ocean, afraid, took hold of the Lord's feet: Forgive all my faults, my Lord. Sky, wind, fire, water and earth, my Lord, are by their very nature dull in what they do. ॥1॥
sundar.59.cau2: Impelled by you, māyā brought them forth for the work of creation; so all the scriptures sing. Whatever the Lord has commanded for each, each finds happiness in keeping to it. ॥2॥
sundar.59.cau3: My Lord, you did well to teach me a lesson; yet the bounds were set by you as well. A drum, the unlettered, a śūdra, an animal and a woman: all of these are meant to receive instruction. ॥3॥
sundar.59.cau4: Through the Lord's might I shall dry up, and the army will get across, but there is no glory for me in that. The Lord's command cannot be set aside, the Vedas sing; whatever pleases you, I will do it at once. ॥4॥
sundar.59.do59: Hearing these most humble words, the compassionate Lord smiled and said: Dear one, tell me the way by which the monkey army may cross. ॥59॥
sundar.60.cau1: My Lord, the monkeys Nīla and Nala are two brothers who received a sage's blessing in childhood. At their touch, even massive mountains will float upon the ocean through your glory. ॥1॥
sundar.60.cau2: I too, holding the Lord's greatness in my heart, will help as far as my strength allows. Have the ocean bridged in this manner, my Lord, so that the three worlds may sing this fair renown. ॥2॥
sundar.60.cau3: With this arrow, my Lord, slay the wicked men who live on my northern shore, heaps of sin that they are. Hearing of the pain in the Ocean's heart, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, steadfast in battle, took it away at once. ॥3॥
sundar.60.cau4: Seeing Śrī Rāma's mighty strength and valour, the Ocean rejoiced and was at ease. He told the Lord all the deeds of those wicked men, bowed at his feet and departed. ॥4॥
sundar.60.cha1: The Ocean went to his own home, and this counsel pleased Śrī Rāma. This story washes away the impurity of the Kali age; the servant Tulasīdāsa has sung it as far as his understanding allows. The virtues of Śrī Rāma are a home of happiness; they put doubt to rest and destroy sorrow. Foolish mind, let go of every hope and every reliance, and sing and hear them always. ॥1॥
sundar.60.do60: Singing the praises of Śrī Rāma brings every blessing. Whoever listens to them with reverence crosses the ocean of worldly existence without a boat. ॥60॥
uttar.0.shloka1: I bow ceaselessly to him who is blue as a peacock's throat, the best of the gods, adorned with the print of the Brahmin's (Bhṛgu's) lotus foot, rich in beauty, clad in yellow, lotus-eyed, at all times full of gladness; who holds arrow and bow in his hand, with hosts of monkeys about him, served by his brother; the adorable lord of Jānakī, the best of the Raghus, Rāma seated on the Puṣpaka. ॥1॥
uttar.0.shloka2: The two lotus feet of the king of Kosala are lovely and tender, worshipped by Brahmā and the great Śiva; caressed by Jānakī's lotus hands, they are the companions of the bee that is the mind of one who meditates on them. ॥2॥
uttar.0.shloka3: Fair and handsome as jasmine, the moon and the conch, the husband of Ambikā, the giver of the success one longs for, compassionate, with lovely lotus eyes: I bow to Śaṅkara, who sets one free from Kāma, the god of desire. ॥3॥
uttar.0.dou1: Only one day of the appointed term was left, and the people of the city were in deep distress. Everywhere women and men, worn thin by separation from Śrī Rāma, were sunk in anxious thought.
uttar.0.dou2: Fair omens of every kind appeared, and everyone's heart was glad. As if announcing the Lord's coming, the city grew delightful on every side.
uttar.0.dou3: Kausalyā and all the other mothers felt such joy in their hearts as if someone were just about to tell them: The Lord has come, with Sītā and his younger brother.
uttar.0.dou4: Again and again Bharata's right eye and his right arm quivered. Taking it for a good omen, he was overjoyed at heart, and he began to ponder.
uttar.1.cau1: Of the term that was his one support only a day remained; as he grasped this, his mind filled with boundless grief. What can be the reason that my Lord has not come? Or has he forgotten me, knowing me to be crooked? ॥1॥
uttar.1.cau2: Ah, blessed and fortunate is Lakṣmaṇa, who loves the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma. The Lord saw that I am deceitful and crooked, and so my master did not take me along. ॥2॥
uttar.1.cau3: Were the Lord to judge me by what I have done, a thousand million kalpas would not see me saved. But the Lord never holds his servant's faults against him; he is the friend of the lowly, and his nature is very gentle. ॥3॥
uttar.1.cau4: In my heart there is that one firm trust: I shall meet Śrī Rāma; the omens too are good. If my life remains once the term is past, who in the world will be as base as I? ॥4॥
uttar.1.do1क: In the ocean of Śrī Rāma's absence Bharata's mind was going under, and just then the son of the Wind arrived, dressed as a Brahmin, as though a ship had come. ॥1 (क)॥
uttar.1.do1ख: He saw Bharata seated on a mat of kuśa grass, his matted locks for a crown, his body worn thin, repeating Rāma, Rāma, Raghupati, tears flowing from his lotus eyes. ॥1 (ख)॥
uttar.2.cau1: At the sight Hanumān rejoiced greatly; his body thrilled and his eyes rained tears. Delighted in his heart in many ways, he spoke words that were like nectar to the ears: ॥1॥
uttar.2.cau2: He for whom you grieve day and night in separation, whose virtues you recite without pause, row upon row, the jewel of Raghu's line, the giver of joy to the good, the protector of gods and sages, has come safe and well. ॥2॥
uttar.2.cau3: He has conquered the enemy in battle, the gods sing his fair fame, and the Lord is on his way with Sītā and his younger brother. Hearing this, Bharata forgot every sorrow, as one parched with thirst does on finding nectar. ॥3॥
uttar.2.cau4: Bharata said: Who are you, dear friend, and where have you come from? You have told me the dearest of news. Hanumān said: Hear my name, O treasury of compassion: I am Hanumān, a monkey, son of the Wind. ॥4॥
uttar.2.cau5: I am a servant of Śrī Rāma, the friend of the lowly. At these words Bharata stood up and, with great respect, held him to his heart. As they met, his heart could not hold his love; tears streamed from his eyes and his body thrilled. ॥5॥
uttar.2.cau6: Bharata said: Hanumān, at the sight of you all my sorrows are over; today I have met my beloved Śrī Rāma. Again and again he asked how all were, and said: Listen, brother, what can I give you? ॥6॥
uttar.2.cau7: I have thought it over and found nothing in the world to equal this message. Dear friend, I can never be free of my debt to you. Now tell me the story of the Lord. ॥7॥
uttar.2.cau8: Then Hanumān, his head bowed at Bharata's feet, told him all the tale of Śrī Rāma's virtues. Bharata said: Tell me, Hanumān, does my compassionate master ever remember me as his servant? ॥8॥
uttar.2.cha1: Has the jewel of the Raghu line ever remembered me as his own servant? Hearing Bharata's most humble words, Hanumān, his body thrilling, fell at his feet. One whose many virtues Śrī Rāma, lord of all that moves and all that is still, tells of with his own lips, how could he not be humble, supremely pure, an ocean of good qualities? ॥1॥
uttar.2.do2क: Hanumān said: My lord, you are as dear to Śrī Rāma as his own life; what I say is true, dear one. Hearing this, Bharata embraced him again and again, his heart unable to contain its joy. ॥2 (क)॥
uttar.2.so2ख: Hanumān bowed his head at Bharata's feet and hurried straight back to Śrī Rāma. Reaching him, he gave the news that all were well; then the Lord, glad at heart, mounted the aerial car and set off. ॥2 (ख)॥
uttar.3.cau1: Bharata came joyfully back to the city of Kosala and gave his guru all the news. Then he made it known in the palace that Śrī Rāma was coming to the city safe and well. ॥1॥
uttar.3.cau2: Hearing it, all the mothers rose and ran; Bharata told them the Lord was well and reassured them. When the townspeople had the news, all of them, men and women, ran out in joy. ॥2॥
uttar.3.cau3: Curds, dūrvā grass, gorocana, fruit, flowers and fresh tulasī leaves, the root of all blessing: heaping these on golden platters, women moving with an elephant's graceful gait went out singing. ॥3॥
uttar.3.cau4: Everyone runs out just as they are, not stopping to bring children or the old along. They ask one another: Brother, have you seen Śrī Rāma, the compassionate? ॥4॥
uttar.3.cau5: Ayodhyā, knowing the Lord was on his way, became a treasure-house of every kind of beauty. A pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant, and the Sarayū's water grew perfectly clear. ॥5॥
uttar.3.do3क: Joyful, with the guru, the family, his younger brother and a throng of Brahmins, Bharata, his heart full of love, went out to meet Śrī Rāma, the abode of grace. ॥3 (क)॥
uttar.3.do3ख: Many women climbed to the upper rooms and gazed at the aerial car in the sky. Seeing it, they sang auspicious songs in sweet voices, full of joy. ॥3 (ख)॥
uttar.3.do3ग: Ayodhyā was an ocean that rejoiced at the sight of its full moon, Śrī Rāma; it swelled with a roar of voices, and the women seemed its waves. ॥3 (ग)॥
uttar.4.cau1: Here Śrī Rāma, the sun to the lotus of the solar race, was showing the monkeys the lovely city. He said: Listen, Sugrīva, Aṅgada and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā. This city is holy and this land is beautiful. ॥1॥
uttar.4.cau2: Though all have praised Vaikuṇṭha, which the Vedas and Purāṇas make known and the world knows of, even it is not as dear to me as Ayodhyā; only a rare few understand this. ॥2॥
uttar.4.cau3: This lovely city is where I was born; the holy Sarayū flows along its northern side, and whoever bathes in it comes, with no labour at all, to live close to me. ॥3॥
uttar.4.cau4: The people who live here are very dear to me; this city is a store of happiness and bestows my own abode. All the monkeys rejoiced to hear the Lord's words: blessed is Ayodhyā, which Śrī Rāma has praised. ॥4॥
uttar.4.do4क: The Lord, the ocean of mercy, saw all the people coming, and he directed the aerial car; it came down to the ground near the city. ॥4 (क)॥
uttar.4.do4ख: When he had alighted, the Lord said to Puṣpaka: Go to Kubera. At Śrī Rāma's bidding it set off, glad, yet sorely grieved to be parted from him. ॥4 (ख)॥
uttar.5.cau1: All the people came with Bharata, their bodies worn thin by separation from Śrī Rāma. The Lord saw Vāmadeva and Vasiṣṭha, chief among sages, and laying his bow and arrows on the ground, ॥1॥
uttar.5.cau2: he ran to his guru and caught hold of his lotus feet; he and his younger brother thrilled from head to foot. The king of sages embraced him and asked if all was well. The Lord said: We are well by your mercy alone. ॥2॥
uttar.5.cau3: Śrī Rāma, lord of Raghu's line and upholder of dharma, greeted all the Brahmins with a bow of the head. Next Bharata took hold of those lotus feet of the Lord before which gods, sages, Śiva and Brahmā bow. ॥3॥
uttar.5.cau4: He lay on the ground and would not rise when they tried to lift him; then the ocean of mercy raised him by force and held him to his heart. The hair on the Lord's dark body stood on end, and his eyes, like fresh lotuses, brimmed with tears. ॥4॥
uttar.5.cha1: Tears flow from his lotus eyes, and the hair on his lovely body stands on end. With deep love the Lord, master of the three worlds, held his younger brother to his heart. How the Lord looks as he meets his brother, I cannot find a likeness to tell. It is as if love and śṛṅgāra, the spirit of beauty, had taken bodies and met, and gained a matchless loveliness. ॥1॥
uttar.5.cha2: The treasury of mercy asks Bharata how he is, but words do not come quickly to him. Listen, Śivā: that joy lies beyond words and mind; only one who finds it knows it. Bharata said: All is well now, Lord of Kosala; knowing your servant to be in distress, you have given him the sight of you. As I was drowning in the ocean of separation, the treasury of compassion took me by the hand. ॥2॥
uttar.5.do5: Then the Lord joyfully embraced Śatrughna, holding him to his heart. Then Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, the two brothers, met in the deepest love. ॥5॥
uttar.6.cau1: Then Lakṣmaṇa embraced Bharata's younger brother, ending the unbearable grief that separation had brought. Bharata bowed his head at Sītā's feet and, with his younger brother, found the highest joy. ॥1॥
uttar.6.cau2: The townspeople rejoiced to see the Lord; all the hardship born of separation vanished. Seeing everyone restless with love, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, worked a wonder. ॥2॥
uttar.6.cau3: At that moment the compassionate Lord appeared in countless forms and met each person as was fitting. Śrī Rāma looked on them with grace and freed every man and woman from sorrow. ॥3॥
uttar.6.cau4: In an instant the Lord met everyone; Umā, no one knew this secret. Having thus made all happy, Śrī Rāma, the home of goodness and virtue, went on ahead. ॥4॥
uttar.6.cau5: Kausalyā and all the mothers ran, like newly calved cows that catch sight of their calves. ॥5॥
uttar.6.cha1: It was as if cows had left their young calves at home and gone, against their will, to graze in the forest, and at the end of the day ran lowing towards the town, milk dripping from their udders. With deep love the Lord met all the mothers and spoke gentle words to them in many ways. The harsh hardship born of separation was gone, and they found joy and happiness beyond count. ॥1॥
uttar.6.do6क: Sumitrā embraced her son, knowing his love for Śrī Rāma's feet. Meeting Śrī Rāma, Kaikeyī felt deeply abashed at heart. ॥6 (क)॥
uttar.6.do6ख: Lakṣmaṇa met all the mothers and rejoiced to receive their blessings. He met Kaikeyī again and again, yet the unrest in his mind would not go. ॥6 (ख)॥
uttar.7.cau1: Sītā met all her mothers-in-law, and touching their feet she was filled with joy. Asking after her welfare, they bless her: May your married happiness stay unshaken. ॥1॥
uttar.7.cau2: They all gaze on Śrī Rāma's lotus face and, knowing the hour to be auspicious, hold back the tears in their eyes. They wave the lamps on golden platters and look again and again at the Lord's form. ॥2॥
uttar.7.cau3: They make offerings over him in many ways, and their hearts fill with supreme bliss and joy. Again and again Kausalyā looks at Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, steadfast in battle. ॥3॥
uttar.7.cau4: She wonders in her heart again and again: How did he kill the lord of Laṅkā? My two boys are so tender, and the demons were great warriors of immense strength. ॥4॥
uttar.7.do7: The mother gazes at the Lord with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā; her heart is immersed in supreme bliss, and again and again her body thrills. ॥7॥
uttar.8.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Nala, Nīla, Jāmbavān and the noble Aṅgada, Hanumān and all the other monkey heroes had taken on charming human forms. ॥1॥
uttar.8.cau2: Bharata's affection, his goodness, his vows and his discipline: all of them tell of these with reverence and deep love. Seeing the ways of the townsfolk, they all praise their love for the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
uttar.8.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma called all his friends and taught them all: Bow at the sage's feet. This is Guru Vasiṣṭha, revered by our family; by his grace the demons were slain in battle. ॥3॥
uttar.8.cau4: Listen, sage: these are all my friends; in the ocean of battle they became my rafts. For my good they put their lives at stake; I hold them dearer even than Bharata. ॥4॥
uttar.8.cau5: Hearing the Lord's words they were all overwhelmed; with every moment fresh joys rose in them. ॥5॥
uttar.8.do8क: Next they bent their heads at Kausalyā's feet. She blessed them with joy: You are as dear to me as Rāma. ॥8 (क)॥
uttar.8.do8ख: Flowers rained down till the sky was thick with them, and Śrī Rāma, the source of joy, went on towards the palace. Crowds of the city's women and men climbed to the balconies to watch him. ॥8 (ख)॥
uttar.9.cau1: Everyone adorned golden pitchers in wonderful ways and set them, decked, at their own doors. For good fortune all put up festoons, banners and flags. ॥1॥
uttar.9.cau2: All the lanes were sprinkled with fragrance, and many auspicious squares were drawn with elephant-pearls. Auspicious things of every kind were arranged, and in joy many kettledrums sounded through the city. ॥2॥
uttar.9.cau3: Everywhere women make offerings over him and, hearts brimming with joy, give their blessings. Young women arrange many lamps on golden platters and sing auspicious songs. ॥3॥
uttar.9.cau4: They wave the lamps before the remover of distress, the sun to the lotus-forest of the Raghu line. The Vedas, Śeṣa and Sarasvatī have described the beauty, wealth and well-being of the city; ॥4॥
uttar.9.cau5: yet even they are left spellbound at the sight of this; then how, Umā, can mortals tell of his virtues? ॥5॥
uttar.9.do9क: The women were night-lotuses in the lake of Ayodhyā, and separation from Śrī Rāma was the sun; now that it has set, they have blossomed at the sight of the moon that is Śrī Rāma. ॥9 (क)॥
uttar.9.do9ख: Good omens of many kinds appear, and drums sound in the sky. Having given the men and women of the city their lord again, the Lord went on to the palace. ॥9 (ख)॥
uttar.10.cau1: Knowing that Kaikeyī was ashamed, Pārvatī, the Lord went first to her house. He comforted her and gave her great happiness, and then Śrī Hari went to his own palace. ॥1॥
uttar.10.cau2: When the ocean of mercy entered the palace, all the men and women of the city were happy. Guru Vasiṣṭha sent for the Brahmins and said: Today the hour is good, the day is good, everything has come together. ॥2॥
uttar.10.cau3: All you Brahmins, gladly give your command that Śrī Rāma take his seat on the throne. The sage Vasiṣṭha's pleasing words delighted all the Brahmins as soon as they heard them. ॥3॥
uttar.10.cau4: Many Brahmins said in gentle words: Śrī Rāma's coronation gladdens the whole world. Now, best of sages, make no delay; place the mark of kingship on the Mahārāja's brow. ॥4॥
uttar.10.do10क: Then the sage spoke to Sumantra, who set off gladly as soon as he heard, and going at once he had many chariots, horses and elephants made ready. ॥10 (क)॥
uttar.10.do10ख: Then, sending runners here and there, he had auspicious things brought, and coming back he joyfully bowed his head at Vasiṣṭha's feet. ॥10 (ख)॥
uttar.11.cau1: The city of Ayodhyā was decked most beautifully, and the gods let fall a steady shower of flowers. Śrī Rāma sent for his servants and told them: First go and bathe my friends. ॥1॥
uttar.11.cau2: At these words people ran here and there and at once bathed Sugrīva and the rest. Then Śrī Rāma, treasury of compassion, called Bharata and with his own hands untangled his matted hair. ॥2॥
uttar.11.cau3: The Lord, the gracious Śrī Rāma who loves his devotees, bathed all three brothers. Bharata's good fortune and the Lord's tenderness could not be sung by a thousand million Śeṣas. ॥3॥
uttar.11.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma untangled his own matted locks and, asking the Guru's leave, bathed. After bathing the Lord put on his ornaments; seeing his limbs, a hundred Kāmadevas felt ashamed. ॥4॥
uttar.11.do11क: With honour the mothers-in-law quickly bathed Sītā, and dressed every limb with care in heavenly garments and fine ornaments. ॥11 (क)॥
uttar.11.do11ख: On Śrī Rāma's left shines Ramā (Sītā), a mine of beauty and virtue. Seeing it, all the mothers rejoiced, counting their lives fulfilled. ॥11 (ख)॥
uttar.11.do11ग: Listen, Garuḍa: at that time Brahmā, Śiva, hosts of sages and all the gods came mounted on their aerial chariots to see the source of joy. ॥11 (ग)॥
uttar.12.cau1: Seeing the Lord, the sage's heart filled with love, and at once he called for a heavenly throne. Its radiance, like the sun's, was beyond words; Śrī Rāma bowed to the Brahmins and sat upon it. ॥1॥
uttar.12.cau2: Seeing Śrī Rāma with Sītā, daughter of Janaka, the whole company of sages rejoiced greatly. Then the Brahmins chanted Vedic mantras, and in the sky gods and sages cried out: Victory, victory! ॥2॥
uttar.12.cau3: First the sage Vasiṣṭha applied the tilaka, then he gave leave to all the Brahmins. The mothers rejoiced to see their son and waved the lamps before him again and again. ॥3॥
uttar.12.cau4: The Brahmins received gifts of many kinds, and every beggar was made one who need never beg. Seeing the master of the three worlds on the throne, the gods beat their drums. ॥4॥
uttar.12.cha1: Countless drums sound in the sky; gandharvas and kinnaras sing. Troupes of apsarās dance, and gods and sages find supreme bliss. Bharata and the other younger brothers, with Vibhīṣaṇa, Aṅgada, Hanumān and the rest, stand resplendent, holding the parasol, the whisk, the fan, the bow, the sword, the shield and the spear. ॥1॥
uttar.12.cha2: With Sītā beside him, the jewel of the solar line shines with the beauty of many Kāmadevas. The yellow garment on his beautiful body, dark as a fresh rain-cloud, enchants the minds of the gods. Crown, armlets and other wonderful ornaments adorn every limb. His eyes are lotuses, his chest and arms are mighty; blessed are those who behold him. ॥2॥
uttar.12.do12क: Garuḍa, that splendour, that assembly and that joy cannot be told. Sarasvatī, Śeṣa and the Vedas describe it, and its savour is known to Maheśa. ॥12 (क)॥
uttar.12.do12ख: Each offering his own praise, the gods went back to their own realms. Then the Vedas, in the guise of bards, came to where Śrī Rāma was. ॥12 (ख)॥
uttar.12.do12ग: The all-knowing Lord, the treasury of mercy, received them with great honour. No one grasped the secret at all, and they began to sing his praises. ॥12 (ग)॥
uttar.13.cha1: Glory to you, who are with form and beyond form, of form beyond compare, crest-jewel of kings. By the strength of your arms you slew Rāvaṇa and the other fierce, mighty and wicked demons. Taking birth as a man, you broke the burden of the world and burned away its cruel sorrows. Glory to you, compassionate Lord, protector of those who bow to you; we bow to you together with your Śakti, Sītā. ॥1॥
uttar.13.cha2: O Hari, gods and demons, nāgas and men, all that moves and does not move, under the sway of your hard māyā (the Lord's power of illusion), wander for countless days and nights on the road of worldly existence, filled with time, karma and the guṇas. Those on whom you have looked with compassion, my Lord, are freed from the threefold suffering. O Rāma, skilled in cutting away the weariness of worldly existence, protect us; we bow to you. ॥2॥
uttar.13.cha3: Those who, drunk with pride of knowledge, did not honour devotion to you, which ends worldly existence, we see, O Hari, win a state hard even for the gods to reach, and fall from it. Those who trust you, give up every other hope, and remain your servants cross the ocean of worldly existence without toil by repeating your name; it is you, our Lord, whom we remember. ॥3॥
uttar.13.cha4: The feet that Śiva and Brahmā worship, whose holy dust, once it touched her, set free the sage's wife, from whose nails came the Gaṅgā, river of the gods, revered by sages, purifier of the three worlds, which bear the banner, the thunderbolt, the goad and the lotus, and grew calluses from thorns as they walked the forest: those two lotus feet, O Mukunda, O Rāma, O lord of Ramā, we ever worship. ॥4॥
uttar.13.cha5: The Vedas and scriptures tell of a beginningless tree whose root is the Unmanifest, with four barks, six trunks, twenty-five branches, countless leaves and thick flowers, two kinds of fruit, bitter and sweet, and a single creeper that lives clinging to it, ever putting out fresh shoots and flowers: to that tree of worldly existence we bow. ॥5॥
uttar.13.cha6: Some meditate on Brahman as unborn, non-dual, known by experience alone, beyond the mind: let them speak of it and know it so; we, my Lord, ever sing the glory of your form with attributes. Lord, home of compassion, mine of virtues, O God, this is the boon we ask: that, casting off the faults of mind, speech and action, we may love your feet. ॥6॥
uttar.13.do13क: While all looked on, the Vedas made this noble prayer; then they vanished and went to the abode of Brahmā. ॥13 (क)॥
uttar.13.do13ख: Listen, Garuḍa: then Śiva came to where Śrī Rāma was, and made his prayer with a voice choked with feeling, his whole body thrilling. ॥13 (ख)॥
uttar.14.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, beloved of Ramā, who brings peace; save your servant, troubled by fear of the fever of worldly existence. Lord of Avadh, lord of the gods, lord of Ramā, all-pervading one: I have come for refuge and I ask you, Lord, save me. ॥1॥
uttar.14.cau2: Destroyer of the ten-headed, twenty-armed one, you have taken away the earth's great and grievous ills. The hosts of demons were moths, burned up in the fierce blaze of the fire of your arrows. ॥2॥
uttar.14.cau3: Lovelier than all, the ornament of the earth's circle, you bear the noble arrows, bow and quiver. To the dense darkness of the great night of pride, delusion and possessiveness, you are the host of the sun's rays. ॥3॥
uttar.14.cau4: Kāma, the hunter, has struck down the deer that are people, piercing their hearts with the arrows of base pleasures. Slay him, my Lord, O Hari, and save these helpless ones, wretches who have strayed and fallen in the forest of the senses. ॥4॥
uttar.14.cau5: People are struck down by many diseases and partings; these are the fruits of disregarding your feet. Those men lie in the fathomless ocean of worldly existence who have no love for your lotus feet. ॥5॥
uttar.14.cau6: Ever most wretched, sullied and sorrowful are those who have no love for your lotus feet. Those whose support is your story ever hold dear the saints and the infinite Lord. ॥6॥
uttar.14.cau7: They have no attachment, no greed, no pride, no arrogance; wealth and misfortune are the same to them. This is why sages gladly become your servants, and give up for ever their trust in yoga. ॥7॥
uttar.14.cau8: With love they keep their vows unbroken and serve your lotus feet with a pure heart. Holding scorn and honour alike, all such saints wander the earth in happiness. ॥8॥
uttar.14.cau9: Bee at the lotus of the sages' hearts, O hero of the Raghus, greatly steadfast in battle, unconquered: I worship you. O Hari, I chant your name and bow to you, the great cure for the disease of worldly existence, the enemy of pride. ॥9॥
uttar.14.cau10: Supreme home of virtue, goodness and grace, lord of Śrī, I bow to you without ceasing. Joy of the Raghus, root out the mass of opposites; protector of the earth, look upon this humble one. ॥10॥
uttar.14.do14क: Again and again I ask this boon; grant it gladly, lord of Śrī: unfailing devotion to your lotus feet, and the company of the good for ever. ॥14 (क)॥
uttar.14.do14ख: Having told of Śrī Rāma's virtues, Śiva, Umā's lord, went joyfully to Kailāsa. Then the Lord had the monkeys given lodgings comfortable in every way. ॥14 (ख)॥
uttar.15.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: this story is purifying; it destroys the threefold affliction and the fear of worldly existence. On hearing of the great king's auspicious coronation, people gain dispassion and discernment. ॥1॥
uttar.15.cau2: Those who hear it or sing it with desires in their hearts win happiness and wealth of many kinds. After enjoying in the world joys rare even for the gods, at the hour of death they go to the city of Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.15.cau3: The liberated, the dispassionate and the worldly who hear it gain devotion, the supreme state and ever new wealth. Garuḍa, I have told the story of Śrī Rāma as far as my own understanding could range; it takes away fear and sorrow. ॥3॥
uttar.15.cau4: It makes dispassion, discernment and devotion firm, and is a fine boat for crossing the river of delusion. In the city of Kosala there was fresh rejoicing every day, and people of every community were happy. ॥4॥
uttar.15.cau5: Everyone's love for Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, to which Śiva, the sages and Brahmā bow, grew new each day. Those who came asking were clothed in garments of many kinds, and the Brahmins received gifts of every sort. ॥5॥
uttar.15.do15: All the monkeys were immersed in the bliss of Brahman, and every heart held love for the Lord's feet. They never noticed the days going by, and six months passed. ॥15॥
uttar.16.cau1: They forgot their homes and did not think of them even in dreams, just as ill will towards others never enters a saint's mind. Then Śrī Rāma called all his friends; they all came and bowed their heads with respect. ॥1॥
uttar.16.cau2: With the greatest love he seated them close to him and spoke gentle words that gladden devotees: You have served me greatly. In what words can I praise you to your face? ॥2॥
uttar.16.cau3: That is why you have become so dear to me: for my sake you gave up your homes and their comforts. My younger brothers, the kingdom, wealth, Sītā, my body, my home, family and loved ones: ॥3॥
uttar.16.cau4: all are dear to me, but none as dear as you. I do not speak falsely; this is my way. Everyone holds his servant dear, as is the rule; but my love for those who serve me is greater still. ॥4॥
uttar.16.do16: Now go home, all of you, my friends, and worship me with steadfast discipline. Knowing me as ever present in all and the well-wisher of all, keep loving me dearly. ॥16॥
uttar.17.cau1: Hearing the Lord's words they were all overwhelmed; forgetting who they were and where, they lost all sense of their bodies. They stood before him with joined palms, gazing without a blink, too full of love to say anything. ॥1॥
uttar.17.cau2: The Lord saw their supreme love and taught them special knowledge in many ways. Before the Lord they could say nothing, and gazed again and again at his lotus feet. ॥2॥
uttar.17.cau3: Then the Lord sent for ornaments and garments of many colours, matchless and lovely. Sugrīva was dressed first, Bharata having arranged the garments with his own hands. ॥3॥
uttar.17.cau4: At the Lord's bidding Lakṣmaṇa dressed Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, who is dear to Śrī Rāma's heart. Aṅgada stayed seated and did not stir; seeing his love, the Lord did not call him. ॥4॥
uttar.17.do17क: Śrī Rāma dressed Jāmbavān, Nīla and all the others. Holding Śrī Rāma's form in their hearts and bowing their heads at his feet, they all set off. ॥17 (क)॥
uttar.17.do17ख: Then Aṅgada rose and bowed his head, and with tears in his eyes and palms joined spoke most humbly, in words that seemed steeped in the nectar of love: ॥17 (ख)॥
uttar.18.cau1: Listen, all-knowing one, ocean of grace and joy, merciful to the lowly, friend of the distressed. My Lord, when Vāli was dying he left me in your very lap. ॥1॥
uttar.18.cau2: Keep to your proud name as the refuge of those without refuge, and do not forsake me, friend of your devotees. To me you are master, teacher, father and mother; where could I go, leaving your lotus feet? ॥2॥
uttar.18.cau3: Consider it yourself and tell me, O king of men: leaving my Lord, what business have I at home? I am a child, without knowledge, sense or strength; keep this humble servant in your refuge, my Lord. ॥3॥
uttar.18.cau4: I will do every lowly task of the household, and by gazing on your lotus feet I shall cross the ocean of worldly existence. With these words he fell at the Lord's feet and said: Protect me. Do not tell me now to go home, my Lord. ॥4॥
uttar.18.do18क: Śrī Rāma, the very bound of compassion, heard Aṅgada's humble words. The Lord raised him and clasped him to his heart, his lotus eyes filled with tears. ॥18 (क)॥
uttar.18.do18ख: The Lord put the garland from his own breast, robes and jewels on Vāli's son, and then, after counselling him in many ways, gave him leave to go. ॥18 (ख)॥
uttar.19.cau1: Mindful of what the devotees had done, Bharata went with his younger brother Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa to see them off. No small love filled Aṅgada's heart; again and again he turned to look towards Śrī Rāma, ॥1॥
uttar.19.cau2: and again and again he prostrated himself, hoping in his heart that Śrī Rāma would tell him to stay. Remembering over and over how Śrī Rāma looked, spoke, walked and met him with a smile, he grieved. ॥2॥
uttar.19.cau3: Seeing the Lord's wish, he made many humble entreaties and went on his way, holding the lotus feet in his heart. Bharata escorted all the monkeys with great honour, and then returned with his brothers. ॥3॥
uttar.19.cau4: Then Hanumān clasped Sugrīva's feet and pleaded with him in many ways: Let me serve at Śrī Rāma's feet for ten days, my lord, and then I shall come and see your feet again. ॥4॥
uttar.19.cau5: Sugrīva said: Son of the Wind, you are a store of merit; go and serve the Lord, the home of grace. With these words all the monkeys left at once. Aṅgada said: Listen, Hanumān: ॥5॥
uttar.19.do19क: Give the Lord my prostrations; I ask you this with joined palms. And keep reminding Śrī Rāma of me, again and again. ॥19 (क)॥
uttar.19.do19ख: With these words Vāli's son went on his way, and Hanumān came back. He told the Lord of Aṅgada's love, and the Lord was overcome with it. ॥19 (ख)॥
uttar.19.do19ग: Harder than the thunderbolt and gentler far than a flower: such is Śrī Rāma's heart, Garuḍa. Tell me, who can understand it? ॥19 (ग)॥
uttar.20.cau1: Then the compassionate Lord sent for the Niṣāda chief, bestowed ornaments and garments on him as a blessing, and said: Go home, keep me in remembrance, and follow dharma in thought, deed and word. ॥1॥
uttar.20.cau2: You are my friend, and a brother to me like Bharata; keep coming to the city always. On hearing this he was filled with great joy, and fell at the Lord's feet with tears in his eyes. ॥2॥
uttar.20.cau3: Holding the Lord's lotus feet in his heart he went home, and told his family of the Lord's nature. Seeing Śrī Rāma's ways, the citizens said again and again: Blessed is the Lord, the treasure of joy. ॥3॥
uttar.20.cau4: When Śrī Rāma took his seat on the throne, the three worlds rejoiced and all their sorrows left them. Nobody held a grudge against another; through Śrī Rāma's power all strife was gone. ॥4॥
uttar.20.do20: The people were each devoted to the dharma of their own class (varṇa) and stage of life (āśrama). They always walked the path of the Veda and lived in happiness, with no fear, no grief and no disease. ॥20॥
uttar.21.cau1: In Śrī Rāma's kingdom no one was touched by the afflictions that come from the body, from the gods or from other creatures. Everyone loved one another, and each walked devoted to his own dharma as the Veda directs. ॥1॥
uttar.21.cau2: Dharma stood on all its four feet throughout the world; there was no sin, not even in dreams. Every man and woman was given to devotion to Śrī Rāma, and all were fit for the supreme state. ॥2॥
uttar.21.cau3: There was no untimely death and no pain of any kind; all were handsome, and all were sound and free of disease in body. No one was poor, unhappy or wretched; no one was ignorant or without auspicious marks. ॥3॥
uttar.21.cau4: All were free of hypocrisy, given to dharma and virtuous; men and women alike were skilful and accomplished. All knew the worth of merit, all were learned and wise, all were grateful, and none was clever in deceit. ॥4॥
uttar.21.do21: Listen, Garuḍa: in Śrī Rāma's kingdom, throughout the world of moving and unmoving beings, no one suffered sorrow caused by time, karma, nature or the guṇas. ॥21॥
uttar.22.cau1: Śrī Rāma of Kosala was the one king of the earth, girdled by the seven seas. Yet for him in each of whose hairs lie many worlds, this lordship was no great thing. ॥1॥
uttar.22.cau2: Once that greatness of the Lord is understood, to describe this is to belittle him greatly. Yet, Garuḍa, the very ones who know that greatness find their joy in this story once more. ॥2॥
uttar.22.cau3: Great sages of subdued senses declare that this play is the very fruit of knowing that greatness. The happiness and wealth of Śrī Rāma's reign neither Śeṣa, king of serpents, nor Sarasvatī could describe. ॥3॥
uttar.22.cau4: All were generous, all did good to others; men and women all served at the feet of the Brahmins. Every man kept the vow of one wife, and wives sought their husbands' good in thought, word and deed. ॥4॥
uttar.22.do22: Daṇḍa, the rod, was found only in the hands of ascetics, and bheda, division, only in the dance of a troupe of dancers; and conquest was heard of only as conquest of the mind: such was the reign of Śrī Rāma. ॥22॥
uttar.23.cau1: The forest trees were ever in flower and in fruit, and the elephant and the lion shared one place. Bird and beast laid aside the enmity born in them, and love grew up among them all. ॥1॥
uttar.23.cau2: Birds sang, and herds of beasts of many kinds roamed the forest without fear, rejoicing. A cool, fragrant breeze blew gently, and bees went humming, carrying the nectar of flowers. ॥2॥
uttar.23.cau3: When asked, creepers and trees dripped honey, and the cows yielded whatever milk was wished for. The land stayed full of harvest at all times; the Tretā age took on the ways of the Kṛta age. ॥3॥
uttar.23.cau4: Mines of many kinds of gems appeared in the mountains, which knew the king for the soul of the world. Every river ran with the best of water, cool and clear, delightful to drink. ॥4॥
uttar.23.cau5: The seas stayed within their limits and left gems along the shore, which men picked up. Every pond was crowded with lotuses, and all the ten quarters were bright and glad. ॥5॥
uttar.23.do23: The moon steeped the earth in its rays, and the sun burned no more than the need called for; clouds gave rain when it was asked for, in the reign of Śrī Rāma. ॥23॥
uttar.24.cau1: The Lord performed millions of horse sacrifices and gave many gifts to the Brahmins. He guards the path of the Vedas and is foremost in upholding dharma; he is beyond the guṇas, and in enjoyment he is like Indra. ॥1॥
uttar.24.cau2: Sītā is always at one with her husband's wishes; she is a mine of beauty, gentle-natured and humble. She knows the greatness of the Lord, the ocean of mercy, and serves his lotus feet with her whole heart. ॥2॥
uttar.24.cau3: Though there are many servants, men and women, in the house, all of them ever skilled in the ways of service, yet Sītā does the work of the house with her own hands and follows Śrī Rāma's every command. ॥3॥
uttar.24.cau4: Whatever way pleases the Lord, the ocean of mercy, Śrī (Sītā), knowing the ways of service, does just that. She serves all her mothers-in-law in the house, Kausalyā and the rest, with no pride and no vanity in her. ॥4॥
uttar.24.cau5: Umā, she is Ramā, to whom Brahmā and the other gods bow; she is the Mother of the world, ever beyond reproach. ॥5॥
uttar.24.do24: She whose glance of grace the gods long for, and who does not so much as look at them, sets that nature of hers aside and loves the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma. ॥24॥
uttar.25.cau1: All the brothers serve him in keeping with his wishes, and their love for Śrī Rāma's feet is exceedingly great. They keep their eyes on the Lord's lotus face, waiting for the compassionate Lord to ask something of them some day. ॥1॥
uttar.25.cau2: Śrī Rāma loves his brothers and teaches them right counsel in many ways. The people of the city live in joy and enjoy every pleasure, such as even the gods can hardly find. ॥2॥
uttar.25.cau3: Day and night they keep praying to Brahmā, asking for love for the feet of Śrī Rāma. Two beautiful sons were born to Sītā, Lava and Kuśa, whose praises the Vedas and Purāṇas sing. ॥3॥
uttar.25.cau4: Both are victorious, modest and abodes of virtue, so beautiful that they seem reflections of Śrī Hari himself. Each of the brothers had two sons, rich in beauty, virtue and good character. ॥4॥
uttar.25.do25: He who is beyond knowledge, speech and the senses, the unborn, who is beyond māyā, the mind and the guṇas, he, who is being, consciousness and bliss in full, is acting out a noble human life. ॥25॥
uttar.26.cau1: At daybreak, after bathing in the Sarayū, he sits in the assembly with Brahmins and good men. Vasiṣṭha expounds the Vedas and Purāṇas, and Śrī Rāma listens, though he knows it all. ॥1॥
uttar.26.cau2: He eats together with his younger brothers, and seeing this every mother's heart brims with happiness. The two brothers Bharata and Śatrughna go to the grove with Hanumān, son of the Wind. ॥2॥
uttar.26.cau3: Sitting there, they ask for the story of Śrī Rāma's virtues, and Hanumān, wise of mind, dives deep into them and tells it. Hearing of those spotless virtues they are filled with joy, and entreat him to tell them again and again. ॥3॥
uttar.26.cau4: In every home Purāṇas are recited and Śrī Rāma's holy deeds are told in many ways. Men and women go on singing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and so doing they never notice the days and nights go by. ॥4॥
uttar.26.do26: All the store of happiness and wealth of the people of Ayodhyā a thousand Śeṣas could not describe, for there Śrī Rāma reigns as king. ॥26॥
uttar.27.cau1: Nārada, Sanaka and other great sages, to see the Lord of Kosala, come to Ayodhyā every day, and at the sight of the city they forget their dispassion. ॥1॥
uttar.27.cau2: The upper storeys are built of gold and gems, with lovely floors cast in many colours. Round the city runs a wall of great beauty, crowned with fine battlements of every colour. ॥2॥
uttar.27.cau3: It is as if the hosts of the nine planets had formed an army and come to lay siege to Amarāvatī. The ground is paved with glass of many colours, and seeing it even the minds of great sages dance. ॥3॥
uttar.27.cau4: The white mansions kiss the sky above, and their pinnacles seem to scorn the brilliance of the sun and moon. Windows wrought of many gems sparkle, and in every house lamps of gems glow. ॥4॥
uttar.27.cha1: Lamps of gems shine, the mansions gleam, and the thresholds are made of coral. There are pillars of gems, and walls fashioned by Brahmā himself, inlaid with gold, gems and emeralds. The mansions are beautiful, charming and spacious, and their courtyards are built of lovely crystal. At every single gateway the doors are of gold, finely wrought and set with many diamonds. ॥1॥
uttar.27.do27: In every house there are lovely picture halls, where the deeds of Śrī Rāma are painted with great art; any sage who gazes at them has his heart stolen away. ॥27॥
uttar.28.cau1: Everyone has planted flower gardens and laid them out with care in many styles. In them graceful creepers of many kinds, lovely to see, are always in bloom, as if it were spring. ॥1॥
uttar.28.cau2: Bees hum with a sweet and charming sound, and a pleasant breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is always blowing. Children have reared birds of many kinds, which speak sweetly and look lovely as they fly. ॥2॥
uttar.28.cau3: Peacocks, swans, cranes and pigeons look splendid upon the mansions. Seeing their own reflections here and there, they call in many ways and dance. ॥3॥
uttar.28.cau4: Children teach the parrots and mynas: Say Rāma, Raghupati, protector of his people. The royal gateway is beautiful in every way, and so are the streets, the crossroads and the markets. ॥4॥
uttar.28.cha1: The lovely markets are beyond describing; there goods are had without payment. Where he in whom Ramā dwells is himself king, how could the wealth of the place be sung? Cloth dealers, bankers and many merchants sit there, as though each were Kubera. Women, men, children and the old, whoever they are, are all happy, all upright and fair to see. ॥1॥
uttar.28.do28: On the northern side flows the Sarayū, its water clear and deep. Charming ghats are built along it, and there is not the least mud on its banks. ॥28॥
uttar.29.cau1: Far off, in an open place, is a fine ghat where troops of horses and elephants drink. There are many ghats for drawing water, most charming, and there men do not bathe. ॥1॥
uttar.29.cau2: The royal ghat is fine and beautiful in every way; there men of all four varṇas bathe. All along the bank stand temples of the gods, with lovely groves on every side of them. ॥2॥
uttar.29.cau3: At spots along the riverside dwell sages and renunciants who have turned from the world and delight in knowledge. Lovely tulasī lines the banks, set out clump by clump by many sages. ॥3॥
uttar.29.cau4: The beauty of the city cannot be told at all, and outside the city too all is supremely lovely. At the sight of the city every sin takes flight; there are woods, groves, stepwells and lakes. ॥4॥
uttar.29.cha1: Peerless stepwells, lakes and wells, charming and wide, add to its beauty. Seeing their fine steps and clear water, gods and sages are entranced. Lotuses of many colours grow there, many birds call and bees hum. The delightful gardens, with the songs of cuckoos and other birds, seem to call out to the passers-by. ॥1॥
uttar.29.do29: Can the city whose king is the Lord of Ramā be described? Aṇimā and the other powers, and all joys and riches, fill the whole of Ayodhyā. ॥29॥
uttar.30.cau1: Everywhere people sing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as they sit together they urge this upon one another: Worship Śrī Rāma, who cherishes those who bow to him, the home of beauty, good character, grace of form and every virtue. ॥1॥
uttar.30.cau2: Worship him whose eyes are lotuses and whose body is dark, who guards his servants as the eyelids guard the eyes. Worship him who bears lovely arrows, bow and quiver, the sun to the lotus grove of the saints, steadfast in battle. ॥2॥
uttar.30.cau3: Worship him who is Garuḍa to the terrible serpent of Time, who wipes out the sense of mine in all who bow to him free of desire. Worship him who is the hunter of the herd of deer, greed and delusion, a lion to the elephant of desire, and the giver of joy to his devotees. ॥3॥
uttar.30.cau4: He is the sun to the thick darkness of doubt and grief, and the fire that burns the dense forest of the demons. Why do you not worship Śrī Rāma, together with Janaka's daughter, who shatters the fear of worldly existence? ॥4॥
uttar.30.cau5: He is a mass of frost to the mosquitoes of countless desires; he is ever the same, unborn and imperishable. Worship the delight of the sages, who takes away the burden of the earth, the generous Lord of Tulasīdāsa. ॥5॥
uttar.30.do30: In this way the women and men of the city sing the praises of Śrī Rāma, and the Lord, treasury of compassion, is ever gracious to them all. ॥30॥
uttar.31.cau1: Garuḍa, ever since the mighty sun of Śrī Rāma's glory rose, its light has filled the three worlds; to many it has brought joy, and to many grief of heart. ॥1॥
uttar.31.cau2: I shall tell you in full of those who grieve. First, the night of ignorance came to an end. The owls of sin hid wherever they could, and the white lilies of desire and anger shrank shut. ॥2॥
uttar.31.cau3: Actions of many kinds, the guṇas, time and one's nature: these cakora birds never find any joy. Envy, vanity, delusion and pride are thieves whose craft succeeds in no direction. ॥3॥
uttar.31.cau4: In the lake of dharma the lotuses of knowledge and realised knowledge opened in many ways. Happiness, contentment, dispassion and discernment, these many cakravāka birds, were freed from grief. ॥4॥
uttar.31.do31: When this sun of glory shines in anyone's heart, those named last grow strong, and those named first are destroyed. ॥31॥
uttar.32.cau1: Once Śrī Rāma, with his brothers and with Hanumān, son of the Wind, most dear to him, went to see a beautiful grove; every tree was in flower and covered in fresh leaves. ॥1॥
uttar.32.cau2: Knowing it to be the right time, Sanaka and his brothers came, masses of radiance, graced with virtue and good character. They are ever absorbed in the bliss of Brahman; to look at they are children, yet they are of great age. ॥2॥
uttar.32.cau3: They seem the four Vedas in bodily form; these sages see all alike and are free of all sense of difference. The quarters of the sky are their only clothing, and their one passion is to listen wherever the deeds of Śrī Rāma are being told. ॥3॥
uttar.32.cau4: Bhavānī, Sanaka and his brothers had been staying where the wise and great sage Agastya, the pot-born, lives. The great sage had told the story of Śrī Rāma at length; from it knowledge is born, as fire is born from the fire-sticks. ॥4॥
uttar.32.do32: Seeing the sages coming, Śrī Rāma joyfully prostrated himself before them. Welcoming them and asking after their well-being, the Lord gave them his own yellow robe to sit on. ॥32॥
uttar.33.cau1: The three brothers too, with Hanumān, son of the Wind, prostrated themselves, and their joy was great. The sages gazed on Śrī Rāma's matchless beauty and were lost in it; they could not hold their minds back. ॥1॥
uttar.33.cau2: Dark of body, with lotus eyes, he is the home of beauty and the one who frees from worldly existence. They stared without a blink, not closing their eyes, while the Lord, palms joined, bowed his head. ॥2॥
uttar.33.cau3: Seeing their state, Śrī Rāma shed tears and the hair of his body stood on end. The Lord took the great sages by the hand, sat them down and spoke words of the utmost charm: ॥3॥
uttar.33.cau4: Today I am blessed; listen, lords of sages: the sight of you wipes out sin. The company of the good comes by great good fortune, and through it the round of birth is broken with no effort at all. ॥4॥
uttar.33.do33: The company of saints is the road to liberation, and the company of the sensual the road to worldly existence: so say the saints, the poets, the learned, the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the good books. ॥33॥
uttar.34.cau1: Hearing the Lord's words, the four sages rejoiced and, thrilling all over, began a hymn of praise: Glory to you, Lord, endless, free from every ill, sinless, many and one, full of compassion. ॥1॥
uttar.34.cau2: Glory to you who are beyond attributes, glory, glory to you, ocean of virtues, home of joy, beautiful and supremely refined. Glory to you, consort of Lakṣmī; glory to you, upholder of the earth; peerless, unborn, without beginning, a mine of splendour. ॥2॥
uttar.34.cau3: You are a treasury of knowledge, free of pride yourself and giving honour to others; your holy fame is told by the Purāṇas and the Vedas. You know the truth, you remember every kindness, you destroy ignorance; you have many names and yet no name, and are without stain. ॥3॥
uttar.34.cau4: You are all things, you pervade all and dwell for ever in every heart: protect us. Shatter the pairs of opposites, our troubles and the snare of worldly existence; dwell in our hearts, Śrī Rāma, and crush desire and pride. ॥4॥
uttar.34.do34: Highest bliss, dwelling-place of compassion, you bring every wish of the heart to fulfilment. Śrī Rāma, give us loving devotion that never fails. ॥34॥
uttar.35.cau1: Give us devotion, O Lord of the Raghus, the devotion that purifies above all and puts an end to the threefold affliction and the arrogance of worldly existence. To those who bow before you, you are the wish-granting cow and the wish-fulfilling tree: be pleased, my Lord, and give us this boon. ॥1॥
uttar.35.cau2: O Lord of the Raghus, you are Agastya to the ocean of worldly existence; you are easily won by service and give every joy. Rend the cruel sorrows born of the mind, friend of the lowly, and let evenness of mind spread wide. ॥2॥
uttar.35.cau3: You drive away hope, fear, envy and the rest, and you increase humility, discernment and dispassion. Crest-jewel of kings, ornament of the earth, give us devotion, the boat that crosses the river of birth and death. ॥3॥
uttar.35.cau4: You are the swan who dwells for ever in the Mānasa lake of the sages' minds; Brahmā and Śiva worship your lotus feet. You are the banner of Raghu's line, the guardian of the bounds the Vedas set, and the devourer of time, karma, nature and the guṇas. ॥4॥
uttar.35.cau5: You carry souls across and are yourself the boat, and you take away every fault; ornament of the three worlds, you are the Lord of Tulasīdāsa. ॥5॥
uttar.35.do35: Praising him again and again and bowing their heads in love, Sanaka and his brothers went to the abode of Brahmā, having received the boon they wanted most. ॥35॥
uttar.36.cau1: Once Sanaka and the others had departed for the world of Brahmā, the brothers bowed their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet. All of them were shy of asking the Lord, and all of them looked towards Hanumān. ॥1॥
uttar.36.cau2: They longed to hear words from the Lord's own lips, the hearing of which removes every error. The Lord, who knows all hearts, understood everything and asked: Tell me, Hanumān, what is it? ॥2॥
uttar.36.cau3: Then Hanumān, with joined palms, said: Listen, Lord, compassionate to the lowly. My Lord, Bharata wants to ask you something, but his mind hesitates to put the question. ॥3॥
uttar.36.cau4: Śrī Rāma said: You know my nature, Hanumān. Has Bharata ever been in any way apart from me? Hearing this from the Lord, Bharata clasped his feet and said: Listen, my Lord, remover of the distress of those who bow to you. ॥4॥
uttar.36.do36: My Lord, I have no doubt at all, nor grief nor delusion even in a dream. It is all your grace alone, you who are grace and bliss in fullness. ॥36॥
uttar.37.cau1: Treasury of mercy, I am going to make bold: I am your servant, and you give joy to your own. O Lord of the Raghus, the Vedas and the Purāṇas have sung the glory of saints in many ways. ॥1॥
uttar.37.cau2: You too have praised them with your own lips, and the Lord's love for them is great. My Lord, ocean of mercy, wise in virtues and knowledge, I wish to hear what marks them out. ॥2॥
uttar.37.cau3: Protector of those who bow to you, explain to me the difference between the saint and the wicked, setting each apart. Śrī Rāma said: Listen, brother: the marks of saints are countless and well known in the Vedas and the Purāṇas. ॥3॥
uttar.37.cau4: Saints and the wicked behave towards each other as sandalwood and the axe do. Listen, brother: the axe cuts down the sandal tree of Malaya, and the tree gives it its own virtue, filling it with fragrance. ॥4॥
uttar.37.do37: That is why sandalwood is placed on the heads of the gods and is loved by all the world, while the axe's blade gets this penalty: it is burnt in the fire and pounded with the sledge. ॥37॥
