uttar.106.cau4: Proud, crooked, ill-starred and low-born, I bore ill will to my guru day and night. He was most compassionate, without the least anger, and again and again he gave me good counsel. ॥4॥
uttar.106.cau5: A base man strikes down and ruins first of all the very one through whom he gained his greatness. Listen, brother: smoke, born of fire, rises to the rank of a cloud and puts that fire out. ॥5॥
uttar.106.cau6: Dust lies scorned on the road and bears the kicks of everyone, every day. But when the wind lifts it, it first fills the wind itself, and then settles in the eyes of kings and on their crowns. ॥6॥
uttar.106.cau7: Listen, Garuḍa: understanding this, the wise keep no company with the base. Poets and the learned sing this rule of conduct: with the wicked, neither quarrel nor friendship is good. ॥7॥
uttar.106.cau8: My master, one should always stay aloof, and shun the wicked as one would a dog. I was wicked, with deceit and crookedness in my heart; my guru spoke for my good, but it did not please me. ॥8॥
uttar.106.do106क: Once I was in Śiva's temple, repeating the name of Śiva. My guru came in, and in my pride I did not rise and bow to him. ॥106 (क)॥
uttar.106.do106ख: Compassionate as he was, he said nothing, and there was not a trace of anger in his heart. But Maheśa could not bear the grave sin of slighting the guru. ॥106 (ख)॥
uttar.107.cau1: A voice from the sky sounded in the temple: Wretch, ignorant and proud! Though your guru feels no anger, being most merciful and of perfect understanding, ॥1॥
uttar.107.cau2: still, fool, I shall curse you, for I cannot abide a breach of right conduct. Wicked one, if I do not punish you, my path of the Veda will be broken. ॥2॥
uttar.107.cau3: Fools who envy their guru lie in the Raurava hell for ten million ages. Then they take bodies among the lower creatures and suffer pain for ten thousand births. ॥3॥
uttar.107.cau4: Sinner, you sat on like a python; wicked one, your mind steeped in filth, become a snake. Go into the hollow of some great tree and stay there, lowest of the low, sunk to this base state. ॥4॥
uttar.107.do107क: Hearing Śiva's dreadful curse, my guru cried out in dismay. Seeing me tremble violently, he felt anguish rise in his heart. ॥107 (क)॥
uttar.107.do107ख: The Brahmin prostrated himself with love and, facing Śiva, joined his palms. Then, thinking of the terrible fate that awaited me, he began to pray in a voice choked with feeling. ॥107 (ख)॥
uttar.108.cau1: O Īśāna, I bow to the Lord whose form is liberation, the mighty, the all-pervading, Brahman, the Veda itself. Abiding in his own being, beyond attributes and all distinctions, free of desire, the sky of consciousness, dwelling in the sky: you I worship. ॥1॥
uttar.108.cau2: Formless, the root of Oṃ, the fourth state beyond the three, beyond speech, knowledge and the senses, the Lord, lord of the mountain, terrible, the death even of Mahākāla, compassionate, the home of virtues, beyond the world: to him I bow. ॥2॥
uttar.108.cau3: Fair as the snowy mountain and deep, his body bright with the radiance and beauty of ten million Kāmas; on his head the lovely Gaṅgā shimmers in waves, the young moon gleams on his brow, and serpents lie at his throat; ॥3॥
uttar.108.cau4: his earrings swaying, his brows fair and his eyes large and lovely, his face serene, his throat blue, full of compassion; clad in the skin of the lion, garlanded with skulls: Śaṅkara, the beloved, the Lord of all, I worship. ॥4॥
uttar.108.cau5: The fierce, the supreme, the bold, the highest Lord, the undivided, the unborn, shining like ten million suns, who uproots the three kinds of pain, trident in hand, reached through loving feeling: the lord of Bhavānī I worship. ॥5॥
uttar.108.cau6: You who are beyond all parts, the auspicious, who bring the aeon to its end, ever the giver of joy to the good, enemy of Tripura, mass of consciousness and bliss, dispeller of delusion, enemy of Kāma: my Lord, be gracious, be gracious. ॥6॥
uttar.108.cau7: Lord of Umā, as long as men, in this world or the next, do not worship your lotus feet, they find no happiness, no peace, no end to their torment. Be gracious, my Lord, who dwell in all beings. ॥7॥
uttar.108.cau8: I know neither yoga nor japa nor worship; Śambhu, at every moment and always, I bow to you. My Lord, I am scorched by the flood of the sorrows of age and birth and have fallen into distress: protect me, O Īśa, O Śambhu. ॥8॥
uttar.108.shloka9: This Rudrāṣṭaka was spoken by the Brahmin to please Hara. Śiva is gracious to those who recite it with devotion. ॥9॥
uttar.108.do108क: Śiva, who knows all, heard the prayer and saw the Brahmin's love. Then again a voice from the sky sounded in the temple: Best of Brahmins, ask for a boon. ॥108 (क)॥
uttar.108.do108ख: The Brahmin said: Lord, if you are pleased with me, and, master, if you love the lowly, then, Lord, grant me first devotion to your own feet, and after that a second boon. ॥108 (ख)॥
uttar.108.do108ग: The soul is dull; in the power of your māyā it wanders, always astray. Lord, ocean of mercy, Bhagavān, do not be angry with it. ॥108 (ग)॥
uttar.108.do108घ: Śiva, kind to the lowly, be merciful to him now, so that, my Lord, before long the curse may give way to grace. ॥108 (घ)॥
uttar.109.cau1: Treasury of mercy, now do that which will bring him the highest good. Hearing the Brahmin's words, steeped in the good of another, the voice from the sky said: So be it. ॥1॥
uttar.109.cau2: Though he has committed a dreadful sin, and I in my anger have cursed him, yet, seeing your goodness, I shall show him special grace. ॥2॥
uttar.109.cau3: Brahmins who are forgiving and do good to others are as dear to me as Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara. Brahmin, my curse will not go for nothing; he will surely pass through a thousand births. ॥3॥
uttar.109.cau4: But the unbearable pain that comes with being born and dying will not touch him in the least. In no birth will his knowledge fade. Śūdra, listen: my word holds true. ॥4॥
uttar.109.cau5: You were born in Śrī Rāma's city, and then you set your mind on serving me. Through the power of that city and through my grace, devotion to Śrī Rāma will arise in your heart. ॥5॥
uttar.109.cau6: Now hear my true words, brother: serving the Brahmins is the vow that pleases Śrī Hari. Never again insult a Brahmin; know the saints to be equal to the infinite Lord. ॥6॥
uttar.109.cau7: Indra's thunderbolt, my great trident, the rod of Death and the dreadful discus of Śrī Hari: one whom these cannot kill is burnt up in the fire of hostility to Brahmins. ॥7॥
uttar.109.cau8: Keep this discernment in your mind, and nothing in the world will be beyond your reach. And I give you one more blessing: your going will be unhindered everywhere. ॥8॥
uttar.109.do109क: Hearing Śiva's words, my guru rejoiced and said: So be it. Then he counselled me and went home, keeping Śiva's feet in his heart. ॥109 (क)॥
uttar.109.do109ख: Driven by time, I went to the Vindhya mountains and became a serpent. Then, when some time had passed, I left that body without any struggle. ॥109 (ख)॥
uttar.109.do109ग: Garuḍa, mount of Hari, whatever body I took I would lay down again with ease, as a man puts on new clothes and casts off the old. ॥109 (ग)॥
uttar.109.do109घ: Śiva kept the rule of the Veda, and I did not suffer. In this way, Garuḍa, I took many bodies, yet my knowledge never left me. ॥109 (घ)॥
uttar.110.cau1: Whatever body I took, beast or bird, god or man, in each I kept up the worship of Śrī Rāma. One pain I can never forget: the gentle, gracious nature of my guru. ॥1॥
uttar.110.cau2: My last body was that of a Brahmin, which the Purāṇas and the Vedas declare hard even for the gods to win. There too I played among the boys, acting out all the deeds of Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.110.cau3: When I grew up, my father taught me; I understood, listened and pondered, but none of it appealed to me. Every desire had fled my mind; I was absorbed in Śrī Rāma's feet alone. ॥3॥
uttar.110.cau4: Tell me, Garuḍa, who would be so unlucky as to leave the cow of plenty of the gods and tend a she-ass? Lost in love, I cared for nothing else; my father wore himself out teaching me. ॥4॥
uttar.110.cau5: When my father and mother were taken by death, I went to the forest to worship the protector of his people. Wherever in the woods I came upon great sages, I would go to their hermitages, one after another, and bow my head. ॥5॥
uttar.110.cau6: I would ask them the tales of Śrī Rāma's virtues; they would tell them, Garuḍa, and I would listen in delight. So I roamed, hearing the virtues of Śrī Hari recounted, and by Śiva's grace nothing stopped my way. ॥6॥
uttar.110.cau7: The three deep-rooted cravings fell away from me, and one longing grew strong in my heart: only when I see the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma shall I count my birth fulfilled. ॥7॥
uttar.110.cau8: Every sage I asked would tell me that God is made up of all beings. The doctrine of the attributeless did not please me; love for Brahman with attributes grew ever stronger in my heart. ॥8॥
uttar.110.do110क: Remembering my guru's words, my mind was fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet. I roamed singing the glory of Śrī Rāma, my love new at every moment. ॥110 (क)॥
uttar.110.do110ख: The sage Lomaśa was seated under a banyan, in its shade, on the summit of Meru. When I saw him I bowed my head at his feet and spoke very humbly. ॥110 (ख)॥
uttar.110.do110ग: King of birds, the kind sage heard my humble, gentle words, and asked me courteously: Brahmin, what brings you here? ॥110 (ग)॥
uttar.110.do110घ: Then I said: Treasury of mercy, you know all things and are wise. Revered one, teach me the worship of Brahman with attributes. ॥110 (घ)॥
uttar.111.cau1: Then, Garuḍa, the great sage told me with reverence something of the story of Śrī Rāma's virtues. And that sage of realised knowledge, absorbed in the knowledge of Brahman, judging me a most fit recipient, ॥1॥
uttar.111.cau2: began to teach me about Brahman: it is unborn, one without a second, without attributes, the lord of the heart; without parts, without desire, without name and without form; it is known only by experience, it is undivided, and nothing compares with it. ॥2॥
uttar.111.cau3: It is beyond the reach of mind and senses, stainless, imperishable, changeless, boundless, a mass of joy. You are That, the Vedas sing; between it and you there is no difference, as there is none between water and its wave. ॥3॥
uttar.111.cau4: The sage explained it to me in many ways, but the doctrine of the attributeless would not enter my heart. Once more I spoke, my head bowed at his feet: Great sage, teach me the worship of the Lord with attributes. ॥4॥
uttar.111.cau5: My mind is a fish in the water of devotion to Śrī Rāma; how could it live apart from it, wise and great sage? Be kind and give me that teaching by which, with my own eyes, I may see Śrī Rāma. ॥5॥
uttar.111.cau6: When I have seen the Lord of Avadh to my eyes' content, then I will hear the teaching on the attributeless. The sage, after telling once more the peerless story of Śrī Hari, refuted the view of the Lord with attributes and set forth the attributeless. ॥6॥
uttar.111.cau7: Then I would push aside the view of the attributeless and argue, stubborn beyond measure, for the Lord with attributes. I answered him and answered back, and signs of anger showed in the sage's body. ॥7॥
uttar.111.cau8: Listen, my lord: when much disrespect is shown, anger springs up even in the hearts of the wise. If someone rubs sandalwood too hard, even from it fire breaks out. ॥8॥
uttar.111.do111क: Again and again the sage, in anger, expounded knowledge, while I sat there and turned over many thoughts in my own mind: ॥111 (क)॥
uttar.111.do111ख: Can anger arise where there is no sense of duality? Can duality exist without ignorance? Can the soul, in the grip of māyā, limited and inert, be the equal of God? ॥111 (ख)॥
uttar.112.cau1: Does sorrow ever come to one who looks to the good of all? Can poverty touch one who owns the touchstone? Can those who wrong others live free of fear? And do the lustful stay without a stain? ॥1॥
uttar.112.cau2: Does anyone's line survive harm done to a Brahmin? Once one has known one's own true nature, is there still karma? Has good sense ever sprung up in anyone in the company of the wicked? Does one who goes to another's wife reach a good end? ॥2॥
uttar.112.cau3: Do those who know the Supreme Self fall into worldly existence? Are those who revile Śrī Hari ever happy? Does a kingdom last without knowledge of right policy? Do sins remain when the deeds of Śrī Hari are told? ॥3॥
uttar.112.cau4: Is holy fame won without merit? Does anyone earn ill fame without sin? Is there any gain equal to devotion to Śrī Hari, which the Vedas, the saints and the Purāṇas sing? ॥4॥
uttar.112.cau5: Brother, to gain a human body and not worship Śrī Rāma: what loss in the world could equal this? Is there any other sin like backbiting, Garuḍa, or any dharma like compassion? ॥5॥
uttar.112.cau6: In this way I kept weighing countless arguments in my mind, and did not hear the sage's teaching with respect. When again and again I planted myself on the side of the Lord with attributes, the sage spoke in anger: ॥6॥
uttar.112.cau7: Fool, I give you the highest teaching and you will not accept it; you keep bringing answer upon answer. You put no faith in words of truth; like a crow you are afraid of everything. ॥7॥
uttar.112.cau8: Wretch, your heart clings hard to your own side: become at once the lowest of birds. I took the curse upon my head; I felt no fear, and no dejection came over me. ॥8॥
uttar.112.do112क: At once I became a crow; then, bowing my head again at the sage's feet and remembering Śrī Rāma, the jewel of the Raghu line, I flew away in gladness. ॥112 (क)॥
uttar.112.do112ख: Umā, those whose love is fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet, who have left desire, pride and anger behind, see the whole world as full of their own Lord: with whom, then, should they quarrel? ॥112 (ख)॥
uttar.113.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, Garuḍa: no blame at all lies with the sage; the one who stirs the heart is Śrī Rāma, the ornament of the Raghu line. To try my love, the ocean of mercy made the sage's mind simple and unwary. ॥1॥
uttar.113.cau2: The Lord saw that in thought, word and deed I was his own; then he turned the sage's mind back again. The sage saw my great gentleness of nature and my special faith in Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥2॥
uttar.113.cau3: Deeply astonished, he repented again and again, and the sage called me back with respect. He comforted me in many ways, and then, glad at heart, gave me the mantra of Rāma. ॥3॥
uttar.113.cau4: The sage, a treasury of compassion, taught me the meditation on Śrī Rāma in the form of a child. That lovely, joy-giving meditation delighted me greatly; I have already told it to you. ॥4॥
uttar.113.cau5: The sage kept me there with him for some time, and then he told the Rāmacaritamānasa. When he had told me this story with reverence, the sage spoke again in gracious words: ॥5॥
uttar.113.cau6: Dear one, I received this lovely and hidden lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds by the grace of Śiva. It is because I know you to be Śrī Rāma's own devotee that I have told you all of it in full. ॥6॥
uttar.113.cau7: Dear one, never tell it to those who have no devotion to Śrī Rāma in their hearts. In many ways the sage instructed me, and I bowed my head at his feet with love. ॥7॥
uttar.113.cau8: Touching my head with his lotus hand, the great sage blessed me with joy: Unbroken devotion to Śrī Rāma will dwell in your heart for ever; this, from now on, is my grace upon you. ॥8॥
uttar.113.do113क: May you always be dear to Śrī Rāma, a home of good qualities, free of pride; able to take any form at will, dying only when you choose, a treasury of knowledge and dispassion. ॥113 (क)॥
uttar.113.do113ख: Moreover, in whatever hermitage you dwell, remembering the Blessed Lord, there ignorance will not spread for a yojana around. ॥113 (ख)॥
uttar.114.cau1: No sorrow born of time, karma, the guṇas, faults or one's own nature will ever touch you. The many lovely secrets of Śrī Rāma, hidden and open, in the epics and the Purāṇas, ॥1॥
uttar.114.cau2: all of them too you will know without effort; may your love for Śrī Rāma's feet be new every day. Whatever you wish for in your mind, by the grace of Śrī Hari nothing will be beyond your reach. ॥2॥
uttar.114.cau3: Listen, Garuḍa, steady of mind: when the sage's blessing had been heard, a deep voice of Brahman sounded from the sky: So be it, wise sage, as you have spoken; he is my devotee in deed, mind and speech. ॥3॥
uttar.114.cau4: Hearing the voice from the sky, I was filled with joy; I was lost in love, and all my doubt was gone. I made my entreaty to the sage and, receiving his leave, bowed my head again and again at his lotus feet; ॥4॥
uttar.114.cau5: then I came joyfully to this hermitage, having gained by the Lord's grace a boon that is hard to win. Listen, Garuḍa: since I came to live here, twenty-seven kalpas have gone by. ॥5॥
uttar.114.cau6: I am always singing the virtues of Śrī Rāma, and wise birds listen with reverence. Each time Śrī Rāma, for his devotees' sake, takes a human body in Ayodhyā, ॥6॥
uttar.114.cau7: each time I go and live in Śrī Rāma's city, and find my joy in watching his play as a child. Then, Garuḍa, keeping Śrī Rāma's child form in my heart, I come back to my own hermitage. ॥7॥
uttar.114.cau8: I have told you the whole story of how I came to have a crow's body. Dear one, I have answered all your questions; immense is the glory of devotion to Śrī Rāma. ॥8॥
uttar.114.do114क: This body is dear to me for this reason: in it love for Śrī Rāma's feet was born in me. In it I had the sight of my own Lord, and all my doubts were gone. ॥114 (क)॥
uttar.114.do114ख: I held stubbornly to the side of devotion, and the great sage laid a curse on me; yet I gained a boon that even sages rarely win: see the power of worship. ॥114 (ख)॥
uttar.115.cau1: Those who know such devotion and yet forsake it, and labour for knowledge alone, are dullards: they abandon the wish-fulfilling cow at home and wander, searching the milkweed for milk. ॥1॥
uttar.115.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: those who turn from devotion to Śrī Hari and seek happiness by some other means are fools of foolish deeds who would swim across the vast ocean without a boat. ॥2॥
uttar.115.cau3: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's words, Bhavānī, Garuḍa spoke joyfully and gently: By your grace, my lord, there is now no doubt in my heart, no grief, no delusion, no error. ॥3॥
uttar.115.cau4: I have heard the many holy virtues of Śrī Rāma, and by your grace I have found rest. One thing I ask you, my lord; explain it to me clearly, treasury of mercy. ॥4॥
uttar.115.cau5: The saints, the sages, the Vedas and the Purāṇas say that nothing is as hard to gain as knowledge. That very knowledge, master, the sage taught you, yet you did not honour it as you honour devotion. ॥5॥
uttar.115.cau6: How great is the difference between knowledge and devotion? Tell me all of it, my lord, home of grace. The wise crow was pleased to hear Garuḍa's words, and replied with respect: ॥6॥
uttar.115.cau7: Between devotion and knowledge there is no difference at all; both take away the suffering born of worldly existence. My lord, the great sages do name some difference; hear it carefully, best of birds. ॥7॥
uttar.115.cau8: Knowledge, dispassion, yoga and realised knowledge, listen, Garuḍa: all these are male. The power of the male is strong in every way; the female is by nature weak and of an inert kind. ॥8॥
uttar.115.do115क: Only the man who is free of attachment and steady of mind can give up woman; not the man of desire, ruled by the senses, who has turned away from Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥115 (क)॥
uttar.115.so115ख: Even such a sage, a treasury of knowledge, gazing on the moonlike face of a doe-eyed woman, falls under her sway, Garuḍa: woman is the māyā of Viṣṇu made manifest. ॥115 (ख)॥
uttar.116.cau1: Here I take no side; I state the view of the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the saints. Delusion does not come to a woman from a woman's beauty; this, Garuḍa, is a matchless rule. ॥1॥
uttar.116.cau2: Listen: māyā and devotion are both of the feminine kind, as everyone knows. Then too, devotion is dear to Śrī Rāma, and māyā, poor thing, is no more than a dancer. ॥2॥
uttar.116.cau3: Śrī Rāma favours devotion; that is why māyā fears her so. The one in whose heart devotion to Śrī Rāma dwells always and unhindered, peerless and free of all adjuncts: ॥3॥
uttar.116.cau4: seeing him, māyā shrinks back and can exert none of her power over him. Considering this, sages of realised knowledge ask for devotion, the mine of every joy. ॥4॥
uttar.116.do116क: This secret of Śrī Rāma no one comes to know quickly. Whoever knows it by Śrī Rāma's grace is never deluded, not even in a dream. ॥116 (क)॥
uttar.116.do116ख: Hear, most skilful Garuḍa, a further difference between knowledge and devotion, hearing which one comes to have unbroken love for Śrī Rāma's feet for ever. ॥116 (ख)॥
uttar.117.cau1: Listen, dear one, to this story beyond telling: it can be understood, but not described. The soul is a part of the Lord, imperishable, conscious, stainless, by its nature a mass of joy. ॥1॥
uttar.117.cau2: That soul, my lord, fell under the sway of māyā and was caught like a parrot or a monkey. A knot was tied between the inert and the conscious; though it is false, it is hard to undo. ॥2॥
uttar.117.cau3: From then on the soul has been bound to worldly existence; the knot does not loosen, nor does the soul find happiness. The Vedas and Purāṇas have told many remedies, but it does not come loose; it only tangles more and more. ॥3॥
uttar.117.cau4: In the soul's heart the darkness of delusion is thick; the knot cannot even be seen, so how can it come loose? Even when the Lord brings about such a circumstance, it may only now and then be undone. ॥4॥
uttar.117.cau5: Suppose that by Śrī Hari's grace the lovely cow of sāttvika faith comes to dwell in the heart; the countless prayers, austerities, vows, restraints and observances, and the good dharma and conduct that the Vedas speak of, ॥5॥
uttar.117.cau6: are the green grass; when that cow grazes on it and, finding her young calf of devout feeling, lets down her milk; with withdrawal from the world as the milking tether, faith as the pail, and the pure mind, one's own servant, as the cowherd; ॥6॥
uttar.117.cau7: having milked, brother, the milk that is supreme dharma, let him boil it well on the fire of desirelessness; then cool it in the breeze of contentment and forbearance, and set it into curd with the starter of fortitude and calm. ॥7॥
uttar.117.cau8: With gladness let him churn it with the churning-stick of reflection, on the post of self-control, with the rope of truth and kind speech; then by churning draw out the butter of dispassion, stainless, lovely and wholly pure. ॥8॥
uttar.117.do117क: Then let him kindle the fire of yoga and feed it with deeds good and bad; when the dross of attachment has burnt away, let the intellect cool the ghee of knowledge. ॥117 (क)॥
uttar.117.do117ख: Then the intellect, which is realised knowledge itself, having gained that clear ghee, should fill the lamp of the mind and set it firm on a stand made of evenness. ॥117 (ख)॥
uttar.117.do117ग: From the cotton of the three states and the three guṇas let the intellect draw out the fibre of turīya, the fourth state, then card it and twist it into a firm, tight wick. ॥117 (ग)॥
uttar.117.so117घ: In this way let the lamp of realised knowledge be lit, a mass of radiance, on coming near which pride and all the other moths are burnt up. ॥117 (घ)॥
uttar.118.cau1: The unbroken awareness so'ham asmi (I am That) is the lamp's most brilliant flame. The joy of knowing the Self gives a clear light; then the delusion of difference that worldly existence grows from is destroyed, ॥1॥
uttar.118.cau2: and the boundless darkness of delusion and the rest, the household of mighty ignorance, is dispelled. Then that same intellect, gaining light, sits in the house of the heart and unties the knot. ॥2॥
uttar.118.cau3: If it can untie the knot, the soul attains its end. But knowing that the knot is being untied, king of birds, māyā then raises many obstacles. ॥3॥
uttar.118.cau4: She urges on many ṛddhis and siddhis (riches and powers), brother, who come and tempt the intellect with greed. By charm, force and trickery they draw near and blow out the lamp with the breeze of their garments. ॥4॥
uttar.118.cau5: If the intellect is truly wise, it knows them for its harm and will not even look at them. If that obstacle does not stop the intellect, then the gods make trouble. ॥5॥
uttar.118.cau6: The doors of the senses are the many windows of that house, and at each of them gods have taken their post. As soon as they see the wind of the sense-objects coming, they force the shutters open. ॥6॥
uttar.118.cau7: When that gale enters the house of the heart, the lamp of realised knowledge goes out. The knot was not undone, the light was gone, and the intellect was thrown into confusion by the wind of the sense-objects. ॥7॥
uttar.118.cau8: Knowledge does not please the senses or their gods; their love is always for the enjoyment of sense-objects. The wind of the sense-objects has bewildered the intellect; who then will light the lamp again in the same way? ॥8॥
uttar.118.do118क: Then the soul suffers once more the many pains of the round of birth and death. Śrī Hari's māyā is very hard to cross, lord of birds; it cannot be crossed. ॥118 (क)॥
uttar.118.do118ख: Discernment is hard to tell, hard to understand and hard to practise. If by pure chance, as a woodworm happens to carve a letter, one gains it, even then obstacles are many. ॥118 (ख)॥
uttar.119.cau1: The path of knowledge is a sword's edge; one falls from it in no time, king of birds. He who keeps to that path without a hindrance attains kaivalya, the supreme state. ॥1॥
uttar.119.cau2: Kaivalya, the supreme state, is very hard to reach, say the saints, the Purāṇas, the Vedas and the Āgamas. Yet, my lord, when one worships Śrī Rāma, that same liberation forces its way to him unbidden. ॥2॥
uttar.119.cau3: As water cannot stay without ground, whatever ten million means one tries, so, listen, king of birds, the joy of liberation cannot remain without devotion to Śrī Hari. ॥3॥
uttar.119.cau4: Considering this, wise devotees of Śrī Hari disdain liberation and are drawn to devotion. Through devotion, without effort or labour, ignorance, the root of worldly existence, is destroyed, ॥4॥
uttar.119.cau5: as one eats for the sake of being satisfied, and the fire of the stomach digests the food. Such is devotion to Śrī Hari, easy and joy-giving; who is so foolish as not to love it? ॥5॥
uttar.119.do119क: Without the feeling of servant and served, Garuḍa, one cannot cross worldly existence. Weigh this settled truth and worship Śrī Rāma's lotus feet. ॥119 (क)॥
uttar.119.do119ख: He makes the conscious inert and the inert conscious: blessed are the souls who worship Śrī Rāma, so mighty. ॥119 (ख)॥
uttar.120.cau1: I have explained the doctrine of knowledge; now hear the power of the jewel of devotion. Devotion to Śrī Rāma is a lovely wish-fulfilling gem; in whoever's heart it dwells, Garuḍa, ॥1॥
uttar.120.cau2: it is supreme light day and night, needing no lamp, no ghee, no wick. The poverty of delusion does not come near, and the wind of greed does not put it out. ॥2॥
uttar.120.cau3: The darkness of mighty ignorance is dispelled, and the swarms of moths are all defeated. Desire and the other villains do not come near one in whose heart devotion dwells. ॥3॥
uttar.120.cau4: For him poison becomes like nectar and a foe a friend; without that gem no one finds happiness. The grave ailments of the mind, which hold all creatures in misery, do not seize him. ॥4॥
uttar.120.cau5: If the gem of devotion to Śrī Rāma lives in someone's heart, not a trace of sorrow touches him even in dreams. In this world those are the crown of the wise who strive well to gain that gem. ॥5॥
uttar.120.cau6: Though that gem is there for all the world to see, no one gains it without Śrī Rāma's grace. The means of finding it are easy, but luckless men spurn them. ॥6॥
uttar.120.cau7: The Vedas and Purāṇas are holy mountains, and the many stories of Śrī Rāma are the fine mines in them. The good who know their secrets are the prospectors, a sound mind the pick, and knowledge and dispassion the eyes, Garuḍa. ॥7॥
uttar.120.cau8: Whoever searches for it with love finds the gem of devotion, mine of every joy. My lord, this is the faith of my heart: greater than Śrī Rāma is the servant of Śrī Rāma. ॥8॥
uttar.120.cau9: Śrī Rāma is the ocean and the steadfast good are the clouds; Śrī Hari is the sandal tree and the saints the breeze. The fruit of all is lovely devotion to Śrī Hari, and no one has gained it without a saint. ॥9॥
uttar.120.cau10: Considering this, whoever keeps the company of the good finds devotion to Śrī Rāma within easy reach, Garuḍa. ॥10॥
uttar.120.do120क: Brahman, the Veda, is the ocean, knowledge is Mount Mandara, and the saints are the gods who churn it and draw out the nectar of the story, whose sweetness is devotion. ॥120 (क)॥
uttar.120.do120ख: With dispassion as shield and knowledge as sword, slaying the foes pride, greed and delusion, the one who wins the victory is devotion to Śrī Hari; think it over and see, lord of birds. ॥120 (ख)॥
uttar.121.cau1: Then Garuḍa, king of birds, spoke lovingly: Gracious one, if you have affection for me, my lord, regard me as your own servant and answer my seven questions in full. ॥1॥
uttar.121.cau2: First tell me, my lord of steady mind, which body is the hardest of all to gain. What is the great sorrow, and what the great joy? Consider this too and tell it briefly. ॥2॥
uttar.121.cau3: You know the inner nature of the good and the wicked; describe their innate ways. What merit, renowned in the Vedas, is greatest? And tell me which sin is the most terrible. ॥3॥
uttar.121.cau4: Explain to me the diseases of the mind; you know all things, and your kindness to me is great. Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, dear one, with respect and deep love; I will tell this teaching briefly. ॥4॥
uttar.121.cau5: No body equals the human body; all creatures, moving and unmoving, long for it. It is the ladder to hell, to heaven and to liberation, and it gives the blessings of knowledge, dispassion and devotion. ॥5॥
uttar.121.cau6: Those men who take that body and do not worship Śrī Hari, but cling to the senses, grow base and baser; they take bits of broken glass in exchange, casting the philosopher's stone from their hand. ॥6॥
uttar.121.cau7: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy in the world like meeting the saints. To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the very nature of the saints, king of birds. ॥7॥
uttar.121.cau8: The saints bear suffering for the good of others; the wretched wicked, to bring others suffering. Like the birch tree, the kindly saints always endure great hardship for others' good. ॥8॥
uttar.121.cau9: The wicked, like hemp, bind others, and have their skin stripped and die in torment for it. The wicked do others harm though nothing is in it for them, like the snake and the rat; listen, Garuḍa. ॥9॥
uttar.121.cau10: They ruin others' wealth and are ruined themselves, as hailstones beat down the crops and melt away. The rise of the wicked brings the world distress, as does that of Ketu, the notorious evil planet. ॥10॥
uttar.121.cau11: The rise of the saints always brings happiness, as the moon and the sun bring joy to the whole world. The highest dharma, known from the Vedas, is non-violence, and no sin is as heavy as speaking ill of others. ॥11॥
uttar.121.cau12: One who reviles Śiva or the guru becomes a frog, and keeps that body for a thousand births. One who reviles the brāhmaṇas suffers many hells and is then born in the world in the body of a crow. ॥12॥
uttar.121.cau13: Proud creatures who revile the gods and the Vedas fall into the Raurava hell. Those given to reviling the saints become owls, lovers of the night of delusion, the sun of knowledge gone from them. ॥13॥
uttar.121.cau14: The dull who revile everyone are born as bats. Now hear, dear one, of the diseases of the mind, from which all people suffer. ॥14॥
uttar.121.cau15: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from them in turn spring many pains. Desire is wind, boundless greed is phlegm, and anger is bile, which always burns the breast. ॥15॥
uttar.121.cau16: If these three brothers make friends, the painful sannipāta (a fever of all three humours) arises. The many cravings for sense-objects, hard to fulfil, are all those pains; who knows their names? ॥16॥
uttar.121.cau17: Attachment is ringworm, envy is the itch, and joy and grief are a host of throat diseases. The burning at seeing another's happiness is consumption; wickedness and crookedness of mind are leprosy. ॥17॥
uttar.121.cau18: Egotism is a most painful gout; hypocrisy, deceit, pride and vanity are the guinea-worm. Craving is a severe dropsy, and the three kinds of longing are a raging tertian fever. ॥18॥
uttar.121.cau19: Envy and lack of discernment are two kinds of fever. How far can I go on naming the many evil diseases? ॥19॥
uttar.121.do121क: Men die in the grip of a single disease, and these are many diseases, past all cure. They torment the soul without end; how then can it find samādhi, inner stillness? ॥121 (क)॥
uttar.121.do121ख: Observances, dharma, good conduct, austerity, knowledge, sacrifice, prayer and charity, and remedies by the million besides: yet with them, Garuḍa, these diseases do not go. ॥121 (ख)॥
uttar.122.cau1: In this way all creatures in the world are sick, suffering from sorrow, delight, fear, attachment and separation. These few ailments of the mind I have sung of; they are in everyone, yet rare are those who have perceived them. ॥1॥
uttar.122.cau2: Once recognised, these wicked ailments dwindle a little, but these tormentors of people are not destroyed. Once they get the wrong food of sense-objects, they sprout even in the hearts of sages; what chance, then, for poor men? ॥2॥
uttar.122.cau3: By Śrī Rāma's grace all these diseases perish, if the means come together in this way: faith in the words of the true guru, the physician, and for restraint, no longing for the objects of sense. ॥3॥
uttar.122.cau4: Devotion to Śrī Rāma is the life-giving herb, and a mind full of faith is what it is taken with. Taken in this way, those diseases are surely cured; otherwise they do not go, though ten million remedies be tried. ॥4॥
uttar.122.cau5: Know the mind to be free of disease, my lord, when the strength of dispassion grows in the heart, when the hunger for right understanding increases, new every day, and the weakness of longing for the senses has gone. ॥5॥
uttar.122.cau6: When the mind has bathed in the water of pure knowledge, devotion to Śrī Rāma fills the heart and stays there. Śiva, Brahmā, Śuka, Sanaka and his brothers, and Nārada, sages skilled in reflection on Brahman, ॥6॥
uttar.122.cau7: are all of this one view, lord of birds: love should be given to Śrī Rāma's lotus feet. The Vedas, the Purāṇas and every scripture say that without devotion to Śrī Rāma there is no happiness. ॥7॥
uttar.122.cau8: Hair may grow on a tortoise's back, a barren woman's son may kill a man, flowers of every kind may blossom in the sky; still no being hostile to Śrī Hari finds happiness. ॥8॥
uttar.122.cau9: A mirage's water may quench thirst, horns may spring from a hare's head, darkness may put out the sun; still no being turned from Śrī Rāma finds happiness. ॥9॥
uttar.122.cau10: Fire may even spring out of ice, yet no one turned away from Śrī Rāma finds happiness. ॥10॥
uttar.122.do122क: Ghee may come from churning water, oil may be pressed from sand, but without the worship of Śrī Hari the ocean of worldly existence is not crossed: this truth is unshakable. ॥122 (क)॥
uttar.122.do122ख: The Lord can make a mosquito into Brahmā, and make Brahmā lower than a mosquito. Seeing this, the wise give up doubt and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥122 (ख)॥
uttar.123.shloka122ग: I tell you what is firmly settled, and my words are not false: those who worship Śrī Hari cross over what is most hard to cross. ॥122 (ग)॥
uttar.123.cau1: My lord, I have told the incomparable deeds of Śrī Hari, at length and in brief, as far as my understanding goes. Garuḍa, this is the settled teaching of the Vedas: worship Śrī Rāma, setting every other task aside. ॥1॥
uttar.123.cau2: Leaving the Lord Śrī Rāma, whom else should one serve, who claims even a fool like me for his own? You are realised knowledge itself, with no delusion in you; yet, my lord, you have shown me great kindness, ॥2॥
uttar.123.cau3: in that you asked me for the most holy story of Śrī Rāma, which delights the minds of Śuka, Sanaka and his brothers, and Śiva. In this world the company of the good is hard to find even once, for a moment or for a short while. ॥3॥
uttar.123.cau4: Garuḍa, think it over in your own heart: was I fit to worship Śrī Rāma? I, the lowest of birds and impure in every way, have been made by the Lord holy and known throughout the world. ॥4॥
uttar.123.do123क: Today I am blessed, deeply blessed, though lacking in every way, for Śrī Rāma, knowing me as his own, has granted me the meeting with a saint. ॥123 (क)॥
uttar.123.do123ख: My lord, I have spoken as my understanding allows, and have kept nothing back. The deeds of Śrī Rāma are an ocean: can anyone touch its bottom? ॥123 (ख)॥
uttar.124.cau1: Remembering Śrī Rāma's many virtues, the wise Kākabhuśuṇḍi rejoiced again and again. Then he said: He whose glory the Vedas have sung as neti, not this, whose might, majesty and lordship are beyond compare, ॥1॥
uttar.124.cau2: whose feet are worshipped by Śiva and Brahmā: his grace on me is his utmost tenderness. Such a nature I neither hear of nor see anywhere; whom, Garuḍa, could I count equal to Śrī Rāma? ॥2॥
uttar.124.cau3: Seekers, adepts, the liberated, the detached, poets, the learned, the grateful, renunciants, yogis, heroes, great ascetics, the wise, those intent on dharma, scholars and those of realised knowledge: ॥3॥
uttar.124.cau4: none of them crosses over without serving my Lord. To Śrī Rāma I bow, I bow, I bow. Going to his refuge, even heaps of sin like me are made pure: I bow to the Imperishable. ॥4॥
uttar.124.do124क: His name is the cure for the sickness of worldly life and removes the three terrible torments; may he, the compassionate one, be ever kind to me and to you. ॥124 (क)॥
uttar.124.do124ख: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's auspicious words and seeing his love for Śrī Rāma's feet, Garuḍa spoke words full of love, all his doubt gone: ॥124 (ख)॥
uttar.125.cau1: Hearing your words, steeped in the delight of devotion to Śrī Rāma, I have reached life's fulfilment. A new love for Śrī Rāma's feet has arisen in me, and all the trouble born of māyā has gone. ॥1॥
uttar.125.cau2: In the ocean of delusion you became my ship; my lord, you have given me joys of many kinds. I have nothing to give in return; again and again I bow to your feet. ॥2॥
uttar.125.cau3: Your every wish is fulfilled and you love Śrī Rāma; dear sir, no one is as fortunate as you. Saints, trees, rivers, mountains and the earth: everything they do is for the good of others. ॥3॥
uttar.125.cau4: Poets have called a saint's heart like butter, but they did not know how to put it rightly. Butter melts when it is itself heated; the holy saints melt at the sorrow of others. ॥4॥
uttar.125.cau5: My life and my birth have borne fruit; by your grace all my doubt is gone. Always know me as your own servant. So, Umā, the best of birds said again and again. ॥5॥
uttar.125.do125क: Then Garuḍa, steady of mind, bowed his head at his feet with love, and went to Vaikuṇṭha, keeping Śrī Rāma in his heart. ॥125 (क)॥
uttar.125.do125ख: Girijā, there is no gain to equal the meeting with saints, yet it does not come without the grace of Śrī Hari: so the Vedas and Purāṇas sing. ॥125 (ख)॥
uttar.126.cau1: I have told this most holy history; as soon as the ears hear it, the snares of worldly existence fall away, and love arises for the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma, the wish-fulfilling tree of those who bow to him, the treasury of compassion. ॥1॥
uttar.126.cau2: Sins born of thought, deed and word leave those who listen to this story with ears and mind intent. Pilgrimage and the whole range of spiritual practices, mastery in yoga, dispassion and knowledge, ॥2॥
uttar.126.cau3: rites of many kinds, dharma, vows and gifts, restraint, self-control, japa, austerity and many sacrifices, compassion for living beings, service of Brahmins and of the guru, and the excellence of learning, humility and discernment: ॥3॥
uttar.126.cau4: of every practice the Vedas describe, Bhavānī, the fruit is devotion to Śrī Hari. That devotion to Śrī Rāma, sung in the Vedas, few have won, and those few only by his grace. ॥4॥
uttar.126.do126: Devotion to Śrī Hari, hard even for sages to win, is gained without effort by those men who hear this story continually, with faith. ॥126॥
uttar.127.cau1: He alone knows all, he alone has true worth, he alone is the knower; he alone is the ornament of the earth, a scholar and a giver. He alone is devoted to dharma and the protector of his family, whose mind is given to Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥1॥
uttar.127.cau2: He alone is skilled in right conduct and truly wise; he alone has rightly understood the teaching of the Vedas. He alone is a poet, a scholar and steadfast in battle, who leaves guile behind and worships Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.127.cau3: Blessed the land where the Gaṅgā flows; blessed the woman who keeps faith with her husband. Blessed the king who rules by right policy; blessed the Brahmin who does not stray from his dharma. ॥3॥
uttar.127.cau4: Blessed the wealth that takes the first course, giving; blessed and ripe the mind that is set on merit. Blessed the hour spent in the company of the good; blessed the birth with unbroken devotion to Brahmins. ॥4॥
uttar.127.do127: Blessed is that family, Umā, listen: the world reveres it and it is supremely pure, the family that brings forth a humble man wholly given to Śrī Rāma. ॥127॥
uttar.128.cau1: I have told this story as my understanding allows, though at first I kept it hidden. Seeing the great love in your mind, I then told you the story of Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
uttar.128.cau2: This should not be told to the deceitful and the stubborn, nor to one who does not listen with his mind to Śrī Hari's play. Nor should it be told to the greedy, the angry or the lustful, nor to one who does not worship the Lord of all that moves and does not move. ॥2॥
uttar.128.cau3: Never tell it to one hostile to Brahmins, even if he is a king equal to Indra. Those fit for Śrī Rāma's story are the ones to whom the company of the good is very dear. ॥3॥
uttar.128.cau4: Those who love the guru's feet, hold to right conduct and serve Brahmins: they too are fit for it. And to one who holds Śrī Rāma dear as life, it gives a joy beyond all others. ॥4॥
uttar.128.do128: Whoever longs for love of Śrī Rāma's feet, or for the state of liberation, let him drink this story with feeling from the cups of his ears. ॥128॥
uttar.129.cau1: Girijā, I have told you Śrī Rāma's story, which quells the sins of the Kali age and cleans the mind of its stains. It is the reviving herb for the sickness of the round of rebirth; so the Vedas and the wise sing of Śrī Rāma's story. ॥1॥
uttar.129.cau2: In it are seven lovely steps, the paths to devotion to Śrī Rāma. Only he on whom Śrī Hari's grace is very great sets foot upon this path. ॥2॥
uttar.129.cau3: Those who sing this story without guile find the wishes of their heart fulfilled. For those who tell it, hear it and approve it, the ocean of worldly existence is no wider than a cow's hoofprint, and they step across. ॥3॥
uttar.129.cau4: Having heard the whole story, which delighted her heart, Girijā spoke in gentle words: My lord, by your grace my doubt is gone, and a new love for Śrī Rāma's feet has arisen. ॥4॥
uttar.129.do129: Lord of the universe, by your grace I am now fulfilled. Firm devotion to Śrī Rāma has arisen in me, and all my sorrows are past. ॥129॥
uttar.130.cau1: This auspicious dialogue of Śiva and Umā brings happiness and allays sorrow. It breaks the bonds of worldly existence, destroys doubt, brings joy to the devotees and is beloved of the good. ॥1॥
uttar.130.cau2: Those in the world who worship Śrī Rāma hold nothing as dear as this. Through Śrī Rāma's grace I have sung, as my understanding allows, this pure and lovely story. ॥2॥
uttar.130.cau3: In this age of Kali there is no other means: not yoga, nor sacrifice, nor japa, austerity, vows or worship. Remember Śrī Rāma, sing of Śrī Rāma, and hear the host of Śrī Rāma's virtues always. ॥3॥
uttar.130.cau4: Poets, the Vedas, saints and the Purāṇas sing of him whose great vow is to make the fallen pure. Mind, give up crookedness and worship him; who has ever worshipped Śrī Rāma and not found salvation? ॥4॥
uttar.130.cha1: Listen, foolish mind: who has worshipped Śrī Rāma, purifier of the fallen, and not found salvation? He delivered many wicked ones: the courtesan, Ajāmila, the hunter, the vulture, the elephant and others. Even those among the Ābhīras, Yavanas, Kirātas, Khasas, Śvapacas and others who are sin itself become pure by uttering the Name but once; Rāma, I bow to you. ॥1॥
uttar.130.cha2: Those who tell, hear and sing this story of Śrī Rāma, the ornament of Raghu's line, wash away the impurity of the Kali age and of the mind, and reach Śrī Rāma's abode without toil. Whoever finds five or seven of its caupāīs charming and keeps them in his heart, from him Śrī Rāma takes away the faults born of the five dreadful forms of ignorance. ॥2॥
uttar.130.cha3: He who is beautiful and wise, a treasury of grace, and loves the helpless, is Śrī Rāma alone; who else equals him in doing good for no gain of his own and in granting liberation? By the merest trace of his grace even dull-witted Tulasīdāsa has found supreme rest; there is no lord anywhere like Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
uttar.130.do130क: O hero of the Raghus, there is none as lowly as I, and none who befriends the lowly as you do. Bearing this in mind, O jewel of Raghu's line, take away the harsh distress of my worldly existence. ॥130 (क)॥
uttar.130.do130ख: Just as a man of desire holds a woman dear, and the greedy hold money dear, so, O Lord of the Raghus, O Rāma, may you be dear to me without cease. ॥130 (ख)॥
uttar.end.shloka1: The Rāmāyaṇa, hard to fathom, which the Lord Śrī Śambhu, the great poet, composed long ago so that ceaseless devotion to the lotus feet of glorious Śrī Rāma might be gained, Tulasīdāsa, holding it to be absorbed in the name of Śrī Rāma, and to still the darkness within his own heart, has likewise set it in the common tongue as this Mānasa. ॥1॥
uttar.end.shloka2: Holy, taking away sin, ever bringing good, bestowing realised knowledge and devotion, removing the stain of māyā and delusion, utterly pure, brimming with the water of love, auspicious: those who bathe with devotion in this Mānasa of Śrī Rāma's deeds are not scorched by the fierce rays of the sun of worldly existence. ॥2॥

bal.17.so17: I bow to Hanumān, son of the Wind, a fire to the forest of the wicked, full of wisdom.
In the house of his heart Śrī Rāma dwells, holding his bow and arrows. ॥17॥
kishkindha.0.shloka1: Beautiful as the jasmine and the blue lotus, mighty beyond measure, both abodes of realised knowledge,
rich in splendour, excellent archers, praised by the Vedas, dear to the hosts of cows and Brahmins,
taking human form by māyā (the Lord's power of illusion), the two best of the Raghus, the armour of true dharma, benevolent to all,
intent on the search for Sītā and travelling the road: may those two indeed grant us devotion. ॥1॥
kishkindha.0.shloka2: Born of the ocean of the Veda, utterly destroying the stains of the Kali age, and imperishable,
ever shining on the lovely, peerless moon of glorious Śiva's face,
the medicine for the sickness of worldly existence, the giver of joy, the very life of Śrī Jānakī:
blessed are the meritorious who drink without ceasing the nectar of Śrī Rāma's name. ॥2॥
kishkindha.0.sou1: Knowing Kāśī as the land where liberation is born, a mine of knowledge and the destroyer of sin,
and the place where Śiva and Bhavānī dwell, why should one not turn to Kāśī and live there?
kishkindha.0.sou2: He drank the deadly poison when the hosts of gods were burning:
dull mind, why do you not worship him? Who is as compassionate as Śaṅkara?
kishkindha.1.cau1: Then Śrī Rāma went on and drew near the mountain Ṛṣyamūka.
There Sugrīva lived with his ministers. Seeing the two coming, the very bounds of matchless strength, ॥1॥
kishkindha.1.cau2: Sugrīva, greatly alarmed, said: Listen, Hanumān: these two men are treasuries of strength and beauty.
Take the form of a young brahmacārī, go and see. Find out in your mind who they are, and let me know by a sign. ॥2॥
kishkindha.1.cau3: If they are sent by Vāli and mean harm, I must flee at once and leave this mountain.
Hanumān took the form of a Brahmin and went there, and bowing his head he asked: ॥3॥
kishkindha.1.cau4: Who are you, heroes, one dark and one fair, roaming the forest in the guise of Kṣatriyas?
Treading the hard ground on tender feet, my lords, for what reason do you wander in the forest? ॥4॥
kishkindha.1.cau5: Your limbs are soft, charming and beautiful, yet you bear the harsh sun and winds of the forest.
Are you one of the three gods, or are you the two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa? ॥5॥
kishkindha.1.do1: Or are you the cause of the world, who carries souls across worldly existence and lifts the burden of the earth,
the Lord of all the worlds, who has come down in human form? ॥1॥
kishkindha.2.cau1: Śrī Rāma said: We are sons of Daśaratha, king of Kosala, and we came to the forest at our father's bidding.
We are two brothers named Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. With us was a lovely woman of delicate frame. ॥1॥
kishkindha.2.cau2: Here a demon carried off Sītā, and we wander searching for her, Brahmin.
We have told you our own story; now, Brahmin, tell us yours plainly. ॥2॥
kishkindha.2.cau3: Recognising the Lord, Hanumān clasped his feet and fell at them. That joy, Umā, cannot be described.
His body thrilled; he could not utter a word, gazing at the beauty of the Lord's guise. ॥3॥
kishkindha.2.cau4: Then, steadying himself, he sang the Lord's praise, his heart glad at knowing his own master.
He said: My Lord, it was right for me to ask; but why do you ask, as if you were a man? ॥4॥
kishkindha.2.cau5: Under the sway of your māyā I wander astray; that is why I did not know my Lord. ॥5॥
kishkindha.2.do2: For one thing, I am dull, in the grip of delusion, crooked of heart and ignorant;
and then the Lord, the friend of the lowly, forgot me as well. ॥2॥
kishkindha.3.cau1: My Lord, though I have many faults, let the servant never slip from his master's mind.
My Lord, the soul is deluded by your māyā; it is set free only by your own grace. ॥1॥
kishkindha.3.cau2: Besides, O hero of the Raghus, I swear by you that I know no way at all of worship.
A servant relying on his master, and a son on his mother, stays free of care; it falls to the master to provide for him. ॥2॥
kishkindha.3.cau3: With these words, overwhelmed, he threw himself at the Lord's feet; he showed his own form, and love flooded his heart.
Then Śrī Rāma raised him and held him to his breast, and soothed him, bathing him with the tears of his own eyes. ॥3॥
kishkindha.3.cau4: The Lord said: Listen, Hanumān: let your heart not be downcast; I hold you twice as dear as Lakṣmaṇa.
All call me impartial; yet my servant is dear to me, since he has no other refuge. ॥4॥
kishkindha.3.do3: Hanumān, he alone is single-minded whose understanding never wavers from this:
I am the servant, and my master is the Lord, whose form is all that moves and all that does not move. ॥3॥
kishkindha.4.cau1: Seeing his master favourable, Hanumān, son of the Wind, rejoiced at heart, and all his pain was gone.
He said: My Lord, the king of the monkeys lives on this mountain; that Sugrīva is your servant. ॥1॥
kishkindha.4.cau2: My Lord, make friends with him, and knowing him to be helpless, free him from fear.
He will set the search for Sītā going; he will send out monkeys by the million, here and there. ॥2॥
kishkindha.4.cau3: Having explained the whole matter so, he took them both up on his back.
The sight of Śrī Rāma made Sugrīva feel that his birth had been supremely blessed. ॥3॥
kishkindha.4.cau4: He greeted them with reverence, bowing his head at their feet, and Śrī Rāma and his younger brother embraced him.
Sugrīva thought to himself: O Creator, will these two show me love? ॥4॥
kishkindha.4.do4: Then Hanumān told each side the other's whole story,
and, with fire as witness, joined them in a friendship firmly sealed. ॥4॥
kishkindha.5.cau1: They made friends and held nothing back between them, and Lakṣmaṇa told all of Śrī Rāma's story.
Sugrīva, his eyes filled with tears, said: My Lord, the princess of Mithilā will be found. ॥1॥
kishkindha.5.cau2: Once I was sitting here with my ministers, deep in thought,
when I saw her going by the path of the sky, helpless in another's power and weeping bitterly. ॥2॥
kishkindha.5.cau3: Crying, Rāma, Rāma, alas Rāma, she saw us and let fall a garment.
Śrī Rāma asked for it, and Sugrīva gave it at once. Pressing the cloth to his breast, he grieved deeply. ॥3॥
kishkindha.5.cau4: Sugrīva said: Listen, O hero of the Raghus: put away grief and take courage.
I will serve you in every way, so that Jānakī may come back to you. ॥4॥
kishkindha.5.do5: Hearing his friend's words, the ocean of mercy, the utmost in strength, was glad,
and said: Tell me, Sugrīva, why do you live in the forest? ॥5॥
kishkindha.6.cau1: Sugrīva said: My Lord, Vāli and I are brothers, and the love between us was beyond words.
My Lord, a son of Maya, Māyāvī by name, came to our town. ॥1॥
kishkindha.6.cau2: At midnight he shouted his challenge at the city gate, and Vāli could not bear the enemy's show of might.
Vāli ran at him, and seeing him the other fled; I too went, close behind my brother. ॥2॥
kishkindha.6.cau3: He went into a cave in a great mountain, and then Vāli told me plainly:
Wait for me a fortnight; if I do not come back by then, know that I have been killed. ॥3॥
kishkindha.6.cau4: I stayed there a month, O slayer of Khara, and then a great stream of blood gushed out.
He has killed Vāli, I thought, and will come and kill me; so I set a rock there and fled. ॥4॥
kishkindha.6.cau5: Seeing the city without its lord, the ministers made me king against my will.
Vāli killed him and came home, and seeing me he let ill feeling grow in his heart. ॥5॥
kishkindha.6.cau6: He beat me savagely, as one beats an enemy, and seized all I had, and my wife too.
For fear of him, O compassionate hero of the Raghus, I wandered all the worlds in distress. ॥6॥
kishkindha.6.cau7: Because of a curse he does not come here, and still I live in fear at heart.
As he heard his servant's sorrow, the Lord who is kind to the lowly felt both his mighty arms throb. ॥7॥
kishkindha.6.do6: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, Sugrīva: one arrow alone will slay Vāli.
Even if he runs to Brahmā and Rudra for refuge, his life will not be spared. ॥6॥
kishkindha.7.cau1: Those who are not pained by a friend's pain: even to look on them is a grave sin.
One should count one's own mountain of sorrow as a speck of dust, and a friend's speck of sorrow as Mount Meru. ॥1॥
kishkindha.7.cau2: Those in whom such a mind has not come naturally, why do the fools insist on making friends?
A friend turns one from the wrong path to the right one, makes one's virtues known and hides one's faults. ॥2॥
kishkindha.7.cau3: He gives and takes with no misgiving in his mind, and always does one good as far as his strength allows.
In times of trouble his love grows a hundredfold. The Vedas say these are the marks of a good friend. ॥3॥
kishkindha.7.cau4: One who speaks soft, studied words to your face, but behind your back works harm with crookedness in his heart,
whose mind, brother, moves crookedly like a snake: such a false friend is best given up. ॥4॥
kishkindha.7.cau5: A wicked servant, a miserly king, an ill-natured woman and a deceitful friend: these four are like a stabbing pain.
Friend, set your worry aside and rely on my strength; I will do your work in every way. ॥5॥
kishkindha.7.cau6: Sugrīva said: Listen, O hero of the Raghus: Vāli is mighty and unshaken in battle.
Sugrīva showed him the bones of Dundubhi and the palm trees, and Śrī Rāma brought them down without effort. ॥6॥
kishkindha.7.cau7: Seeing his boundless strength, Sugrīva loved him the more, and was sure that he would slay Vāli.
Again and again he bowed his head at the Lord's feet; knowing him for the Lord, the king of the monkeys rejoiced at heart. ॥7॥
kishkindha.7.cau8: Then knowledge dawned on him, and he said: My Lord, by your grace my mind has become still.
I will give up comfort, wealth, family and greatness, all of it, and serve you. ॥8॥
kishkindha.7.cau9: The saints who worship your feet say that all these stand in the way of devotion to Rāma.
Foe and friend, joy and sorrow in this world are the work of māyā, not the ultimate truth. ॥9॥
kishkindha.7.cau10: It is Vāli who has done me the greatest good, Rāma: thanks to him I have found you, who end all sorrow.
If one fights with someone in a dream, on waking one understands and feels abashed. ॥10॥
kishkindha.7.cau11: My Lord, now grant me this grace, that I may leave everything and worship you day and night.
Hearing Sugrīva's words full of dispassion, Śrī Rāma, bow in hand, smiled and said: ॥11॥
kishkindha.7.cau12: All that you have said is true; but, friend, my word cannot prove false.
As a showman makes a monkey dance, Garuḍa, so Śrī Rāma makes all dance: so the Vedas sing. ॥12॥
kishkindha.7.cau13: Taking Sugrīva with him, Śrī Rāma set out, bow and arrows in hand.
Then Śrī Rāma sent Sugrīva on; strengthened by him, Sugrīva went close and roared. ॥13॥
kishkindha.7.cau14: Hearing it, Vāli rushed out in a fury; his wife caught his feet in her hands and pleaded with him:
Listen, my husband: the two brothers Sugrīva has joined are the very bounds of splendour and strength. ॥14॥
kishkindha.7.cau15: They are Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, sons of the king of Kosala, who could conquer even Death in battle. ॥15॥
kishkindha.7.do7: Vāli said: Listen, my timid dear: Śrī Rāma looks on all alike.
If perchance he kills me, then I shall have found my Lord. ॥7॥
kishkindha.8.cau1: With these words Vāli set out in his great pride, counting Sugrīva no more than a blade of grass.
The two clashed. Vāli taunted him fiercely, struck him with his fist and gave a mighty roar. ॥1॥
kishkindha.8.cau2: Then Sugrīva fled in distress, for the blow of that fist had struck him like a thunderbolt.
Sugrīva said: It is as I told you, O compassionate hero of the Raghus: he is not my brother; he is my death. ॥2॥
kishkindha.8.cau3: Śrī Rāma said: You two brothers look alike, and because of that confusion I did not kill him.
He laid his hand on Sugrīva, whose body turned hard as a thunderbolt, and every pain left him. ॥3॥
kishkindha.8.cau4: He placed a garland of flowers round Sugrīva's neck and sent him back, giving him great strength.
Again the two fought in many ways, while Śrī Rāma watched from behind a tree. ॥4॥
kishkindha.8.do8: Sugrīva tried many tricks and all his strength, then, seized by fear, lost heart.
Then Śrī Rāma drew an arrow and shot Vāli in the middle of his chest. ॥8॥
kishkindha.9.cau1: Struck by the arrow, Vāli fell to the ground in agony, but seeing the Lord before him he rose and sat up.
Dark was the Lord's body, his hair bound up in matted locks on his head, his eyes red, an arrow fitted to his bow. ॥1॥
kishkindha.9.cau2: Gazing again and again, he set his mind on the Lord's feet; he knew him for the Lord and held his birth fulfilled.
There was love in his heart but harsh words on his lips; looking at Śrī Rāma, he said: ॥2॥
kishkindha.9.cau3: My Lord, you came down to earth for the sake of dharma, yet you have killed me like a hunter.
Am I your enemy, and Sugrīva dear to you? For what fault, my Lord, have you killed me? ॥3॥
kishkindha.9.cau4: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, wicked one: a younger brother's wife, a sister, a son's wife and a daughter — these four are all alike.
Whoever looks on them with an evil eye may be slain, and there is no sin in it. ॥4॥
kishkindha.9.cau5: Fool, your pride is beyond measure; you would not listen to your wife's counsel.
You knew he leant on the strength of my arms, and still, base and arrogant as you are, you sought to kill him. ॥5॥
kishkindha.9.do9: Vāli said: Listen, Rāma: my cleverness is of no use before my master.
My Lord, now that at my last hour I have you for my refuge, am I a sinner still? ॥9॥
kishkindha.10.cau1: Hearing Vāli's very gentle words, Śrī Rāma laid his own hand on his head.
Śrī Rāma said: Let me make your body undying; keep your life. Vāli said: Listen, treasury of mercy: ॥1॥
kishkindha.10.cau2: Sages strive birth after birth, and yet at the end the name Rāma does not rise to their lips.
He by the power of whose name Śiva grants to all alike in Kāśī the state that never perishes ॥2॥
kishkindha.10.cau3: has come before my eyes. My Lord, will such a chance ever come about again? ॥3॥
kishkindha.10.cha1: He whose virtues the Vedas ever sing, saying “not this, not this”, stands before my eyes,
he whom sages, having mastered breath and mind and drained the senses of their relish, only now and then attain in meditation.
Taking me to be in the grip of great pride, the Lord told me to keep my body;
but who would be fool enough to insist on cutting down the wish-fulfilling tree to make a hedge for an acacia? ॥1॥
kishkindha.10.cha2: Now, my Lord, look on me with compassion and grant the boon I ask:
in whatever form of life my karma has me born, there may I love Śrī Rāma's feet.
This son of mine is my equal in humility and strength; take him to yourself, Lord, giver of all good.
Lord of gods and men, take Aṅgada by the arm and make him your own servant. ॥2॥
kishkindha.10.do10: Holding firm in love for Śrī Rāma's feet, Vāli gave up his body,
as an elephant does not even notice a garland of flowers slipping from its neck. ॥10॥
kishkindha.11.cau1: Śrī Rāma sent Vāli to his own abode. The townsfolk all came running in distress.
Tārā lamented in many ways, her hair loosened, heedless of her body. ॥1॥
kishkindha.11.cau2: Seeing Tārā distraught, Śrī Rāma gave her knowledge and lifted the māyā that held her.
He said: Earth, water, fire, sky and air — of these five is this body made, and it is utterly base. ॥2॥
kishkindha.11.cau3: That body lies plainly before you in sleep, and the soul is eternal: for whom, then, do you weep?
Knowledge dawned in her; she fell at the Lord's feet and asked for, and received, the boon of supreme devotion. ॥3॥
kishkindha.11.cau4: Umā, the Lord Śrī Rāma makes all dance like a wooden puppet.
Then he gave Sugrīva his command, and Sugrīva duly performed all the rites for the dead. ॥4॥
kishkindha.11.cau5: Śrī Rāma instructed his younger brother: Go and give the kingdom to Sugrīva.
Bowing their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet, all set out as he bade them. ॥5॥
kishkindha.11.do11: Lakṣmaṇa at once summoned the townspeople and an assembly of Brahmins,
and gave the kingdom to Sugrīva and to Aṅgada the rank of heir to the throne. ॥11॥
kishkindha.12.cau1: Umā, there is no friend in the world like Śrī Rāma: no guru, father, mother, brother or master.
Gods, men and sages all follow one way: they love for their own ends. ॥1॥
kishkindha.12.cau2: Sugrīva, harried day and night by dread of Vāli, his body covered with wounds and his breast burning with care —
that same Sugrīva the Lord made king of the monkeys. Such is the boundless compassion of Śrī Rāma's nature. ॥2॥
kishkindha.12.cau3: Why should those who forsake such a Lord, even knowing him, not fall into the net of misfortune?
Then he sent for Sugrīva and taught him the conduct of a king in many ways. ॥3॥
kishkindha.12.cau4: The Lord said: Listen, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys: for fourteen years I shall not enter a town.
The summer is over and the rains have come; I shall make my dwelling on a mountain close by. ॥4॥
kishkindha.12.cau5: Rule the kingdom with Aṅgada, and keep my work always in your heart.
When Sugrīva had gone back to his palace, Śrī Rāma made his dwelling on Mount Pravarṣaṇa. ॥5॥
kishkindha.12.do12: Long before, the gods had shaped a lovely cave in that mountain and kept it,
for Śrī Rāma, the treasury of mercy, would come and live there for some days. ॥12॥
kishkindha.13.cau1: The lovely forest, in full flower, was glorious, and swarms of bees hummed in their craving for honey.
From the time the Lord came, fine tubers, roots, fruits and leaves grew in plenty. ॥1॥
kishkindha.13.cau2: Seeing that charming, peerless mountain, Śrī Rāma, sovereign of the gods, stayed there with his younger brother.
Gods, siddhas and sages took the bodies of bees, birds and deer and served the Lord. ॥2॥
kishkindha.13.cau3: From the time the Lord of Ramā made his home there, the forest became full of blessing.
There was a slab of crystal, very white and fair, and on it the two brothers sat at ease. ॥3॥
kishkindha.13.cau4: He would tell his younger brother many discourses on devotion, dispassion, kingly conduct and discernment.
It was the season of rains; clouds covered the sky, and their thunder sounded most pleasing. ॥4॥
kishkindha.13.do13: Śrī Rāma said: Lakṣmaṇa, see the flocks of peacocks dancing at the sight of the clouds,
as a householder given to dispassion rejoices on seeing a devotee of Viṣṇu. ॥13॥
kishkindha.14.cau1: The massing clouds thunder dreadfully in the sky; without my beloved my heart is afraid.
The flash of lightning does not stay in the clouds, just as the love of the wicked does not last. ॥1॥
kishkindha.14.cau2: The clouds come down low to the earth to rain, as the wise bow down when they gain learning.
The mountains bear the beating of the drops as saints bear the words of the wicked. ॥2॥
kishkindha.14.cau3: The little rivers fill and rush on, breaking their banks, as the wicked swagger over even a little wealth.
Water falling on the ground turns muddy, as though māyā had wrapped itself round the soul. ॥3॥
kishkindha.14.cau4: Gathering little by little, the water fills the ponds, as good qualities come to a good man.
River water reaching the ocean grows still, as the soul becomes steadfast when it finds Śrī Hari. ॥4॥
kishkindha.14.do14: The earth is green and so thick with grass that no path can be made out,
as true scriptures are hidden by the wrangling of false doctrine. ॥14॥
kishkindha.15.cau1: The croaking of frogs on every side is pleasant, as though bands of young students were reciting the Vedas.
Many trees have put out new leaves, like the mind of a seeker who has found discernment. ॥1॥
kishkindha.15.cau2: The arka and javāsa plants have lost their leaves, as under good rule the schemes of the wicked come to nothing.
Search as you may, there is no dust to be found anywhere, as anger drives dharma far away. ॥2॥
kishkindha.15.cau3: How fair the earth looks, rich with crops, like the wealth of one who does good to others.
In the thick darkness of night the fireflies glitter, as if a band of hypocrites had gathered. ॥3॥
kishkindha.15.cau4: Heavy rain has burst the beds of the fields, as women go astray when they become independent.
Clever farmers weed their crops, as the wise cast off delusion, pride and vanity. ॥4॥
kishkindha.15.cau5: The cakravāka birds are nowhere to be seen, as virtues flee when the Kali age comes.
Rain falls on barren ground, but no grass springs up, as desire does not arise in the heart of Hari's devotee. ॥5॥
kishkindha.15.cau6: The earth teems and glows with creatures of every kind, as the people prosper under good rule.
Here and there many travellers have halted, weary, as the senses come to rest when knowledge arises. ॥6॥
kishkindha.15.do15क: At times a strong wind blows and the clouds melt away here and there,
as the good ways of a family perish when an unworthy son is born into it. ॥15 (क)॥
kishkindha.15.do15ख: At times there is deep darkness in the daytime, and at times the sun shines out,
as knowledge is lost in bad company and springs up again in good. ॥15 (ख)॥
kishkindha.16.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa, see: the rains are past and autumn has come, lovely beyond compare.
Flowering kāsa grass has spread over all the earth, as if the rainy season were showing its old age. ॥1॥
kishkindha.16.cau2: The star Agastya has risen, and the roads have lost their water, as greed is dried up by contentment.
The clear water of rivers and lakes is as lovely as a saint's heart freed from pride and delusion. ॥2॥
kishkindha.16.cau3: Little by little the water of rivers and lakes dries up, as the wise let go of the sense of “mine”.
Knowing autumn has come, the wagtails have arrived, as good deeds shine out when their time comes. ॥3॥
kishkindha.16.cau4: With neither mud nor dust, the earth looks as fine as the deeds of a king skilled in statecraft.
The fish are in distress as the water shrinks, like a foolish householder left without money. ॥4॥
kishkindha.16.cau5: The cloudless sky shines clear, like a devotee of Hari who has given up every hope.
Here and there falls a light autumn shower, as only a rare one gains devotion to me. ॥5॥
kishkindha.16.do16: Kings, ascetics, merchants and beggars have gladly left the cities and set out,
as people in all four stages of life lay down their toil once they gain devotion to Hari. ॥16॥
kishkindha.17.cau1: The fish in deep water are happy, as one who has taken refuge in Śrī Hari meets not a single obstacle.
With its lotuses in bloom the lake is as lovely as the attributeless Brahman when it takes on attributes. ॥1॥
kishkindha.17.cau2: The humming of the bees is wonderful to hear, and the birds raise lovely calls of many kinds.
The cakravāka is pained at heart to see the night fall, as a wicked man is pained to see another's wealth. ॥2॥
kishkindha.17.cau3: The cātaka keeps crying out, so great is its thirst, as one hostile to Śiva never finds happiness.
At night the moon takes away the heat of the autumn sun, as the sight of a saint drives sins away. ॥3॥
kishkindha.17.cau4: Flocks of cakoras gaze at the moon as devotees of Hari gaze on Hari when they have found him.
Mosquitoes and gadflies have died out for fear of the cold, as a family dies out when it turns against Brahmins. ॥4॥
kishkindha.17.do17: The creatures that had crowded the earth have gone now that autumn has come,
as hosts of doubts and delusions go when one meets a true guru. ॥17॥
kishkindha.18.cau1: Dear brother, the rains have passed and the clear season is here, yet no word of Sītā has reached us.
If once I can somehow learn where she is, I will conquer even Death and bring her back in the blink of an eye. ॥1॥
kishkindha.18.cau2: If she lives, dear brother, then wherever she is, I will make every effort and bring her home.
Even Sugrīva has let me slip from his mind: he has won a kingdom, a treasury, a city and a wife. ॥2॥
kishkindha.18.cau3: With the arrow that killed Vāli I will kill that fool tomorrow.
Umā, can he by whose grace pride and delusion fall away be angry even in a dream? ॥3॥
kishkindha.18.cau4: This play is understood only by wise sages who have given their love to the feet of Śrī Rāma.
Perceiving the Lord's anger, Lakṣmaṇa strung his bow and gripped arrows in his hand. ॥4॥
kishkindha.18.do18: Then Śrī Rāma, in whom compassion knows no bounds, counselled his younger brother:
Dear brother, only frighten my friend Sugrīva and bring him here. ॥18॥
kishkindha.19.cau1: Here Hanumān, son of the Wind, reflected that Sugrīva had forgotten Śrī Rāma's work.
He went to him, bowed his head at his feet, and reasoned with him in all four ways: conciliation, gifts, threat and division. ॥1॥
kishkindha.19.cau2: Hearing this, Sugrīva was seized with fear and said: The objects of the senses have stolen my wits.
Now, son of the Wind, send bands of messengers to wherever the troops of monkeys are, ॥2॥
kishkindha.19.cau3: and tell them that whoever does not come within a fortnight will die at my hands.
Then Hanumān summoned the messengers and showed them all great honour. ॥3॥
kishkindha.19.cau4: He set before them fear, affection and right counsel, and they all bowed at his feet and set off.
Just then Lakṣmaṇa came into the city; seeing his anger, the monkeys fled this way and that. ॥4॥
kishkindha.19.do19: Then, bow strung, he declared: I will reduce this city to ashes.
Seeing the city in distress, Vāli's son Aṅgada came forward. ॥19॥
kishkindha.20.cau1: Aṅgada bowed his head at his feet and pleaded, and Lakṣmaṇa held out his arm to him in assurance that he need not fear.
When the king of the monkeys heard with his own ears that Lakṣmaṇa was angry, he was overcome with fear and said: ॥1॥
kishkindha.20.cau2: Listen, Hanumān: go with Tārā, plead with the prince and bring him round.
Hanumān went with Tārā, bowed at Lakṣmaṇa's feet, and spoke of the Lord's fair fame. ॥2॥
kishkindha.20.cau3: Pleading with him, they led him into the palace, bathed his feet and gave him a seat on the couch.
Then Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, laid his head at his feet; Lakṣmaṇa clasped his arm and drew him to his breast. ॥3॥
kishkindha.20.cau4: Sugrīva said: My lord, nothing intoxicates like the objects of the senses; in a moment they cloud even the minds of sages.
Lakṣmaṇa was pleased to hear these humble words and counselled him in many ways. ॥4॥
kishkindha.20.cau5: Hanumān, son of the Wind, told the whole story of how the bands of messengers had gone out. ॥5॥
kishkindha.20.do20: Then Sugrīva set out joyfully, with Aṅgada and the other monkeys,
and with Śrī Rāma's younger brother leading the way they came to where Śrī Rāma was. ॥20॥
kishkindha.21.cau1: Sugrīva bowed his head at the Lord's feet and with joined palms said: My Lord, the fault is not mine at all.
Your māyā is overwhelmingly strong, O Lord; one is set free from it only if you show mercy, Rāma. ॥1॥
kishkindha.21.cau2: My Lord, gods, men and sages are all in the power of the senses, and I am a base beast, a monkey full of lust.
One whom the arrow of a woman's eyes has not struck, who has stayed awake through the dark night of fierce anger, ॥2॥
kishkindha.21.cau3: and who has never let the noose of greed close round his neck, is your equal, O Lord of the Raghus.
This virtue does not come by any practice; only a rare few gain it, by your grace. ॥3॥
kishkindha.21.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma smiled and said: You are as dear to me as my brother Bharata.
Now set your heart on the means by which news of Sītā may be had. ॥4॥
kishkindha.21.do21: While they were talking in this way, the troops of monkeys arrived.
Hosts of monkeys of many colours could be seen in every direction. ॥21॥
kishkindha.22.cau1: Umā, I saw that monkey army; anyone who would try to count it is a fool.
They come and bow their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet, and every one of them is blessed by gazing on his face. ॥1॥
kishkindha.22.cau2: There was not one monkey in the army whose welfare Śrī Rāma did not ask after.
This is nothing great for the Lord: Śrī Rāma has the universe for his form and pervades all. ॥2॥
kishkindha.22.cau3: At his command they took their places here and there, and Sugrīva instructed them all, saying:
This is Śrī Rāma's work and my request: go, you troops of monkeys, in every direction. ॥3॥
kishkindha.22.cau4: Go and search for Janaka's daughter, and come back within a month, brothers.
Whoever lets the time run out and returns without news will end up being put to death by me. ॥4॥
kishkindha.22.do22: As soon as they heard his words, all the monkeys set off at once in every direction.
Then Sugrīva called Aṅgada, Nala and Hanumān. ॥22॥
kishkindha.23.cau1: Sugrīva said: Listen, Nīla, Aṅgada, Hanumān, and wise Jāmbavān of steady mind:
all of you, fine warriors, go south together and ask everyone for news of Sītā. ॥1॥
kishkindha.23.cau2: In thought, deed and word, think out the means by which Śrī Rāma's work may be accomplished.
One should take the sun on one's back and a fire on one's breast, but serve one's master with one's whole being, free of deceit. ॥2॥
kishkindha.23.cau3: Leaving māyā aside, one should look to the world beyond; then every sorrow born of worldly existence is wiped away.
Brothers, this is the fruit of having a body: to give up every desire and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
kishkindha.23.cau4: He alone knows true worth, he alone is fortunate, who loves the feet of Śrī Rāma.
Asking leave and bowing their heads at his feet, they set off joyfully, remembering Śrī Rāma. ॥4॥
kishkindha.23.cau5: Last of all Hanumān, son of the Wind, bowed his head, and the Lord, knowing the work would be done by him, called him close.
Laying his lotus hand on Hanumān's head, he gave him his signet ring, for he knew him as his own. ॥5॥
kishkindha.23.cau6: The Lord said: Comfort Sītā in every way, tell her of my strength and my longing, and come back quickly.
Hanumān counted his birth fulfilled and set off holding the treasury of mercy in his heart. ॥6॥
kishkindha.23.cau7: Though the Lord, protector of the gods, knows everything, he keeps to the ways of statecraft. ॥7॥
kishkindha.23.do23: They all went on, searching forests, rivers, lakes, mountains and caves,
their minds wholly absorbed in Śrī Rāma's work, forgetting all care for their own bodies. ॥23॥
kishkindha.24.cau1: Any demon they ran into anywhere lost his life to a single slap.
They searched the mountains and forests in many ways, and if they met a sage, they all crowded round him. ॥1॥
kishkindha.24.cau2: Thirst came upon them and they grew desperate; there was no water anywhere, and the thick forest left them lost.
Hanumān judged in his mind that without water to drink they would all soon die. ॥2॥
kishkindha.24.cau3: Climbing a mountain peak, he looked all around and saw a marvel at a cave in the ground:
cakravākas, herons and swans were flying up, and many birds were going inside. ॥3॥
kishkindha.24.cau4: Hanumān, son of the Wind, climbed down and led the whole band to the cave to show it to them.
Putting Hanumān in front, they went into the cave without delay. ॥4॥
kishkindha.24.do24: Once inside, they came upon a splendid garden and a lake bright with many open lotuses.
A lovely abode was there, where a woman was seated, a very mass of austerity. ॥24॥
kishkindha.25.cau1: Keeping their distance, they bowed their heads to her; she questioned them, and they told her all that had befallen them.
Then she said: Drink water, and eat the many kinds of fine, juicy fruit. ॥1॥
kishkindha.25.cau2: They bathed and ate the sweet fruit, then all came back to her.
She told them her whole story and said: Now I shall go to where Śrī Rāma is. ॥2॥
kishkindha.25.cau3: Close your eyes and leave the cave; you will find Sītā, so do not despair.
The heroes closed their eyes, and when they looked again they were all standing on the shore of the ocean. ॥3॥
kishkindha.25.cau4: She then went to where Śrī Rāma was, and bowed her head at his lotus feet.
Many were the prayers she offered, and the Lord blessed her with unfailing devotion. ॥4॥
kishkindha.25.do25: Taking the Lord's command upon her head, she went to the forest of Badarī,
holding in her heart the two feet of Śrī Rāma to which Brahmā and Śiva bow. ॥25॥
kishkindha.26.cau1: Here the monkeys were thinking to themselves that the time allowed was over and nothing had been done.
Gathering together, they said to one another: Brothers, what are we to do without news? ॥1॥
kishkindha.26.cau2: Aṅgada said, his eyes brimming with tears: Either way, death is upon us.
No news of Sītā has been found here, and back there the king of the monkeys will put us to death. ॥2॥
