Bharata said: Tell me, Hanumān, does my compassionate master ever remember me as his servant? ॥8॥
uttar.2.cha1: Has the jewel of the Raghu line ever remembered me as his own servant?
Hearing Bharata's most humble words, Hanumān, his body thrilling, fell at his feet.
One whose many virtues Śrī Rāma, lord of all that moves and all that is still, tells of with his own lips,
how could he not be humble, supremely pure, an ocean of good qualities? ॥1॥
uttar.2.do2क: Hanumān said: My lord, you are as dear to Śrī Rāma as his own life; what I say is true, dear one.
Hearing this, Bharata embraced him again and again, his heart unable to contain its joy. ॥2 (क)॥
uttar.2.so2ख: Hanumān bowed his head at Bharata's feet and hurried straight back to Śrī Rāma.
Reaching him, he gave the news that all were well; then the Lord, glad at heart, mounted the aerial car and set off. ॥2 (ख)॥
uttar.3.cau1: Bharata came joyfully back to the city of Kosala and gave his guru all the news.
Then he made it known in the palace that Śrī Rāma was coming to the city safe and well. ॥1॥
uttar.3.cau2: Hearing it, all the mothers rose and ran; Bharata told them the Lord was well and reassured them.
When the townspeople had the news, all of them, men and women, ran out in joy. ॥2॥
uttar.3.cau3: Curds, dūrvā grass, gorocana, fruit, flowers and fresh tulasī leaves, the root of all blessing:
heaping these on golden platters, women moving with an elephant's graceful gait went out singing. ॥3॥
uttar.3.cau4: Everyone runs out just as they are, not stopping to bring children or the old along.
They ask one another: Brother, have you seen Śrī Rāma, the compassionate? ॥4॥
uttar.3.cau5: Ayodhyā, knowing the Lord was on his way, became a treasure-house of every kind of beauty.
A pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant, and the Sarayū's water grew perfectly clear. ॥5॥
uttar.3.do3क: Joyful, with the guru, the family, his younger brother and a throng of Brahmins,
Bharata, his heart full of love, went out to meet Śrī Rāma, the abode of grace. ॥3 (क)॥
uttar.3.do3ख: Many women climbed to the upper rooms and gazed at the aerial car in the sky.
Seeing it, they sang auspicious songs in sweet voices, full of joy. ॥3 (ख)॥
uttar.3.do3ग: Ayodhyā was an ocean that rejoiced at the sight of its full moon, Śrī Rāma;
it swelled with a roar of voices, and the women seemed its waves. ॥3 (ग)॥
uttar.4.cau1: Here Śrī Rāma, the sun to the lotus of the solar race, was showing the monkeys the lovely city.
He said: Listen, Sugrīva, Aṅgada and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā. This city is holy and this land is beautiful. ॥1॥
uttar.4.cau2: Though all have praised Vaikuṇṭha, which the Vedas and Purāṇas make known and the world knows of,
even it is not as dear to me as Ayodhyā; only a rare few understand this. ॥2॥
uttar.4.cau3: This lovely city is where I was born; the holy Sarayū flows along its northern side,
and whoever bathes in it comes, with no labour at all, to live close to me. ॥3॥
uttar.4.cau4: The people who live here are very dear to me; this city is a store of happiness and bestows my own abode.
All the monkeys rejoiced to hear the Lord's words: blessed is Ayodhyā, which Śrī Rāma has praised. ॥4॥
uttar.4.do4क: The Lord, the ocean of mercy, saw all the people coming,
and he directed the aerial car; it came down to the ground near the city. ॥4 (क)॥
uttar.4.do4ख: When he had alighted, the Lord said to Puṣpaka: Go to Kubera.
At Śrī Rāma's bidding it set off, glad, yet sorely grieved to be parted from him. ॥4 (ख)॥
uttar.5.cau1: All the people came with Bharata, their bodies worn thin by separation from Śrī Rāma.
The Lord saw Vāmadeva and Vasiṣṭha, chief among sages, and laying his bow and arrows on the ground, ॥1॥
uttar.5.cau2: he ran to his guru and caught hold of his lotus feet; he and his younger brother thrilled from head to foot.
The king of sages embraced him and asked if all was well. The Lord said: We are well by your mercy alone. ॥2॥
uttar.5.cau3: Śrī Rāma, lord of Raghu's line and upholder of dharma, greeted all the Brahmins with a bow of the head.
Next Bharata took hold of those lotus feet of the Lord before which gods, sages, Śiva and Brahmā bow. ॥3॥
uttar.5.cau4: He lay on the ground and would not rise when they tried to lift him; then the ocean of mercy raised him by force and held him to his heart.
The hair on the Lord's dark body stood on end, and his eyes, like fresh lotuses, brimmed with tears. ॥4॥
uttar.5.cha1: Tears flow from his lotus eyes, and the hair on his lovely body stands on end.
With deep love the Lord, master of the three worlds, held his younger brother to his heart.
How the Lord looks as he meets his brother, I cannot find a likeness to tell.
It is as if love and śṛṅgāra, the spirit of beauty, had taken bodies and met, and gained a matchless loveliness. ॥1॥
uttar.5.cha2: The treasury of mercy asks Bharata how he is, but words do not come quickly to him.
Listen, Śivā: that joy lies beyond words and mind; only one who finds it knows it.
Bharata said: All is well now, Lord of Kosala; knowing your servant to be in distress, you have given him the sight of you.
As I was drowning in the ocean of separation, the treasury of compassion took me by the hand. ॥2॥
uttar.5.do5: Then the Lord joyfully embraced Śatrughna, holding him to his heart.
Then Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, the two brothers, met in the deepest love. ॥5॥
uttar.6.cau1: Then Lakṣmaṇa embraced Bharata's younger brother, ending the unbearable grief that separation had brought.
Bharata bowed his head at Sītā's feet and, with his younger brother, found the highest joy. ॥1॥
uttar.6.cau2: The townspeople rejoiced to see the Lord; all the hardship born of separation vanished.
Seeing everyone restless with love, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, worked a wonder. ॥2॥
uttar.6.cau3: At that moment the compassionate Lord appeared in countless forms and met each person as was fitting.
Śrī Rāma looked on them with grace and freed every man and woman from sorrow. ॥3॥
uttar.6.cau4: In an instant the Lord met everyone; Umā, no one knew this secret.
Having thus made all happy, Śrī Rāma, the home of goodness and virtue, went on ahead. ॥4॥
uttar.6.cau5: Kausalyā and all the mothers ran, like newly calved cows that catch sight of their calves. ॥5॥
uttar.6.cha1: It was as if cows had left their young calves at home and gone, against their will, to graze in the forest,
and at the end of the day ran lowing towards the town, milk dripping from their udders.
With deep love the Lord met all the mothers and spoke gentle words to them in many ways.
The harsh hardship born of separation was gone, and they found joy and happiness beyond count. ॥1॥
uttar.6.do6क: Sumitrā embraced her son, knowing his love for Śrī Rāma's feet.
Meeting Śrī Rāma, Kaikeyī felt deeply abashed at heart. ॥6 (क)॥
uttar.6.do6ख: Lakṣmaṇa met all the mothers and rejoiced to receive their blessings.
He met Kaikeyī again and again, yet the unrest in his mind would not go. ॥6 (ख)॥
uttar.7.cau1: Sītā met all her mothers-in-law, and touching their feet she was filled with joy.
Asking after her welfare, they bless her: May your married happiness stay unshaken. ॥1॥
uttar.7.cau2: They all gaze on Śrī Rāma's lotus face and, knowing the hour to be auspicious, hold back the tears in their eyes.
They wave the lamps on golden platters and look again and again at the Lord's form. ॥2॥
uttar.7.cau3: They make offerings over him in many ways, and their hearts fill with supreme bliss and joy.
Again and again Kausalyā looks at Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, steadfast in battle. ॥3॥
uttar.7.cau4: She wonders in her heart again and again: How did he kill the lord of Laṅkā?
My two boys are so tender, and the demons were great warriors of immense strength. ॥4॥
uttar.7.do7: The mother gazes at the Lord with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā;
her heart is immersed in supreme bliss, and again and again her body thrills. ॥7॥
uttar.8.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Nala, Nīla, Jāmbavān and the noble Aṅgada,
Hanumān and all the other monkey heroes had taken on charming human forms. ॥1॥
uttar.8.cau2: Bharata's affection, his goodness, his vows and his discipline: all of them tell of these with reverence and deep love.
Seeing the ways of the townsfolk, they all praise their love for the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
uttar.8.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma called all his friends and taught them all: Bow at the sage's feet.
This is Guru Vasiṣṭha, revered by our family; by his grace the demons were slain in battle. ॥3॥
uttar.8.cau4: Listen, sage: these are all my friends; in the ocean of battle they became my rafts.
For my good they put their lives at stake; I hold them dearer even than Bharata. ॥4॥
uttar.8.cau5: Hearing the Lord's words they were all overwhelmed; with every moment fresh joys rose in them. ॥5॥
uttar.8.do8क: Next they bent their heads at Kausalyā's feet.
She blessed them with joy: You are as dear to me as Rāma. ॥8 (क)॥
uttar.8.do8ख: Flowers rained down till the sky was thick with them, and Śrī Rāma, the source of joy, went on towards the palace.
Crowds of the city's women and men climbed to the balconies to watch him. ॥8 (ख)॥
uttar.9.cau1: Everyone adorned golden pitchers in wonderful ways and set them, decked, at their own doors.
For good fortune all put up festoons, banners and flags. ॥1॥
uttar.9.cau2: All the lanes were sprinkled with fragrance, and many auspicious squares were drawn with elephant-pearls.
Auspicious things of every kind were arranged, and in joy many kettledrums sounded through the city. ॥2॥
uttar.9.cau3: Everywhere women make offerings over him and, hearts brimming with joy, give their blessings.
Young women arrange many lamps on golden platters and sing auspicious songs. ॥3॥
uttar.9.cau4: They wave the lamps before the remover of distress, the sun to the lotus-forest of the Raghu line.
The Vedas, Śeṣa and Sarasvatī have described the beauty, wealth and well-being of the city; ॥4॥
uttar.9.cau5: yet even they are left spellbound at the sight of this; then how, Umā, can mortals tell of his virtues? ॥5॥
uttar.9.do9क: The women were night-lotuses in the lake of Ayodhyā, and separation from Śrī Rāma was the sun;
now that it has set, they have blossomed at the sight of the moon that is Śrī Rāma. ॥9 (क)॥
uttar.9.do9ख: Good omens of many kinds appear, and drums sound in the sky.
Having given the men and women of the city their lord again, the Lord went on to the palace. ॥9 (ख)॥
uttar.10.cau1: Knowing that Kaikeyī was ashamed, Pārvatī, the Lord went first to her house.
He comforted her and gave her great happiness, and then Śrī Hari went to his own palace. ॥1॥
uttar.10.cau2: When the ocean of mercy entered the palace, all the men and women of the city were happy.
Guru Vasiṣṭha sent for the Brahmins and said: Today the hour is good, the day is good, everything has come together. ॥2॥
uttar.10.cau3: All you Brahmins, gladly give your command that Śrī Rāma take his seat on the throne.
The sage Vasiṣṭha's pleasing words delighted all the Brahmins as soon as they heard them. ॥3॥
uttar.10.cau4: Many Brahmins said in gentle words: Śrī Rāma's coronation gladdens the whole world.
Now, best of sages, make no delay; place the mark of kingship on the Mahārāja's brow. ॥4॥
uttar.10.do10क: Then the sage spoke to Sumantra, who set off gladly as soon as he heard,
and going at once he had many chariots, horses and elephants made ready. ॥10 (क)॥
uttar.10.do10ख: Then, sending runners here and there, he had auspicious things brought,
and coming back he joyfully bowed his head at Vasiṣṭha's feet. ॥10 (ख)॥
uttar.11.cau1: The city of Ayodhyā was decked most beautifully, and the gods let fall a steady shower of flowers.
Śrī Rāma sent for his servants and told them: First go and bathe my friends. ॥1॥
uttar.11.cau2: At these words people ran here and there and at once bathed Sugrīva and the rest.
Then Śrī Rāma, treasury of compassion, called Bharata and with his own hands untangled his matted hair. ॥2॥
uttar.11.cau3: The Lord, the gracious Śrī Rāma who loves his devotees, bathed all three brothers.
Bharata's good fortune and the Lord's tenderness could not be sung by a thousand million Śeṣas. ॥3॥
uttar.11.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma untangled his own matted locks and, asking the Guru's leave, bathed.
After bathing the Lord put on his ornaments; seeing his limbs, a hundred Kāmadevas felt ashamed. ॥4॥
uttar.11.do11क: With honour the mothers-in-law quickly bathed Sītā,
and dressed every limb with care in heavenly garments and fine ornaments. ॥11 (क)॥
uttar.11.do11ख: On Śrī Rāma's left shines Ramā (Sītā), a mine of beauty and virtue.
Seeing it, all the mothers rejoiced, counting their lives fulfilled. ॥11 (ख)॥
uttar.11.do11ग: Listen, Garuḍa: at that time Brahmā, Śiva, hosts of sages
and all the gods came mounted on their aerial chariots to see the source of joy. ॥11 (ग)॥
uttar.12.cau1: Seeing the Lord, the sage's heart filled with love, and at once he called for a heavenly throne.
Its radiance, like the sun's, was beyond words; Śrī Rāma bowed to the Brahmins and sat upon it. ॥1॥
uttar.12.cau2: Seeing Śrī Rāma with Sītā, daughter of Janaka, the whole company of sages rejoiced greatly.
Then the Brahmins chanted Vedic mantras, and in the sky gods and sages cried out: Victory, victory! ॥2॥
uttar.12.cau3: First the sage Vasiṣṭha applied the tilaka, then he gave leave to all the Brahmins.
The mothers rejoiced to see their son and waved the lamps before him again and again. ॥3॥
uttar.12.cau4: The Brahmins received gifts of many kinds, and every beggar was made one who need never beg.
Seeing the master of the three worlds on the throne, the gods beat their drums. ॥4॥
uttar.12.cha1: Countless drums sound in the sky; gandharvas and kinnaras sing.
Troupes of apsarās dance, and gods and sages find supreme bliss.
Bharata and the other younger brothers, with Vibhīṣaṇa, Aṅgada, Hanumān and the rest,
stand resplendent, holding the parasol, the whisk, the fan, the bow, the sword, the shield and the spear. ॥1॥
uttar.12.cha2: With Sītā beside him, the jewel of the solar line shines with the beauty of many Kāmadevas.
The yellow garment on his beautiful body, dark as a fresh rain-cloud, enchants the minds of the gods.
Crown, armlets and other wonderful ornaments adorn every limb.
His eyes are lotuses, his chest and arms are mighty; blessed are those who behold him. ॥2॥
uttar.12.do12क: Garuḍa, that splendour, that assembly and that joy cannot be told.
Sarasvatī, Śeṣa and the Vedas describe it, and its savour is known to Maheśa. ॥12 (क)॥
uttar.12.do12ख: Each offering his own praise, the gods went back to their own realms.
Then the Vedas, in the guise of bards, came to where Śrī Rāma was. ॥12 (ख)॥
uttar.12.do12ग: The all-knowing Lord, the treasury of mercy, received them with great honour.
No one grasped the secret at all, and they began to sing his praises. ॥12 (ग)॥
uttar.13.cha1: Glory to you, who are with form and beyond form, of form beyond compare, crest-jewel of kings.
By the strength of your arms you slew Rāvaṇa and the other fierce, mighty and wicked demons.
Taking birth as a man, you broke the burden of the world and burned away its cruel sorrows.
Glory to you, compassionate Lord, protector of those who bow to you; we bow to you together with your Śakti, Sītā. ॥1॥
uttar.13.cha2: O Hari, gods and demons, nāgas and men, all that moves and does not move, under the sway of your hard māyā (the Lord's power of illusion),
wander for countless days and nights on the road of worldly existence, filled with time, karma and the guṇas.
Those on whom you have looked with compassion, my Lord, are freed from the threefold suffering.
O Rāma, skilled in cutting away the weariness of worldly existence, protect us; we bow to you. ॥2॥
uttar.13.cha3: Those who, drunk with pride of knowledge, did not honour devotion to you, which ends worldly existence,
we see, O Hari, win a state hard even for the gods to reach, and fall from it.
Those who trust you, give up every other hope, and remain your servants
cross the ocean of worldly existence without toil by repeating your name; it is you, our Lord, whom we remember. ॥3॥
uttar.13.cha4: The feet that Śiva and Brahmā worship, whose holy dust, once it touched her, set free the sage's wife,
from whose nails came the Gaṅgā, river of the gods, revered by sages, purifier of the three worlds,
which bear the banner, the thunderbolt, the goad and the lotus, and grew calluses from thorns as they walked the forest:
those two lotus feet, O Mukunda, O Rāma, O lord of Ramā, we ever worship. ॥4॥
uttar.13.cha5: The Vedas and scriptures tell of a beginningless tree whose root is the Unmanifest, with four barks,
six trunks, twenty-five branches, countless leaves and thick flowers,
two kinds of fruit, bitter and sweet, and a single creeper that lives clinging to it,
ever putting out fresh shoots and flowers: to that tree of worldly existence we bow. ॥5॥
uttar.13.cha6: Some meditate on Brahman as unborn, non-dual, known by experience alone, beyond the mind:
let them speak of it and know it so; we, my Lord, ever sing the glory of your form with attributes.
Lord, home of compassion, mine of virtues, O God, this is the boon we ask:
that, casting off the faults of mind, speech and action, we may love your feet. ॥6॥
uttar.13.do13क: While all looked on, the Vedas made this noble prayer;
then they vanished and went to the abode of Brahmā. ॥13 (क)॥
uttar.13.do13ख: Listen, Garuḍa: then Śiva came to where Śrī Rāma was,
and made his prayer with a voice choked with feeling, his whole body thrilling. ॥13 (ख)॥
uttar.14.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, beloved of Ramā, who brings peace; save your servant, troubled by fear of the fever of worldly existence.
Lord of Avadh, lord of the gods, lord of Ramā, all-pervading one: I have come for refuge and I ask you, Lord, save me. ॥1॥
uttar.14.cau2: Destroyer of the ten-headed, twenty-armed one, you have taken away the earth's great and grievous ills.
The hosts of demons were moths, burned up in the fierce blaze of the fire of your arrows. ॥2॥
uttar.14.cau3: Lovelier than all, the ornament of the earth's circle, you bear the noble arrows, bow and quiver.
To the dense darkness of the great night of pride, delusion and possessiveness, you are the host of the sun's rays. ॥3॥
uttar.14.cau4: Kāma, the hunter, has struck down the deer that are people, piercing their hearts with the arrows of base pleasures.
Slay him, my Lord, O Hari, and save these helpless ones, wretches who have strayed and fallen in the forest of the senses. ॥4॥
uttar.14.cau5: People are struck down by many diseases and partings; these are the fruits of disregarding your feet.
Those men lie in the fathomless ocean of worldly existence who have no love for your lotus feet. ॥5॥
uttar.14.cau6: Ever most wretched, sullied and sorrowful are those who have no love for your lotus feet.
Those whose support is your story ever hold dear the saints and the infinite Lord. ॥6॥
uttar.14.cau7: They have no attachment, no greed, no pride, no arrogance; wealth and misfortune are the same to them.
This is why sages gladly become your servants, and give up for ever their trust in yoga. ॥7॥
uttar.14.cau8: With love they keep their vows unbroken and serve your lotus feet with a pure heart.
Holding scorn and honour alike, all such saints wander the earth in happiness. ॥8॥
uttar.14.cau9: Bee at the lotus of the sages' hearts, O hero of the Raghus, greatly steadfast in battle, unconquered: I worship you.
O Hari, I chant your name and bow to you, the great cure for the disease of worldly existence, the enemy of pride. ॥9॥
uttar.14.cau10: Supreme home of virtue, goodness and grace, lord of Śrī, I bow to you without ceasing.
Joy of the Raghus, root out the mass of opposites; protector of the earth, look upon this humble one. ॥10॥
uttar.14.do14क: Again and again I ask this boon; grant it gladly, lord of Śrī:
unfailing devotion to your lotus feet, and the company of the good for ever. ॥14 (क)॥
uttar.14.do14ख: Having told of Śrī Rāma's virtues, Śiva, Umā's lord, went joyfully to Kailāsa.
Then the Lord had the monkeys given lodgings comfortable in every way. ॥14 (ख)॥
uttar.15.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: this story is purifying; it destroys the threefold affliction and the fear of worldly existence.
On hearing of the great king's auspicious coronation, people gain dispassion and discernment. ॥1॥
uttar.15.cau2: Those who hear it or sing it with desires in their hearts win happiness and wealth of many kinds.
After enjoying in the world joys rare even for the gods, at the hour of death they go to the city of Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.15.cau3: The liberated, the dispassionate and the worldly who hear it gain devotion, the supreme state and ever new wealth.
Garuḍa, I have told the story of Śrī Rāma as far as my own understanding could range; it takes away fear and sorrow. ॥3॥
uttar.15.cau4: It makes dispassion, discernment and devotion firm, and is a fine boat for crossing the river of delusion.
In the city of Kosala there was fresh rejoicing every day, and people of every community were happy. ॥4॥
uttar.15.cau5: Everyone's love for Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, to which Śiva, the sages and Brahmā bow, grew new each day.
Those who came asking were clothed in garments of many kinds, and the Brahmins received gifts of every sort. ॥5॥
uttar.15.do15: All the monkeys were immersed in the bliss of Brahman, and every heart held love for the Lord's feet.
They never noticed the days going by, and six months passed. ॥15॥
uttar.16.cau1: They forgot their homes and did not think of them even in dreams, just as ill will towards others never enters a saint's mind.
Then Śrī Rāma called all his friends; they all came and bowed their heads with respect. ॥1॥
uttar.16.cau2: With the greatest love he seated them close to him and spoke gentle words that gladden devotees:
You have served me greatly. In what words can I praise you to your face? ॥2॥
uttar.16.cau3: That is why you have become so dear to me: for my sake you gave up your homes and their comforts.
My younger brothers, the kingdom, wealth, Sītā, my body, my home, family and loved ones: ॥3॥
uttar.16.cau4: all are dear to me, but none as dear as you. I do not speak falsely; this is my way.
Everyone holds his servant dear, as is the rule; but my love for those who serve me is greater still. ॥4॥
uttar.16.do16: Now go home, all of you, my friends, and worship me with steadfast discipline.
Knowing me as ever present in all and the well-wisher of all, keep loving me dearly. ॥16॥
uttar.17.cau1: Hearing the Lord's words they were all overwhelmed; forgetting who they were and where, they lost all sense of their bodies.
They stood before him with joined palms, gazing without a blink, too full of love to say anything. ॥1॥
uttar.17.cau2: The Lord saw their supreme love and taught them special knowledge in many ways.
Before the Lord they could say nothing, and gazed again and again at his lotus feet. ॥2॥
uttar.17.cau3: Then the Lord sent for ornaments and garments of many colours, matchless and lovely.
Sugrīva was dressed first, Bharata having arranged the garments with his own hands. ॥3॥
uttar.17.cau4: At the Lord's bidding Lakṣmaṇa dressed Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, who is dear to Śrī Rāma's heart.
Aṅgada stayed seated and did not stir; seeing his love, the Lord did not call him. ॥4॥
uttar.17.do17क: Śrī Rāma dressed Jāmbavān, Nīla and all the others.
Holding Śrī Rāma's form in their hearts and bowing their heads at his feet, they all set off. ॥17 (क)॥
uttar.17.do17ख: Then Aṅgada rose and bowed his head, and with tears in his eyes and palms joined
spoke most humbly, in words that seemed steeped in the nectar of love: ॥17 (ख)॥
uttar.18.cau1: Listen, all-knowing one, ocean of grace and joy, merciful to the lowly, friend of the distressed.
My Lord, when Vāli was dying he left me in your very lap. ॥1॥
uttar.18.cau2: Keep to your proud name as the refuge of those without refuge, and do not forsake me, friend of your devotees.
To me you are master, teacher, father and mother; where could I go, leaving your lotus feet? ॥2॥
uttar.18.cau3: Consider it yourself and tell me, O king of men: leaving my Lord, what business have I at home?
I am a child, without knowledge, sense or strength; keep this humble servant in your refuge, my Lord. ॥3॥
uttar.18.cau4: I will do every lowly task of the household, and by gazing on your lotus feet I shall cross the ocean of worldly existence.
With these words he fell at the Lord's feet and said: Protect me. Do not tell me now to go home, my Lord. ॥4॥
uttar.18.do18क: Śrī Rāma, the very bound of compassion, heard Aṅgada's humble words.
The Lord raised him and clasped him to his heart, his lotus eyes filled with tears. ॥18 (क)॥
uttar.18.do18ख: The Lord put the garland from his own breast, robes and jewels on Vāli's son,
and then, after counselling him in many ways, gave him leave to go. ॥18 (ख)॥
uttar.19.cau1: Mindful of what the devotees had done, Bharata went with his younger brother Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa to see them off.
No small love filled Aṅgada's heart; again and again he turned to look towards Śrī Rāma, ॥1॥
uttar.19.cau2: and again and again he prostrated himself, hoping in his heart that Śrī Rāma would tell him to stay.
Remembering over and over how Śrī Rāma looked, spoke, walked and met him with a smile, he grieved. ॥2॥
uttar.19.cau3: Seeing the Lord's wish, he made many humble entreaties and went on his way, holding the lotus feet in his heart.
Bharata escorted all the monkeys with great honour, and then returned with his brothers. ॥3॥
uttar.19.cau4: Then Hanumān clasped Sugrīva's feet and pleaded with him in many ways:
Let me serve at Śrī Rāma's feet for ten days, my lord, and then I shall come and see your feet again. ॥4॥
uttar.19.cau5: Sugrīva said: Son of the Wind, you are a store of merit; go and serve the Lord, the home of grace.
With these words all the monkeys left at once. Aṅgada said: Listen, Hanumān: ॥5॥
uttar.19.do19क: Give the Lord my prostrations; I ask you this with joined palms.
And keep reminding Śrī Rāma of me, again and again. ॥19 (क)॥
uttar.19.do19ख: With these words Vāli's son went on his way, and Hanumān came back.
He told the Lord of Aṅgada's love, and the Lord was overcome with it. ॥19 (ख)॥
uttar.19.do19ग: Harder than the thunderbolt and gentler far than a flower:
such is Śrī Rāma's heart, Garuḍa. Tell me, who can understand it? ॥19 (ग)॥
uttar.20.cau1: Then the compassionate Lord sent for the Niṣāda chief, bestowed ornaments and garments on him as a blessing, and said:
Go home, keep me in remembrance, and follow dharma in thought, deed and word. ॥1॥
uttar.20.cau2: You are my friend, and a brother to me like Bharata; keep coming to the city always.
On hearing this he was filled with great joy, and fell at the Lord's feet with tears in his eyes. ॥2॥
uttar.20.cau3: Holding the Lord's lotus feet in his heart he went home, and told his family of the Lord's nature.
Seeing Śrī Rāma's ways, the citizens said again and again: Blessed is the Lord, the treasure of joy. ॥3॥
uttar.20.cau4: When Śrī Rāma took his seat on the throne, the three worlds rejoiced and all their sorrows left them.
Nobody held a grudge against another; through Śrī Rāma's power all strife was gone. ॥4॥
uttar.20.do20: The people were each devoted to the dharma of their own class (varṇa) and stage of life (āśrama).
They always walked the path of the Veda and lived in happiness, with no fear, no grief and no disease. ॥20॥
uttar.21.cau1: In Śrī Rāma's kingdom no one was touched by the afflictions that come from the body, from the gods or from other creatures.
Everyone loved one another, and each walked devoted to his own dharma as the Veda directs. ॥1॥
uttar.21.cau2: Dharma stood on all its four feet throughout the world; there was no sin, not even in dreams.
Every man and woman was given to devotion to Śrī Rāma, and all were fit for the supreme state. ॥2॥
uttar.21.cau3: There was no untimely death and no pain of any kind; all were handsome, and all were sound and free of disease in body.
No one was poor, unhappy or wretched; no one was ignorant or without auspicious marks. ॥3॥
uttar.21.cau4: All were free of hypocrisy, given to dharma and virtuous; men and women alike were skilful and accomplished.
All knew the worth of merit, all were learned and wise, all were grateful, and none was clever in deceit. ॥4॥
uttar.21.do21: Listen, Garuḍa: in Śrī Rāma's kingdom, throughout the world of moving and unmoving beings,
no one suffered sorrow caused by time, karma, nature or the guṇas. ॥21॥
uttar.22.cau1: Śrī Rāma of Kosala was the one king of the earth, girdled by the seven seas.
Yet for him in each of whose hairs lie many worlds, this lordship was no great thing. ॥1॥
uttar.22.cau2: Once that greatness of the Lord is understood, to describe this is to belittle him greatly.
Yet, Garuḍa, the very ones who know that greatness find their joy in this story once more. ॥2॥
uttar.22.cau3: Great sages of subdued senses declare that this play is the very fruit of knowing that greatness.
The happiness and wealth of Śrī Rāma's reign neither Śeṣa, king of serpents, nor Sarasvatī could describe. ॥3॥
uttar.22.cau4: All were generous, all did good to others; men and women all served at the feet of the Brahmins.
Every man kept the vow of one wife, and wives sought their husbands' good in thought, word and deed. ॥4॥
uttar.22.do22: Daṇḍa, the rod, was found only in the hands of ascetics, and bheda, division, only in the dance of a troupe of dancers;
and conquest was heard of only as conquest of the mind: such was the reign of Śrī Rāma. ॥22॥
uttar.23.cau1: The forest trees were ever in flower and in fruit, and the elephant and the lion shared one place.
Bird and beast laid aside the enmity born in them, and love grew up among them all. ॥1॥
uttar.23.cau2: Birds sang, and herds of beasts of many kinds roamed the forest without fear, rejoicing.
A cool, fragrant breeze blew gently, and bees went humming, carrying the nectar of flowers. ॥2॥
uttar.23.cau3: When asked, creepers and trees dripped honey, and the cows yielded whatever milk was wished for.
The land stayed full of harvest at all times; the Tretā age took on the ways of the Kṛta age. ॥3॥
uttar.23.cau4: Mines of many kinds of gems appeared in the mountains, which knew the king for the soul of the world.
Every river ran with the best of water, cool and clear, delightful to drink. ॥4॥
uttar.23.cau5: The seas stayed within their limits and left gems along the shore, which men picked up.
Every pond was crowded with lotuses, and all the ten quarters were bright and glad. ॥5॥
uttar.23.do23: The moon steeped the earth in its rays, and the sun burned no more than the need called for;
clouds gave rain when it was asked for, in the reign of Śrī Rāma. ॥23॥
uttar.24.cau1: The Lord performed millions of horse sacrifices and gave many gifts to the Brahmins.
He guards the path of the Vedas and is foremost in upholding dharma; he is beyond the guṇas, and in enjoyment he is like Indra. ॥1॥
uttar.24.cau2: Sītā is always at one with her husband's wishes; she is a mine of beauty, gentle-natured and humble.
She knows the greatness of the Lord, the ocean of mercy, and serves his lotus feet with her whole heart. ॥2॥
uttar.24.cau3: Though there are many servants, men and women, in the house, all of them ever skilled in the ways of service,
yet Sītā does the work of the house with her own hands and follows Śrī Rāma's every command. ॥3॥
uttar.24.cau4: Whatever way pleases the Lord, the ocean of mercy, Śrī (Sītā), knowing the ways of service, does just that.
She serves all her mothers-in-law in the house, Kausalyā and the rest, with no pride and no vanity in her. ॥4॥
uttar.24.cau5: Umā, she is Ramā, to whom Brahmā and the other gods bow; she is the Mother of the world, ever beyond reproach. ॥5॥
uttar.24.do24: She whose glance of grace the gods long for, and who does not so much as look at them,
sets that nature of hers aside and loves the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma. ॥24॥
uttar.25.cau1: All the brothers serve him in keeping with his wishes, and their love for Śrī Rāma's feet is exceedingly great.
They keep their eyes on the Lord's lotus face, waiting for the compassionate Lord to ask something of them some day. ॥1॥
uttar.25.cau2: Śrī Rāma loves his brothers and teaches them right counsel in many ways.
The people of the city live in joy and enjoy every pleasure, such as even the gods can hardly find. ॥2॥
uttar.25.cau3: Day and night they keep praying to Brahmā, asking for love for the feet of Śrī Rāma.
Two beautiful sons were born to Sītā, Lava and Kuśa, whose praises the Vedas and Purāṇas sing. ॥3॥
uttar.25.cau4: Both are victorious, modest and abodes of virtue, so beautiful that they seem reflections of Śrī Hari himself.
Each of the brothers had two sons, rich in beauty, virtue and good character. ॥4॥
uttar.25.do25: He who is beyond knowledge, speech and the senses, the unborn, who is beyond māyā, the mind and the guṇas,
he, who is being, consciousness and bliss in full, is acting out a noble human life. ॥25॥
uttar.26.cau1: At daybreak, after bathing in the Sarayū, he sits in the assembly with Brahmins and good men.
Vasiṣṭha expounds the Vedas and Purāṇas, and Śrī Rāma listens, though he knows it all. ॥1॥
uttar.26.cau2: He eats together with his younger brothers, and seeing this every mother's heart brims with happiness.
The two brothers Bharata and Śatrughna go to the grove with Hanumān, son of the Wind. ॥2॥
uttar.26.cau3: Sitting there, they ask for the story of Śrī Rāma's virtues, and Hanumān, wise of mind, dives deep into them and tells it.
Hearing of those spotless virtues they are filled with joy, and entreat him to tell them again and again. ॥3॥
uttar.26.cau4: In every home Purāṇas are recited and Śrī Rāma's holy deeds are told in many ways.
Men and women go on singing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and so doing they never notice the days and nights go by. ॥4॥
uttar.26.do26: All the store of happiness and wealth of the people of Ayodhyā
a thousand Śeṣas could not describe, for there Śrī Rāma reigns as king. ॥26॥
uttar.27.cau1: Nārada, Sanaka and other great sages, to see the Lord of Kosala,
come to Ayodhyā every day, and at the sight of the city they forget their dispassion. ॥1॥
uttar.27.cau2: The upper storeys are built of gold and gems, with lovely floors cast in many colours.
Round the city runs a wall of great beauty, crowned with fine battlements of every colour. ॥2॥
uttar.27.cau3: It is as if the hosts of the nine planets had formed an army and come to lay siege to Amarāvatī.
The ground is paved with glass of many colours, and seeing it even the minds of great sages dance. ॥3॥
uttar.27.cau4: The white mansions kiss the sky above, and their pinnacles seem to scorn the brilliance of the sun and moon.
Windows wrought of many gems sparkle, and in every house lamps of gems glow. ॥4॥
uttar.27.cha1: Lamps of gems shine, the mansions gleam, and the thresholds are made of coral.
There are pillars of gems, and walls fashioned by Brahmā himself, inlaid with gold, gems and emeralds.
The mansions are beautiful, charming and spacious, and their courtyards are built of lovely crystal.
At every single gateway the doors are of gold, finely wrought and set with many diamonds. ॥1॥
uttar.27.do27: In every house there are lovely picture halls, where the deeds of Śrī Rāma are painted with great art;
any sage who gazes at them has his heart stolen away. ॥27॥
uttar.28.cau1: Everyone has planted flower gardens and laid them out with care in many styles.
In them graceful creepers of many kinds, lovely to see, are always in bloom, as if it were spring. ॥1॥
uttar.28.cau2: Bees hum with a sweet and charming sound, and a pleasant breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is always blowing.
Children have reared birds of many kinds, which speak sweetly and look lovely as they fly. ॥2॥
uttar.28.cau3: Peacocks, swans, cranes and pigeons look splendid upon the mansions.
Seeing their own reflections here and there, they call in many ways and dance. ॥3॥
uttar.28.cau4: Children teach the parrots and mynas: Say Rāma, Raghupati, protector of his people.
The royal gateway is beautiful in every way, and so are the streets, the crossroads and the markets. ॥4॥
uttar.28.cha1: The lovely markets are beyond describing; there goods are had without payment.
Where he in whom Ramā dwells is himself king, how could the wealth of the place be sung?
Cloth dealers, bankers and many merchants sit there, as though each were Kubera.
Women, men, children and the old, whoever they are, are all happy, all upright and fair to see. ॥1॥
uttar.28.do28: On the northern side flows the Sarayū, its water clear and deep.
Charming ghats are built along it, and there is not the least mud on its banks. ॥28॥
uttar.29.cau1: Far off, in an open place, is a fine ghat where troops of horses and elephants drink.
There are many ghats for drawing water, most charming, and there men do not bathe. ॥1॥
uttar.29.cau2: The royal ghat is fine and beautiful in every way; there men of all four varṇas bathe.
All along the bank stand temples of the gods, with lovely groves on every side of them. ॥2॥
uttar.29.cau3: At spots along the riverside dwell sages and renunciants who have turned from the world and delight in knowledge.
Lovely tulasī lines the banks, set out clump by clump by many sages. ॥3॥
uttar.29.cau4: The beauty of the city cannot be told at all, and outside the city too all is supremely lovely.
At the sight of the city every sin takes flight; there are woods, groves, stepwells and lakes. ॥4॥
uttar.29.cha1: Peerless stepwells, lakes and wells, charming and wide, add to its beauty.
Seeing their fine steps and clear water, gods and sages are entranced.
Lotuses of many colours grow there, many birds call and bees hum.
The delightful gardens, with the songs of cuckoos and other birds, seem to call out to the passers-by. ॥1॥
uttar.29.do29: Can the city whose king is the Lord of Ramā be described?
Aṇimā and the other powers, and all joys and riches, fill the whole of Ayodhyā. ॥29॥
uttar.30.cau1: Everywhere people sing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as they sit together they urge this upon one another:
Worship Śrī Rāma, who cherishes those who bow to him, the home of beauty, good character, grace of form and every virtue. ॥1॥
uttar.30.cau2: Worship him whose eyes are lotuses and whose body is dark, who guards his servants as the eyelids guard the eyes.
Worship him who bears lovely arrows, bow and quiver, the sun to the lotus grove of the saints, steadfast in battle. ॥2॥
uttar.30.cau3: Worship him who is Garuḍa to the terrible serpent of Time, who wipes out the sense of mine in all who bow to him free of desire.
Worship him who is the hunter of the herd of deer, greed and delusion, a lion to the elephant of desire, and the giver of joy to his devotees. ॥3॥
uttar.30.cau4: He is the sun to the thick darkness of doubt and grief, and the fire that burns the dense forest of the demons.
Why do you not worship Śrī Rāma, together with Janaka's daughter, who shatters the fear of worldly existence? ॥4॥
uttar.30.cau5: He is a mass of frost to the mosquitoes of countless desires; he is ever the same, unborn and imperishable.
Worship the delight of the sages, who takes away the burden of the earth, the generous Lord of Tulasīdāsa. ॥5॥
uttar.30.do30: In this way the women and men of the city sing the praises of Śrī Rāma,
and the Lord, treasury of compassion, is ever gracious to them all. ॥30॥
uttar.31.cau1: Garuḍa, ever since the mighty sun of Śrī Rāma's glory rose,
its light has filled the three worlds; to many it has brought joy, and to many grief of heart. ॥1॥
uttar.31.cau2: I shall tell you in full of those who grieve. First, the night of ignorance came to an end.
The owls of sin hid wherever they could, and the white lilies of desire and anger shrank shut. ॥2॥
uttar.31.cau3: Actions of many kinds, the guṇas, time and one's nature: these cakora birds never find any joy.
Envy, vanity, delusion and pride are thieves whose craft succeeds in no direction. ॥3॥
uttar.31.cau4: In the lake of dharma the lotuses of knowledge and realised knowledge opened in many ways.
Happiness, contentment, dispassion and discernment, these many cakravāka birds, were freed from grief. ॥4॥
uttar.31.do31: When this sun of glory shines in anyone's heart,
those named last grow strong, and those named first are destroyed. ॥31॥
uttar.32.cau1: Once Śrī Rāma, with his brothers and with Hanumān, son of the Wind, most dear to him,
went to see a beautiful grove; every tree was in flower and covered in fresh leaves. ॥1॥
uttar.32.cau2: Knowing it to be the right time, Sanaka and his brothers came, masses of radiance, graced with virtue and good character.
They are ever absorbed in the bliss of Brahman; to look at they are children, yet they are of great age. ॥2॥
uttar.32.cau3: They seem the four Vedas in bodily form; these sages see all alike and are free of all sense of difference.
The quarters of the sky are their only clothing, and their one passion is to listen wherever the deeds of Śrī Rāma are being told. ॥3॥
uttar.32.cau4: Bhavānī, Sanaka and his brothers had been staying where the wise and great sage Agastya, the pot-born, lives.
The great sage had told the story of Śrī Rāma at length; from it knowledge is born, as fire is born from the fire-sticks. ॥4॥
uttar.32.do32: Seeing the sages coming, Śrī Rāma joyfully prostrated himself before them.
Welcoming them and asking after their well-being, the Lord gave them his own yellow robe to sit on. ॥32॥
uttar.33.cau1: The three brothers too, with Hanumān, son of the Wind, prostrated themselves, and their joy was great.
The sages gazed on Śrī Rāma's matchless beauty and were lost in it; they could not hold their minds back. ॥1॥
uttar.33.cau2: Dark of body, with lotus eyes, he is the home of beauty and the one who frees from worldly existence.
They stared without a blink, not closing their eyes, while the Lord, palms joined, bowed his head. ॥2॥
uttar.33.cau3: Seeing their state, Śrī Rāma shed tears and the hair of his body stood on end.
The Lord took the great sages by the hand, sat them down and spoke words of the utmost charm: ॥3॥
uttar.33.cau4: Today I am blessed; listen, lords of sages: the sight of you wipes out sin.
The company of the good comes by great good fortune, and through it the round of birth is broken with no effort at all. ॥4॥
uttar.33.do33: The company of saints is the road to liberation, and the company of the sensual the road to worldly existence:
so say the saints, the poets, the learned, the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the good books. ॥33॥
uttar.34.cau1: Hearing the Lord's words, the four sages rejoiced and, thrilling all over, began a hymn of praise:
Glory to you, Lord, endless, free from every ill, sinless, many and one, full of compassion. ॥1॥
uttar.34.cau2: Glory to you who are beyond attributes, glory, glory to you, ocean of virtues, home of joy, beautiful and supremely refined.
Glory to you, consort of Lakṣmī; glory to you, upholder of the earth; peerless, unborn, without beginning, a mine of splendour. ॥2॥
uttar.34.cau3: You are a treasury of knowledge, free of pride yourself and giving honour to others; your holy fame is told by the Purāṇas and the Vedas.
You know the truth, you remember every kindness, you destroy ignorance; you have many names and yet no name, and are without stain. ॥3॥
uttar.34.cau4: You are all things, you pervade all and dwell for ever in every heart: protect us.
Shatter the pairs of opposites, our troubles and the snare of worldly existence; dwell in our hearts, Śrī Rāma, and crush desire and pride. ॥4॥
uttar.34.do34: Highest bliss, dwelling-place of compassion, you bring every wish of the heart to fulfilment.
Śrī Rāma, give us loving devotion that never fails. ॥34॥
uttar.35.cau1: Give us devotion, O Lord of the Raghus, the devotion that purifies above all and puts an end to the threefold affliction and the arrogance of worldly existence.
To those who bow before you, you are the wish-granting cow and the wish-fulfilling tree: be pleased, my Lord, and give us this boon. ॥1॥
uttar.35.cau2: O Lord of the Raghus, you are Agastya to the ocean of worldly existence; you are easily won by service and give every joy.
Rend the cruel sorrows born of the mind, friend of the lowly, and let evenness of mind spread wide. ॥2॥
uttar.35.cau3: You drive away hope, fear, envy and the rest, and you increase humility, discernment and dispassion.
Crest-jewel of kings, ornament of the earth, give us devotion, the boat that crosses the river of birth and death. ॥3॥
uttar.35.cau4: You are the swan who dwells for ever in the Mānasa lake of the sages' minds; Brahmā and Śiva worship your lotus feet.
You are the banner of Raghu's line, the guardian of the bounds the Vedas set, and the devourer of time, karma, nature and the guṇas. ॥4॥
uttar.35.cau5: You carry souls across and are yourself the boat, and you take away every fault; ornament of the three worlds, you are the Lord of Tulasīdāsa. ॥5॥
uttar.35.do35: Praising him again and again and bowing their heads in love,
Sanaka and his brothers went to the abode of Brahmā, having received the boon they wanted most. ॥35॥
uttar.36.cau1: Once Sanaka and the others had departed for the world of Brahmā, the brothers bowed their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet.
All of them were shy of asking the Lord, and all of them looked towards Hanumān. ॥1॥
uttar.36.cau2: They longed to hear words from the Lord's own lips, the hearing of which removes every error.
The Lord, who knows all hearts, understood everything and asked: Tell me, Hanumān, what is it? ॥2॥
uttar.36.cau3: Then Hanumān, with joined palms, said: Listen, Lord, compassionate to the lowly.
My Lord, Bharata wants to ask you something, but his mind hesitates to put the question. ॥3॥
uttar.36.cau4: Śrī Rāma said: You know my nature, Hanumān. Has Bharata ever been in any way apart from me?
Hearing this from the Lord, Bharata clasped his feet and said: Listen, my Lord, remover of the distress of those who bow to you. ॥4॥
uttar.36.do36: My Lord, I have no doubt at all, nor grief nor delusion even in a dream.
It is all your grace alone, you who are grace and bliss in fullness. ॥36॥
uttar.37.cau1: Treasury of mercy, I am going to make bold: I am your servant, and you give joy to your own.
O Lord of the Raghus, the Vedas and the Purāṇas have sung the glory of saints in many ways. ॥1॥
uttar.37.cau2: You too have praised them with your own lips, and the Lord's love for them is great.
My Lord, ocean of mercy, wise in virtues and knowledge, I wish to hear what marks them out. ॥2॥
uttar.37.cau3: Protector of those who bow to you, explain to me the difference between the saint and the wicked, setting each apart.
Śrī Rāma said: Listen, brother: the marks of saints are countless and well known in the Vedas and the Purāṇas. ॥3॥
uttar.37.cau4: Saints and the wicked behave towards each other as sandalwood and the axe do.
Listen, brother: the axe cuts down the sandal tree of Malaya, and the tree gives it its own virtue, filling it with fragrance. ॥4॥
uttar.37.do37: That is why sandalwood is placed on the heads of the gods and is loved by all the world,
while the axe's blade gets this penalty: it is burnt in the fire and pounded with the sledge. ॥37॥
uttar.38.cau1: Saints are not greedy for the things of the senses; they are mines of good conduct and virtue; they grieve at another's grief and rejoice at another's joy.
They are even-minded, have no enemy, are free of pride and dispassionate, and have given up greed, anger, elation and fear. ॥1॥
uttar.38.cau2: Their hearts are tender, they are kind to the lowly, and in thought, word and deed their devotion to me is without guile.
They honour everyone and seek no honour for themselves. Bharata, such beings are as dear to me as my own life. ॥2॥
uttar.38.cau3: They are free of desire and wholly given to my Name; they are homes of peace, dispassion, humility and gladness.
They have coolness, simplicity, friendliness and a love for the feet of brāhmaṇas, which gives birth to dharma. ॥3॥
uttar.38.cau4: Dear one, know the one in whose heart all these marks dwell to be a true saint, always.
Such people never waver from calm, self-restraint, their observances and right conduct, and never speak a harsh word. ॥4॥
uttar.38.do38: Those to whom blame and praise are alike, and whose attachment is to my lotus feet,
those good people, homes of virtue and stores of joy, are dear to me as my life. ॥38॥
uttar.39.cau1: Now hear the nature of the wicked: never keep their company, not even by mistake.
Their company always brings sorrow, as an unruly cow spoils a good kapilā cow. ॥1॥
uttar.39.cau2: The hearts of the wicked burn with a fierce heat; they are for ever burning at the sight of another's wealth.
Wherever they hear someone else run down, they are as delighted as if they had found a treasure just lying there. ॥2॥
uttar.39.cau3: They are given over to desire, anger, pride and greed; they are pitiless, deceitful, crooked, and homes of sin.
They bear enmity to everyone without cause, and do harm even to the one who does them good. ॥3॥
uttar.39.cau4: False is their taking and false their giving, false their meal and false their snack of parched grain.
They speak sweet words like the peacock, and are as hard of heart as the peacock, which devours great snakes. ॥4॥
uttar.39.do39: They harm others and are set on other men's wives, other people's wealth and the slander of others.
Such men are base and steeped in sin: man-eating demons in human form. ॥39॥
uttar.40.cau1: Greed is their blanket and greed their bed; they live for lust and the belly and have no fear of Yama's city.
If they hear anyone praised, they draw long breaths as though a fit of ague had come on them. ॥1॥
uttar.40.cau2: When they see anyone in trouble, they are as happy as if they had become kings of the world.
They are set on their own interest, at odds with their families, given over to lust and greed, and very wrathful. ॥2॥
uttar.40.cau3: They do not heed mother, father, teacher or brāhmaṇa; they go to ruin and destroy others as well.
In their delusion they bear ill will to others, and they have no taste for the company of saints or for the story of Śrī Hari. ॥3॥
uttar.40.cau4: They are oceans of faults, slow of wit and lustful; they mock the Vedas and lord it over others' wealth.
They bear ill will to others, and to brāhmaṇas most of all; they hide pretence and deceit in their hearts and put on a fine appearance. ॥4॥
uttar.40.do40: Such base and wicked people are not found in the Kṛta and Tretā ages;
in the Dvāpara there are a few, and in the Kali age there will be crowds of them. ॥40॥
uttar.41.cau1: Brother, there is no dharma like doing good to others, and nothing so low as causing others pain.
This is the settled finding of all the Purāṇas and the Vedas, dear one, as I tell it; the learned know it well. ॥1॥
uttar.41.cau2: Those who, having a human body, give pain to others suffer the heavy hardships of worldly existence.
Swayed by delusion, men commit many sins; bent on self-interest, they ruin their world to come. ॥2॥
uttar.41.cau3: To them, brother, I am death itself, the one who gives the fruit of good and evil deeds.
Knowing this, the truly wise, who have seen the sorrows of the round of births, worship me. ॥3॥
uttar.41.cau4: They leave behind all action that yields good or ill, and worship me, Lord of gods, men and sages.
I have told you the qualities of saints and of the wicked; those who have understood them and kept them in mind do not fall into worldly existence. ॥4॥
uttar.41.do41: Listen, dear one: merits and faults are many, and all of them are made by māyā.
The merit lies in seeing neither of them; to see them is itself a want of discernment. ॥41॥
uttar.42.cau1: Hearing these words from the Lord's own lips, all the brothers were overjoyed; their love was more than their hearts could hold.
Again and again they made humble entreaty to him, and Hanumān's heart was filled with boundless joy. ॥1॥
uttar.42.cau2: Then Śrī Rāma went to his own palace, and in this way he performed new acts every day.
Again and again the sage Nārada would come and sing the holy deeds of Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.42.cau3: Having seen the ever-new deeds, the sage would go and tell the whole story in Brahmā's world.
Brahmā, hearing it, would be filled with delight and say: Dear one, sing his praises again and again. ॥3॥
uttar.42.cau4: Sanaka and his brothers praise Nārada; though these sages are devoted to Brahman,
on hearing the praises they forget their samādhi and listen with reverence, for they are the most worthy of hearers. ॥4॥
uttar.42.do42: Even those who are free while still in the body and absorbed in Brahman leave their meditation to hear these deeds;
those who take no delight in the story of Śrī Hari have hearts of stone. ॥42॥
uttar.43.cau1: Once Śrī Rāma sent for them, and the guru, the Brahmins and all the citizens came.
When the guru, the sages, the Brahmins and the good had taken their seats, the Lord, who ends worldly existence for his devotees, spoke these words: ॥1॥
uttar.43.cau2: Listen to my words, all you citizens. I do not say this out of any attachment in my heart.
There is no wrong in it, and no lording it over you. Listen, and do whatever pleases you. ॥2॥
uttar.43.cau3: Whoever accepts my command is my servant, and he is the one most dear to me.
Brothers, if I say anything that is not right, set fear aside and stop me. ॥3॥
uttar.43.cau4: It is by great good fortune that you have gained a human body, which all the scriptures declare to be rare even for the gods.
It is the home of spiritual practice and the door to liberation. One who gains it and still does not set right his next world ॥4॥
uttar.43.do43: suffers in the world beyond, and beats his head again and again in remorse,
laying false blame on Time, on karma and on God. ॥43॥
uttar.44.cau1: Brothers, sense pleasure is not the fruit of this body; even heaven is brief and brings sorrow in the end.
Those who gain a human body and give their minds to the objects of the senses are fools who take poison in exchange for nectar. ॥1॥
uttar.44.cau2: No one ever calls him wise who loses the philosopher's stone and picks up a guñjā seed.
This imperishable soul wanders through the four kinds of origin and the eighty-four lakh species. ॥2॥
uttar.44.cau3: It wanders on and on, pushed by māyā, caught in the ring of Time, karma, its own nature and the guṇas.
Now and then God, who loves without cause, has compassion and gives it a human body. ॥3॥
uttar.44.cau4: The human body is a boat for the ocean of worldly existence, and my grace the favourable wind;
the true guru is the helmsman of this sturdy boat. Thus means that are hard to come by have been made easy for it to gain. ॥4॥
uttar.44.do44: The man who has all this at hand and still does not cross the ocean of worldly existence
is ungrateful and dull of mind, and goes the way of one who destroys himself. ॥44॥
uttar.45.cau1: If you want happiness in the next world and here, hear my words and hold them firmly in your hearts.
Brothers, this path is easy and gives joy: devotion to me, which the Purāṇas and the Vedas have sung. ॥1॥
uttar.45.cau2: Knowledge is hard to reach, and many things stand in its way; its practice is hard, and the mind finds no prop in it.
Even if someone gains it after much hardship, without devotion he too is not dear to me. ॥2॥
uttar.45.cau3: Devotion depends on nothing else and is a mine of every joy, yet no creature gains it without the company of the good.
Without a store of merit one does not meet saints, and the company of the good puts an end to the round of births. ॥3॥
uttar.45.cau4: There is one act of merit in the world and no second: to worship the feet of the Brahmins in thought, deed and word.
Sages and gods look with favour on one who serves the Brahmins without deceit. ॥4॥
uttar.45.do45: With folded hands I tell you all one more secret teaching:
without worship of Śiva no one gains devotion to me. ॥45॥
uttar.46.cau1: Tell me, what labour is there on the path of devotion? It needs no yoga, no sacrifice, no japa, austerity or fasting;
only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment always with whatever comes. ॥1॥
uttar.46.cau2: If one who calls himself my servant still puts his hope in men, tell me, what kind of faith is that?
Why say more and draw out the talk? Brothers, it is this conduct that wins me over. ॥2॥
uttar.46.cau3: He who has no enmity or strife, no hope and no fear, finds every quarter full of joy at all times.
One who starts no ventures out of desire, has no home of his own, is free of pride, sin and anger, and is capable and rich in realised knowledge, ॥3॥
uttar.46.cau4: who always loves the company of the good, to whom the objects of the senses, heaven and liberation are as straw,
who holds fast to the side of devotion yet without perversity, and has swept away all wicked argument, ॥4॥
uttar.46.do46: who delights in my many virtues and my name, and is rid of attachment, pride and delusion:
his joy is known only to one who is himself a mass of supreme bliss. ॥46॥
uttar.47.cau1: As soon as they heard Śrī Rāma's nectar-like words, all of them clasped the feet of the abode of mercy.
They said: O treasury of mercy, you are our mother, father, guru and brother, dearer to us than life. ॥1॥
uttar.47.cau2: Rāma, you are our body, our wealth, our home and our well-wisher; in every way you take away the pain of those who bow to you.
No one but you gives such counsel; even mother and father are bent on their own interest. ॥2॥
uttar.47.cau3: O foe of the demons, there are only two in the world who do good without a motive: you and your servants.
All others in the world are friends for their own ends; my Lord, not even in a dream do they seek the highest good. ॥3॥
uttar.47.cau4: Hearing everyone's words, steeped in the sweetness of love, Śrī Rāma rejoiced at heart.
Given leave, they went to their own homes, talking of the Lord's lovely words. ॥4॥
uttar.47.do47: Umā, the men and women of Ayodhyā are fulfilment itself,
for there Śrī Rāma, Brahman, dense with being, consciousness and bliss, is king. ॥47॥
uttar.48.cau1: Once the sage Vasiṣṭha came to where Śrī Rāma, the lovely abode of joy, was.
Śrī Rāma received him with great honour, washed his feet and took the water of the washing. ॥1॥
uttar.48.cau2: The sage said with folded hands: Listen, Rāma, ocean of mercy, to a request of mine.
Watching your conduct again and again, a boundless bewilderment rises in my heart. ॥2॥
uttar.48.cau3: Your glory is boundless, my Lord, and not even the Vedas know it; how am I to tell of it?
The office of family priest is a very low one; the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the smṛtis condemn it. ॥3॥
uttar.48.cau4: When I would not take it up, Brahmā said to me: Son, it will bring you gain hereafter.
Brahman, the Supreme Self, will take human form and be king, the ornament of the line of Raghu. ॥4॥
uttar.48.do48: Then I reflected in my heart: the one for whom yoga, sacrifice, vows and charity are performed
I shall gain through this very work; no other dharma equals it. ॥48॥
uttar.49.cau1: Japa, austerity, observances, yoga, one's own duty, the many good works that spring from the Vedas,
knowledge, compassion, self-restraint, bathing at holy places, every dharma that the Vedas and the good speak of, ॥1॥
uttar.49.cau2: and the reading and hearing of the many Āgamas, Vedas and Purāṇas have but one fruit, my Lord:
unbroken love for your lotus feet. This is the lovely fruit of every practice. ॥2॥
uttar.49.cau3: Is dirt washed away with dirt? Does anyone get ghee by churning water?
O Lord of the Raghus, without the water of loving devotion the dirt within never goes. ॥3॥
uttar.49.cau4: He alone knows all, he alone knows the truth and is learned; he is the home of virtues, with realised knowledge unbroken;
he is capable and has every good mark, who loves your lotus feet. ॥4॥
uttar.49.do49: My Lord, there is one boon I ask; Rāma, be gracious and grant it:
in birth after birth may my love for the Lord's lotus feet never lessen. ॥49॥
uttar.50.cau1: With these words the sage Vasiṣṭha came home; he had greatly pleased the heart of the ocean of mercy.
The Lord, giver of joy to his servants, took Hanumān and his brothers, Bharata and the rest, with him, ॥1॥
uttar.50.cau2: and the compassionate Lord went out of the city and had elephants, chariots and horses brought.
He looked at them all and graciously praised them, and gave them fittingly to whoever wanted them. ॥2॥
uttar.50.cau3: The Lord who takes away all weariness grew weary himself and went to a cool mango grove.
Bharata spread out his own cloth; the Lord sat down, and all the brothers attended on him. ॥3॥
uttar.50.cau4: Then the son of the Wind fanned him, his body thrilling and his eyes filling with tears.
There is no one as fortunate as Hanumān, nor anyone who loves Śrī Rāma's feet as he does. ॥4॥
uttar.50.cau5: Pārvatī, the Lord has praised his love and service again and again with his own lips. ॥5॥
uttar.50.do50: At that moment the sage Nārada came, his vīṇā in his hand,
and began to sing of the sweet glory of Śrī Rāma, which is ever new: ॥50॥
uttar.51.cau1: Look upon me, lotus-eyed Lord, whose gracious glance frees from sorrow.
Dark as a blue lotus, you are a bee drinking the nectar in the heart-lotus of Kāma's enemy, O Hari. ॥1॥
uttar.51.cau2: You break the might of the demon hosts, delight sages and the good, and destroy sin;
you are a mass of fresh clouds to the crop that is the Brahmins, refuge of those without refuge, and one who takes the lowly to himself. ॥2॥
uttar.51.cau3: You whose strong arms broke the earth's great burden, you skilled in slaying Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Virādha,
foe of Rāvaṇa, joy itself, best of kings, moon to the night-lotus of Daśaratha's line, glory to you! ॥3॥
uttar.51.cau4: Your fair fame is known in the Purāṇas, the Vedas and the Āgamas, and assemblies of gods, sages and saints sing it.
Compassionate, breaker of false pride, skilled in every way, you are the adornment of Kosala. ॥4॥
uttar.51.cau5: Your name churns away the filth of the Kali age and destroys attachment. Lord of Tulasīdāsa, protect the one who bows before you. ॥5॥
uttar.51.do51: Having lovingly told of Śrī Rāma's many virtues, the sage Nārada
held the ocean of beauty in his heart and went to Brahmā's realm. ॥51॥
uttar.52.cau1: Listen, Pārvatī: I have told this pure story in full, as far as my understanding goes.
Śrī Rāma's deeds are a thousand million and without end; neither the Vedas nor Sarasvatī can tell them to the end. ॥1॥
uttar.52.cau2: Śrī Rāma is endless, his virtues endless, and endless too his births, deeds and names.
The drops of water and the specks of dust on the earth might be counted, but the telling of Śrī Rāma's deeds never comes to an end. ॥2॥
uttar.52.cau3: This pure story gives the abode of Śrī Hari, and hearing it brings unfailing devotion.
Umā, I have told the whole lovely story that Kākabhuśuṇḍi told Garuḍa, king of birds. ॥3॥
uttar.52.cau4: I have described some of Śrī Rāma's virtues in detail. Now, Pārvatī, tell me what more I should say.
Hearing the blessed story, Umā was glad, and spoke in a very humble and gentle voice: ॥4॥
uttar.52.cau5: Blessed, blessed, blessed am I, foe of Tripura, for I have heard the virtues of Śrī Rāma that rid us of the fear of worldly existence. ॥5॥
uttar.52.do52क: Abode of mercy, by your grace I have now gained all I sought, and no delusion is left in me.
My Lord, I have come to know the glory of Śrī Rāma, the fullness of consciousness and bliss. ॥52 (क)॥
uttar.52.do52ख: My Lord, the moon of your face pours out the nectar of the story of Śrī Rāma;
O steady-minded one, my mind drinks it through the cups of my ears and is never sated. ॥52 (ख)॥
uttar.53.cau1: Those who have had their fill of hearing Śrī Rāma's deeds have never known their special savour.
Even the great sages who are liberated while living go on hearing the virtues of Śrī Hari without end. ॥1॥
uttar.53.cau2: For one who wants to reach the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence, the story of Śrī Rāma is a sturdy boat.
And even for those given to the senses, the many virtues of Śrī Hari are a joy to the ears and a delight to the mind. ॥2॥
uttar.53.cau3: Who is there in the world with ears who does not love the deeds of Śrī Rāma?
Those who find no pleasure in the story of Śrī Rāma are dull creatures who destroy their own selves. ॥3॥
uttar.53.cau4: My Lord, you have sung this Mānasa of the deeds of Śrī Hari, and hearing it I have found boundless joy.
You said that this lovely story was sung by Kākabhuśuṇḍi to Garuḍa. ॥4॥
uttar.53.do53: He is firm in dispassion, knowledge and realised knowledge, and has deep love for Śrī Rāma's feet;
yet devotion to Śrī Rāma in the body of a crow: about this I have the gravest doubt. ॥53॥
uttar.54.cau1: Hear me, Purāri: of a thousand men, one may be found who keeps a vow of dharma.
Among ten million who live by dharma, someone turns away from the objects of sense and gives himself to dispassion. ॥1॥
uttar.54.cau2: The Veda says that among ten million of the dispassionate, scarcely one gains true knowledge.
Among ten million who have knowledge, scarcely one in the world is liberated while living. ॥2॥
uttar.54.cau3: Among a thousand of these, rare is the one of realised knowledge, absorbed in Brahman, a mine of every joy.
Of all beings, the righteous, the dispassionate, the knowing, the liberated while living and those absorbed in Brahman, ॥3॥
uttar.54.cau4: rarest of all, O lord of the gods, is one devoted to Śrī Rāma, rid of pride and māyā.
How did a crow come by such devotion to Śrī Hari? Lord of the universe, explain it to me. ॥4॥
uttar.54.do54: Wholly given to Śrī Rāma, intent on knowledge, a home of virtues, steady of mind:
tell me, my Lord, for what reason did he receive the body of a crow? ॥54॥
uttar.55.cau1: Compassionate one, tell me where the crow obtained this pure and lovely story of the Lord.
And how did you hear it, enemy of Kāma? Tell me, for I am very curious. ॥1॥
uttar.55.cau2: Garuḍa is greatly wise, a heap of virtues, a servant of Śrī Hari who lives very close to him.
Why did he pass over the hosts of sages and go to a crow to hear the story? ॥2॥
uttar.55.cau3: Tell me how the dialogue came about between these two devotees of Śrī Hari, the crow and Garuḍa, the eater of serpents.
Hearing Gaurī's simple, pleasing words, Śiva was glad and said with warm regard: ॥3॥
uttar.55.cau4: Blessed are you, Satī; your understanding is pure, and your love for Śrī Rāma's feet is no small thing.
Now hear a most holy history, on hearing which the delusion of the whole world is dispelled, ॥4॥
uttar.55.cau5: faith in Śrī Rāma's feet springs up, and a person crosses the ocean of worldly existence without effort. ॥5॥
uttar.55.do55: The king of birds too went to the crow and asked just such questions.
I shall tell you all of it with reverence; listen, Umā, with your whole mind. ॥55॥
uttar.56.cau1: Hear, fair-faced one with lovely eyes, how I came to hear this story that sets one free from worldly existence.
Your first descent was in Dakṣa's home, and in that birth you were called Satī. ॥1॥
uttar.56.cau2: When Dakṣa's sacrifice brought you insult, your anger was so great that you gave up your life.
My attendants laid the sacrifice in ruins; all that happened then you know well. ॥2॥
uttar.56.cau3: Then my mind was filled with sorrow, and I grieved at being parted from you, my beloved.
In a mood of detachment I roamed about, looking at the sights of lovely forests, mountains, rivers and lakes. ॥3॥
uttar.56.cau4: Far to the north of Mount Sumeru there is a blue mountain of great beauty.
Its golden peaks are lovely, and four fair ones among them won my heart. ॥4॥
uttar.56.cau5: On each of them stands a single huge tree: a banyan, a pīpal, a pākar and a mango.
Crowning the mountain is a lovely lake; one look at its steps of gems and the mind is charmed. ॥5॥
uttar.56.do56: The lake holds cool, pure, sweet water and a wealth of lotuses in many colours;
the swans in their flocks call with a soft, sweet cry, and lovely bees hum. ॥56॥
uttar.57.cau1: On that lovely mountain lives the bird; even at the end of an age of creation he does not perish.
The many merits and faults that māyā has made, delusion, desire and the rest of unwisdom, ॥1॥
uttar.57.cau2: which pervade the whole world, never come near that mountain.
How the crow lives there and worships Śrī Hari, hear now, Umā, with love. ॥2॥
uttar.57.cau3: Under the pīpal tree he sits in meditation; under the pākar he performs the sacrifice of japa.
In the mango's shade he worships in his mind; apart from the worship of Śrī Hari he has no other work. ॥3॥
uttar.57.cau4: Under the banyan he tells episodes of the story of Śrī Hari, and many birds come to listen.
He sings the wondrous deeds of Śrī Rāma in many ways, with love and reverence. ॥4॥
uttar.57.cau5: All the swans of pure mind that live for ever on that lake listen to him.
Going there, I saw this marvel, and a rare joy rose within me. ॥5॥
uttar.57.do57: Then I took the form of a swan and stayed there for a time,
and having heard the virtues of Śrī Rāma with reverence, I came back to Kailāsa. ॥57॥
uttar.58.cau1: Girijā, I have told you the whole account of the time I went to that bird.
Now hear the story of why Garuḍa, the banner of the race of birds, went to the crow. ॥1॥
uttar.58.cau2: When Śrī Rāma played at battle — a deed I am ashamed to think of —
and let himself be bound by Indrajit, the sage Nārada then sent Garuḍa. ॥2॥
uttar.58.cau3: Once the bonds were cut the serpent-eater went off, yet his heart was seized by a fierce despondency.
Again and again his mind went back to the Lord being bound, and the foe of serpents pondered: ॥3॥
uttar.58.cau4: Brahman, all-pervading, stainless, the lord of speech, the Supreme Lord beyond māyā and delusion:
I heard that he had taken birth in the world, yet I saw nothing of that power. ॥4॥
uttar.58.do58: He whose name men repeat to be freed from the bonds of worldly existence,
that same Rāma a petty demon has tied in a noose of serpents! ॥58॥
uttar.59.cau1: He reasoned with his mind in many ways, but knowledge did not dawn, and confusion clouded his heart.
Worn with distress, his mind piling up arguments, he fell under delusion just as you did. ॥1॥
uttar.59.cau2: Distraught, he sought out the divine sage and laid before him the doubt that troubled him.
Hearing it, Nārada was filled with pity and said: Listen, Garuḍa; the māyā of Śrī Rāma is mighty. ॥2॥
uttar.59.cau3: It steals away the minds even of the wise and by sheer force fills them with delusion.
It has made me dance many a time, king of birds, and it is this that now pervades you. ॥3॥
uttar.59.cau4: A great delusion has arisen in your heart, Garuḍa, and it will not soon go at my words.
King of birds, go to the four-faced Brahmā and do whatever he bids you. ॥4॥
uttar.59.do59: So saying, the divine sage went on his way, singing the virtues of Śrī Rāma,
and in his great wisdom he spoke again and again of the might of Śrī Hari's māyā. ॥59॥
uttar.60.cau1: Then the king of birds went to Brahmā and set his doubt before him.
Brahmā heard it and bowed low to Śrī Rāma; as the Lord's might dawned on him, love welled up in him beyond measure. ॥1॥
uttar.60.cau2: The Creator reflected in his mind: Poets, scholars and the wise are all in the grip of māyā.
The power of Śrī Hari's māyā has no bounds; many a time it has made me dance. ॥2॥
uttar.60.cau3: This world of moving and unmoving beings was made by me; small wonder if the king of birds is deluded.
Then Brahmā spoke in gracious words: Maheśa knows the greatness of Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
uttar.60.cau4: Son of Vinatā, go to Śiva; do not ask anyone anywhere else, dear one.
There your doubt will be removed. As soon as he heard Brahmā's words, the bird set off. ॥4॥
uttar.60.do60: Then, in great anxiety, the king of birds came to me.
Umā, I was then setting out for Kubera's home, and you had stayed on Kailāsa. ॥60॥
uttar.61.cau1: He bowed his head at my feet with reverence and then told me his doubt.
Hearing his entreaty and gentle words, Bhavānī, I said to him with love: ॥1॥
uttar.61.cau2: Garuḍa, we have met on the road; how can I make it clear to you here?
All doubt is broken only when one keeps the company of the good for a long time ॥2॥
uttar.61.cau3: and hears there the lovely story of Śrī Hari that the sages have sung in many ways,
whose theme in the beginning, the middle and the end is the Lord, Śrī Rāma, the Blessed One. ॥3॥
uttar.61.cau4: There is a place, brother, where Śrī Hari's story is told daily; I send you there, so go and hear it.
Hearing it, you will be rid of every doubt, and a deep love for Śrī Rāma's feet will grow in you. ॥4॥
uttar.61.do61: Without the company of the good there is no story of Śrī Hari, and without it delusion does not flee;
and until delusion is gone there is no firm love for Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥61॥
uttar.62.cau1: Without love Śrī Rāma is not found, though one practise yoga, austerity, knowledge and dispassion.
In the north is a beautiful blue mountain; there lives the gentle Kākabhuśuṇḍi. ॥1॥
uttar.62.cau2: He is supremely skilled in the path of devotion to Śrī Rāma, wise, a house of virtues, and very ancient.
Without pause he tells the story of Śrī Rāma, and fine birds of every kind listen with reverence. ॥2॥
uttar.62.cau3: Hear there the countless virtues of Śrī Hari, and your grief that springs from delusion will be gone.
Once I had made it all clear, he went off glad at heart, after bowing his head at my feet. ॥3॥
uttar.62.cau4: That is why, Umā, I gave him no explanation: through Śrī Rāma's grace the hidden reason had become clear to me.
At some time he must have grown proud, and the treasury of mercy wishes to take that pride away. ॥4॥
uttar.62.cau5: And partly for this reason too I did not keep him with me: a bird understands only a bird's speech.
The Lord's māyā is mighty, Bhavānī; who is so wise that it cannot delude him? ॥5॥
uttar.62.do62क: He who is the crown of the wise and of devotees, the mount of the Lord of the three worlds:
even him māyā deluded, and yet base men are full of pride. ॥62 (क)॥
uttar.62.do62ख: When māyā deludes even Śiva and Brahmā, what is any other poor creature?
Knowing this in their hearts, the sages worship the Lord, the master of māyā. ॥62 (ख)॥
uttar.63.cau1: Garuḍa went to where Kākabhuśuṇḍi lived, whose mind is never dulled and whose devotion to Śrī Hari is unbroken.
As he looked on the mountain he grew glad at heart, and all māyā, delusion and care left him. ॥1॥
uttar.63.cau2: He bathed in the pond and drank its water, then went beneath the banyan tree with a glad heart.
Many aged birds had gathered there to hear the delightful deeds of Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.63.cau3: Kākabhuśuṇḍi wished to begin the story, and at that very time Garuḍa, lord of birds, came there.
Seeing the king of all birds coming, the crow and the whole gathering with him were filled with joy. ॥3॥
uttar.63.cau4: He showed the king of birds great honour, welcomed him and asked how he fared, and seated him on a fine seat.
Then, having worshipped him with love, the crow spoke these sweet words: ॥4॥
uttar.63.do63क: My lord, king of birds, seeing you I am blessed.
Give me your command and I will carry it out now. For what purpose have you come, my lord? ॥63 (क)॥
uttar.63.do63ख: Garuḍa said gently: You are always the very form of fulfilment,
you whose praises Śiva himself has sung with reverence from his own lips. ॥63 (ख)॥
uttar.64.cau1: Listen, dear sir: all that I came for is done, now that I have seen you.
Seeing your hermitage, so supremely holy, I am rid of delusion, of doubt and of confusions of many kinds. ॥1॥
uttar.64.cau2: Now the story of Śrī Rāma, which is utterly holy, which always gives joy and destroys sorrow in heaps:
tell it to me with reverence, dear sir; again and again I entreat you, my lord. ॥2॥
uttar.64.cau3: Kākabhuśuṇḍi heard Garuḍa's humble words, artless, full of love, pleasing and wholly pure.
His heart was filled with great eagerness, and he began to tell the tale of Śrī Rāma's virtues. ॥3॥
uttar.64.cau4: First, Bhavānī, with deep love he described at length the lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds.
Then he told of Nārada's boundless delusion, and after that of Rāvaṇa's coming into the world. ॥4॥
uttar.64.cau5: Next he sang of the Lord's descent to earth, and then, with all his heart, told of his childhood. ॥5॥
uttar.64.do64: With great joy in his heart he told the childhood deeds in many ways;
then he told of the sage's coming, and of Śrī Rāma's marriage. ॥64॥
uttar.65.cau1: Then he told of the episode of Śrī Rāma's consecration, and how the king's word shattered the joy of the kingdom.
He told too of the citizens' grief at parting, and of the talk between Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. ॥1॥
uttar.65.cau2: He told of the going to the forest, the boatman's love, the crossing of the Gaṅgā and the stay at Prayāga.
He described the Lord's meeting with Vālmīki, and how the Lord made his home at Citrakūṭa. ॥2॥
uttar.65.cau3: Then came the minister's return to the city, the king's death and Bharata's arrival, with a full account of his love.
He told how, after the king's last rites, Bharata took the citizens with him to the place where the Lord, the home of joy, was staying. ॥3॥
uttar.65.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma reasoned with him in many ways, and he came back to Ayodhyā with the sandals.
He went on to describe Bharata's way of life, the deed of Indra's son, and the Lord's meeting with Atri. ॥4॥
uttar.65.do65: He told of Virādha's slaying and of how Śarabhaṅga gave up his body.
Then he described Sutīkṣṇa's love, and the Lord's time in the holy company of Agastya. ॥65॥
uttar.66.cau1: The hallowing of the Daṇḍaka forest he told next, and then sang of the bond of friendship with the vulture.
Then the Lord made his dwelling at Pañcavaṭī and ended the dread of all the sages. ॥1॥
uttar.66.cau2: Next came the peerless teaching given to Lakṣmaṇa, and how Śūrpaṇakhā was disfigured.
After that he described the slaying of Khara and Dūṣaṇa, and how Rāvaṇa came to learn the whole secret. ॥2॥
uttar.66.cau3: The talk between Rāvaṇa and Mārīca, and how it went, he told in full.
Then came the carrying off of the illusory Sītā, and something of Śrī Rāma's grief in separation. ॥3॥
uttar.66.cau4: He told how the Lord performed the vulture's last rites, and how he slew Kabandha and gave Śabarī the blessed state.
Then he told how Śrī Rāma, voicing his grief of separation, went to the shore of the lake. ॥4॥
uttar.66.do66क: He told of the Lord's talk with Nārada and of the meeting with Hanumān, son of the Wind;
then of the friendship with Sugrīva and the ending of Vāli's life. ॥66 (क)॥
uttar.66.do66ख: He told how, after anointing Sugrīva king, the Lord lived on Mount Pravarṣaṇa.
Then came the description of the rains and of autumn, Śrī Rāma's anger and the monkey king's fear. ॥66 (ख)॥
uttar.67.cau1: He told how the king of the monkeys dispatched his monkeys and they hurried off to all the quarters to search for Sītā;
how they went into the cavern, and how the monkeys then met Sampāti. ॥1॥
uttar.67.cau2: He told how Hanumān, son of the Wind, heard the whole story and leapt across the boundless ocean;
how he entered Laṅkā, and then how he gave Sītā courage. ॥2॥
uttar.67.cau3: He laid waste the grove, counselled Rāvaṇa, burnt the city and leapt back over the ocean.
All the monkeys came to where Śrī Rāma was and brought him word that Sītā was well. ॥3॥
uttar.67.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma went with the army and camped on the ocean shore;
he told how Vibhīṣaṇa came and met him, and the story of the subduing of the ocean. ॥4॥
uttar.67.do67क: He told how the monkey army built the bridge and crossed to the far side of the ocean,
and how Aṅgada, Vāli's son, finest of heroes, went as envoy. ॥67 (क)॥
uttar.67.do67ख: He described in many ways the fighting between demons and monkeys,
and the might and prowess of Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda, and their end. ॥67 (ख)॥
