uttar.68.cau1: He told of the many ways the hordes of demons died, and of the battle between Śrī Rāma and Rāvaṇa;
of Rāvaṇa's death, Mandodarī's grief, Vibhīṣaṇa's kingship and the gods freed from sorrow. ॥1॥
uttar.68.cau2: Then came Sītā's reunion with Śrī Rāma, and the gods praising him with joined palms.
Then the Lord, the home of grace, mounted the Puṣpaka with the monkeys and set out for Ayodhyā. ॥2॥
uttar.68.cau3: The crow sang all the bright deeds of how Śrī Rāma came back to his own city.
Then he told of Śrī Rāma's coronation, and in describing the city spoke of many points of royal policy. ॥3॥
uttar.68.cau4: Kākabhuśuṇḍi told the whole story at length, Bhavānī, just as I have told it to you.
Having heard all of Śrī Rāma's story, Garuḍa spoke, his heart overflowing with joy: ॥4॥
uttar.68.so68क: My doubt is gone; I have heard all the deeds of Śrī Rāma.
By your grace, O jewel among crows, love for Śrī Rāma's feet has come to me. ॥68 (क)॥
uttar.68.so68ख: When I saw the Lord bound in battle, a great delusion came over me:
Śrī Rāma is the very mass of consciousness and bliss; why then should he be distressed? ॥68 (ख)॥
uttar.69.cau1: When I saw deeds so entirely like a man's, a heavy doubt arose in my heart.
That very error I now take as a kindness to me; it was a favour shown me by the treasury of mercy. ॥1॥
uttar.69.cau2: Only one who is sorely tormented by the sun's heat knows the comfort of a tree's shade.
Had I not been so deeply deluded, dear sir, how could I ever have met you? ॥2॥
uttar.69.cau3: And how could I have heard this lovely and most wondrous story of Śrī Hari, which you have sung in so many ways?
This is the teaching of the Vedas, the Āgamas and the Purāṇas, and the siddhas and sages declare it without doubt: ॥3॥
uttar.69.cau4: Pure saints are met only by the one on whom Śrī Rāma looks with grace.
By Śrī Rāma's grace I have seen you, and by your kindness every doubt has left me. ॥4॥
uttar.69.do69क: The crow heard the words of the king of birds, full of humility and love.
His body thrilled, his eyes filled with tears, and his heart rejoiced greatly. ॥69 (क)॥
uttar.69.do69ख: A listener of good sense, gentle nature and purity, who loves the story and serves Śrī Hari:
finding such a one, Umā, the good reveal even what is most secret. ॥69 (ख)॥
uttar.70.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi, whose love for the lord of birds was no small thing, spoke again:
In every respect, my lord, you are to be revered by me, for you enjoy the grace of Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
uttar.70.cau2: You have no doubt, no delusion, no māyā; my lord, it is you who have been kind to me.
Śrī Rāma made delusion the excuse for sending you, king of birds, and so did me honour. ॥2॥
uttar.70.cau3: King of birds, you have told me of your delusion; there is nothing strange in that, my lord.
Nārada, Śiva, Brahmā, Sanaka and the others, foremost of sages who know the Self: ॥3॥
uttar.70.cau4: Whom among them has delusion not blinded? Who in the world has not been made to dance by desire?
Whom has craving not driven mad? Whose heart has anger not scorched? ॥4॥
uttar.70.do70क: The wise, the ascetic, the hero, the poet, the learned, the storehouse of virtues:
which of them in this world has greed not made a mockery of? ॥70 (क)॥
uttar.70.do70ख: Whom has the pride of wealth not twisted? Whom has power not made deaf?
Who is there whom the arrows of a doe-eyed woman's glance have not struck? ॥70 (ख)॥
uttar.71.cau1: Who has not suffered the delirium that the guṇas (the qualities of nature) bring on? Pride and arrogance have let no one go entirely free.
Whom has the fever of youth not driven wild? Whose good name has attachment not ruined? ॥1॥
uttar.71.cau2: Whom has envy not stained? Whom has the wind of grief not shaken?
Whom has the serpent of anxiety not devoured? Who in the world has escaped the grip of māyā? ॥2॥
uttar.71.cau3: Desire is a woodworm and the body is timber; who is so steadfast that this worm has not got into him?
The three cravings, for sons, for wealth and for standing in the world: whose mind have they not sullied? ॥3॥
uttar.71.cau4: All this is the family of māyā, mighty and measureless; who can describe it to the end?
Śiva and four-faced Brahmā themselves fear her; how should other beings count for anything? ॥4॥
uttar.71.do71क: Throughout the world spreads the fierce army of māyā.
Desire and its kin are its generals; hypocrisy, deceit and sham piety are its warriors. ॥71 (क)॥
uttar.71.do71ख: That māyā is the handmaid of Śrī Rāma; once understood, she too is unreal.
Yet without Śrī Rāma's grace she does not let go; I say this, my lord, with my foot set firm. ॥71 (ख)॥
uttar.72.cau1: The māyā that sets the whole world dancing, whose ways no one has been able to discern:
that same māyā, Garuḍa, at a mere play of the Lord's brows, dances like a dancing-girl, her whole retinue with her. ॥1॥
uttar.72.cau2: He is Śrī Rāma, the very substance of being, consciousness and bliss, unborn, realised knowledge itself, the abode of beauty and strength.
He pervades all and is all that is pervaded; he is undivided, endless, complete, the Lord whose power never fails. ॥2॥
uttar.72.cau3: He is beyond the guṇas, vast, beyond speech and the senses, all-seeing, without blemish, unconquered;
free of attachment, formless, free of delusion, eternal, stainless, a mass of bliss. ॥3॥
uttar.72.cau4: He is beyond Nature, the Lord who dwells in every heart, Brahman, desireless, stainless, imperishable.
There is no ground for delusion here; can darkness ever go before the sun? ॥4॥
uttar.72.do72क: For his devotees' sake the Lord, Śrī Rāma, took the body of a king,
and performed supremely sanctifying deeds, just like an ordinary man. ॥72 (क)॥
uttar.72.do72ख: As an actor puts on many guises and dances,
showing the feeling proper to each, yet does not himself become any of them, ॥72 (ख)॥
uttar.73.cau1: Such, Garuḍa, is the play of Śrī Rāma: it bewilders the demons and gives joy to his people.
Those whose minds are soiled, who are slaves to the senses and full of lust, ascribe delusion to the Lord in this way, my master. ॥1॥
uttar.73.cau2: When someone's eyes become diseased, he says the moon is yellow.
When someone is confused about direction, Garuḍa, he says the sun has risen in the west. ॥2॥
uttar.73.cau3: One sitting in a boat sees the world moving, and in his delusion takes himself to be still.
Children spin round, the houses and the rest do not, yet they call one another liars. ॥3॥
uttar.73.cau4: Delusion said of Śrī Hari is just like this, Garuḍa; not even in a dream is there any room for ignorance in him.
But those who are in māyā's grip, dull of mind and luckless, with many kinds of veil over their hearts, ॥4॥
uttar.73.cau5: those fools, out of obstinacy, raise doubts and lay their own ignorance on Śrī Rāma. ॥5॥
uttar.73.do73क: Those given to desire, anger, pride and greed, clinging to the home, which is sorrow itself,
how can they know Śrī Rāma? The fools lie fallen in a well of darkness. ॥73 (क)॥
uttar.73.do73ख: The attributeless form is very easy to reach, but the form with attributes no one knows.
Hearing of his many deeds, some easy to grasp and some beyond grasping, the minds of sages are thrown into confusion. ॥73 (ख)॥
uttar.74.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: as far as my understanding goes I shall tell the lovely story of Śrī Rāma's lordship.
And how I myself fell into delusion, my lord, that whole story too I shall relate to you. ॥1॥
uttar.74.cau2: Dear one, you are a vessel of Śrī Rāma's grace; you love the virtues of Śrī Hari, and you give me joy.
So I hide nothing from you, and I sing of a supreme and charming secret. ॥2॥
uttar.74.cau3: Hear the innate nature of Śrī Rāma: he never lets pride remain in one who is his.
Pride is the root of the round of births; it brings pains of many kinds and every sorrow. ॥3॥
uttar.74.cau4: So the treasury of mercy takes it away, for his tender care for his servant is very great.
Just as, my lord, when a sore forms on a child's body, the mother has it lanced as if she were hard-hearted. ॥4॥
uttar.74.do74क: Though at first the child is hurt and cries, unable to bear it,
the mother, intent on ending the disease, does not count the child's pain. ॥74 (क)॥
uttar.74.do74ख: In the same way Śrī Rāma takes away his servant's pride for his good.
Tulasīdāsa, why do you not cast off error and worship such a Lord? ॥74 (ख)॥
uttar.75.cau1: Listen with all your mind, Garuḍa, as I tell of Śrī Rāma's grace and my own folly.
Whenever Śrī Rāma takes a human body and plays out many sports for his devotees, ॥1॥
uttar.75.cau2: then I go to the city of Ayodhyā and rejoice to watch his childhood play.
I go and see the great festival of his birth, and, captivated, stay there for five years. ॥2॥
uttar.75.cau3: Śrī Rāma as a child is my chosen deity; his body holds the beauty of a thousand million Kāmadevas.
Gazing and gazing at my Lord's face, Garuḍa, I make my eyes fulfil their purpose. ॥3॥
uttar.75.cau4: Taking the form of a small crow, I stay with Śrī Hari and watch his childhood play in all its colours. ॥4॥
uttar.75.do75क: Wherever he roams as a child, I fly along with him;
and the leftovers that drop in the courtyard I gather up and eat. ॥75 (क)॥
uttar.75.do75ख: Once Śrī Rāma played out all his sports to the utmost.
As he recalled that play of the Lord, Kākabhuśuṇḍi's body thrilled with joy. ॥75 (ख)॥
uttar.76.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, Garuḍa; the story of Śrī Rāma gives joy to his servants.
The king's palace is beautiful in every way, inlaid with gold and jewels of many kinds. ॥1॥
uttar.76.cau2: The lovely courtyard where the four brothers play every day is beyond description.
Śrī Rāma moves about the courtyard at his childish games, a joy to his mother. ॥2॥
uttar.76.cau3: His soft body is dark like an emerald, and every limb holds the beauty of many Kāmadevas.
His feet, soft and red as a new lotus, have lovely toes, whose nails take away the moon's lustre. ॥3॥
uttar.76.cau4: On them are four charming marks, the thunderbolt and the rest, and lovely anklets that tinkle sweetly.
Round his waist a pretty girdle of bells, finely made of gold and gems, chimes sweetly and looks lovely. ॥4॥
uttar.76.do76: On the belly are three lovely lines, and the navel is beautiful and deep.
On his broad chest shine a child's ornaments and clothes of many kinds. ॥76॥
uttar.77.cau1: His rosy palms, nails and fingers are charming, and lovely ornaments adorn his long arms.
His shoulders are a lion cub's, his neck like a conch; his chin is lovely and his face the very limit of beauty. ॥1॥
uttar.77.cau2: His speech is a lisping babble, his lips are red, and he has two and two little teeth, bright and fine.
His cheeks are charming, his nose is lovely, and his smile, like the moon's rays, delights everyone. ॥2॥
uttar.77.cau3: His eyes, like blue lotuses, set one free from worldly existence; a tilak of gorocana shines on his forehead.
His brows are arched, his ears even and lovely, and his dark curling locks spread their beauty. ॥3॥
uttar.77.cau4: A fine yellow frock looks lovely on him; his gleeful cries and his glances delight me.
That treasure of beauty plays in the king's courtyard and dances as he gazes at his own reflection, ॥4॥
uttar.77.cau5: and plays with me in many ways, which I am deeply ashamed to describe.
When he runs crowing with delight to catch me, I fly off, and then he shows me a sweet cake. ॥5॥
uttar.77.do77क: When I come near, the Lord laughs; when I fly away, he cries.
When I go near to take hold of his feet, he looks back at me again and again as he runs away. ॥77 (क)॥
uttar.77.do77ख: When I saw him at play just as any ordinary child plays, delusion took hold of me:
what sort of acts is the Lord performing, he who is the very mass of consciousness and bliss? ॥77 (ख)॥
uttar.78.cau1: The moment I let this much into my mind, Garuḍa, māyā, sent by Śrī Rāma, came over me.
Yet that māyā brought me no pain, nor did it bind me to the round of births as it does other beings. ॥1॥
uttar.78.cau2: My lord, there is another reason here; listen to it with care, mount of Hari.
Unbroken knowledge is Sītā's Lord alone; all beings, moving and unmoving, are in māyā's power. ॥2॥
uttar.78.cau3: If everyone's knowledge stayed ever the same, tell me, how could one speak of a difference between God and the soul?
The soul, full of pride, is subject to māyā; and māyā, the mine of the guṇas, is subject to God. ॥3॥
uttar.78.cau4: The soul is dependent, the Lord is his own master; souls are many, the Lord of Lakṣmī is one.
This difference is māyā's making and unreal, yet it will not go without Śrī Hari, though one try ten million means. ॥4॥
uttar.78.do78क: One who seeks liberation without worship of Śrī Rāma,
is a beast without tail or horns, even if he is a man of knowledge. ॥78 (क)॥
uttar.78.do78ख: Let the full moon rise in all its sixteen digits with the whole host of stars,
and let every mountain be set ablaze with forest fire: without the sun the night does not go. ॥78 (ख)॥
uttar.79.cau1: In the same way, Garuḍa, without worship of Śrī Hari the suffering of living beings does not end.
Ignorance does not take hold of Śrī Hari's servant; knowledge, sent by the Lord, takes hold of him. ॥1॥
uttar.79.cau2: So the servant is never lost, best of birds; his devotion, in which he stays distinct from the Lord, grows.
Śrī Rāma saw me bewildered by error and smiled; hear that special play. ॥2॥
uttar.79.cau3: No one grasped the secret of that sport, not his younger brothers, not his mother or father.
Dark of body, with rosy hands and feet, he ran on hands and knees to catch me. ॥3॥
uttar.79.cau4: Then I fled, Garuḍa, and Śrī Rāma stretched out his arm to seize me.
However far I flew into the sky, there I saw Śrī Hari's arm beside me. ॥4॥
uttar.79.do79क: I went as far as Brahmā's world, and as I flew I looked behind me:
between Śrī Rāma's arm and me, dear one, there were only two finger-breadths. ॥79 (क)॥
uttar.79.do79ख: Piercing the seven coverings, as far as I had power to go,
there I went, and seeing the Lord's arm there, I was again thrown into distress. ॥79 (ख)॥
uttar.80.cau1: When terror seized me I shut my eyes; looking again, I found I had come to Kosalapura.
Seeing me, Śrī Rāma smiled, and as he laughed I passed at once into his mouth. ॥1॥
uttar.80.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: within his belly I saw universes in great multitudes.
There were many worlds, most wonderful, each more finely made than the last. ॥2॥
uttar.80.cau3: I saw Brahmās and Śivas by the million, and stars, suns and moons beyond counting,
guardians of the worlds, Yamas and Kālas beyond counting, mountains beyond counting and vast lands, ॥3॥
uttar.80.cau4: boundless oceans, rivers, lakes and forests, and creation spread out in many forms;
gods, sages, siddhas, nāgas, men and kinnaras, and beings of the four kinds, moving and unmoving. ॥4॥
uttar.80.do80क: What was never seen or heard of, what the mind itself cannot hold:
all that marvel I saw; how could it be described? ॥80 (क)॥
uttar.80.do80ख: In each universe I stayed a hundred years,
and in this way I roamed on, seeing many a cosmic egg. ॥80 (ख)॥
uttar.81.cau1: Each world had its own Brahmā, and its own Viṣṇu, Śiva, Manu and guardians of the quarters.
Men, gandharvas, ghosts, vetālas, kinnaras, demons, beasts, birds and serpents were different there too. ॥1॥
uttar.81.cau2: There were hosts of gods and dānavas of many kinds as well; every living being there was of another sort.
Earth, rivers, oceans, lakes and many mountains: the whole of creation there was altogether different. ॥2॥
uttar.81.cau3: In every universe I saw a form of my own, and many kinds of incomparable things.
Each world had an Ayodhyā of its own, a different Sarayū, and different men and women. ॥3॥
uttar.81.cau4: Listen, dear one: Daśaratha, Kausalyā, and the brothers Bharata and the rest appeared in many different forms.
In every universe Śrī Rāma had come down as an incarnation, and I watched his boundless childhood play. ॥4॥
uttar.81.do81क: Garuḍa, I saw everything different from world to world, and exceedingly wonderful.
I roamed through countless worlds, but nowhere did I see the Lord Śrī Rāma any different. ॥81 (क)॥
uttar.81.do81ख: The same childhood, the same beauty, the same compassionate Śrī Rāma.
Driven by the wind of delusion, I went on from world to world, seeing this. ॥81 (ख)॥
uttar.82.cau1: As I wandered through many universes, a hundred aeons seemed to pass.
Roaming on and on, I reached my own hermitage, and there again I spent some time. ॥1॥
uttar.82.cau2: When I heard that my Lord had been born in Ayodhyā, I rose and ran, brimming with love and full of joy.
I went and saw the great festival of his birth, just as I sang of it to you before. ॥2॥
uttar.82.cau3: In Śrī Rāma's belly I saw many worlds; they could only be seen, never described.
There, too, I saw Śrī Rāma once more, the all-knowing, the master of māyā, the compassionate Lord. ॥3॥
uttar.82.cau4: I pondered it again and again, but my mind was clogged with the mire of delusion.
All this I saw within two ghaṛīs (under an hour), and with a deep delusion in my mind I was bewildered. ॥4॥
uttar.82.do82क: Seeing me so distressed, the compassionate Śrī Rāma then laughed.
Listen, steady-minded one: as soon as he laughed, I found myself outside his mouth. ॥82 (क)॥
uttar.82.do82ख: Śrī Rāma began once more to play the same childish games with me.
I reasoned with my mind in countless ways, but it found no rest. ॥82 (ख)॥
uttar.83.cau1: Seeing this play, and grasping that majesty, I forgot the state of my body.
I fell to the ground, unable to speak a word but this: Save me, save me, protector of those in distress! ॥1॥
uttar.83.cau2: The Lord saw me overcome with love, and then he held back the power of his māyā.
The Lord laid his lotus hand on my head, and he who is kind to the lowly took away all my sorrow. ॥2॥
uttar.83.cau3: Śrī Rāma freed me from delusion, he who gives joy to his servants and is a mass of grace.
Thinking over and over of the majesty I had seen before, I felt immense joy in my heart. ॥3॥
uttar.83.cau4: Seeing the Lord's tender love for his devotees, a special love welled up in my heart.
With tears in my eyes, thrilling all over, and with joined palms, I then prayed to him in many ways. ॥4॥
uttar.83.do83क: Hearing my words full of love, and seeing his own servant so humble,
the Lord, abode of Lakṣmī, spoke words that were gentle, deep and full of comfort: ॥83 (क)॥
uttar.83.do83ख: Kākabhuśuṇḍi, know that I am greatly pleased, and ask for a boon:
the siddhis such as aṇimā, other riches, liberation, the mine of all joys, ॥83 (ख)॥
uttar.84.cau1: knowledge, discernment, dispassion, realised knowledge, and the many virtues in the world that even sages find hard to attain:
all this I will give you today, without a doubt; ask for whatever your heart desires. ॥1॥
uttar.84.cau2: Hearing the Lord's words, I was filled with still greater love, and I began to reason in my mind.
The Lord has truly offered to give every joy, but he has not spoken of giving his own devotion. ॥2॥
uttar.84.cau3: Without devotion, every virtue and every joy is like a spread of dishes without salt.
Of what use is joy without worship? Thinking this, Garuḍa, I said: ॥3॥
uttar.84.cau4: My Lord, if you are pleased and would give me a boon, and if you show me grace and love,
then, my master, I ask for the boon my heart longs for; you are generous, and you know what lies within the heart. ॥4॥
uttar.84.do84क: That unbroken, pure devotion to you which the Vedas and Purāṇas sing of,
which great yogīs and sages seek, and which only a rare one finds by the Lord's grace, ॥84 (क)॥
uttar.84.do84ख: O wish-granting tree of the devotees, friend of all who bow to you, ocean of mercy, home of joy,
O Rāma, my Lord, in your mercy give me that same devotion to you. ॥84 (ख)॥
uttar.85.cau1: Saying evamastu (so be it), Śrī Rāma spoke words that gave the greatest joy:
Listen, crow: you are wise by nature; why would you not ask for such a boon? ॥1॥
uttar.85.cau2: You have asked for devotion, the mine of all joys; no one in the world is as fortunate as you.
Sages who burn their bodies in the fire of japa and yoga do not attain it with millions of efforts. ॥2॥
uttar.85.cau3: I am delighted to see your wisdom; your asking for devotion pleased me greatly.
Listen, bird: by my grace all good qualities will now dwell in your heart. ॥3॥
uttar.85.cau4: Devotion, knowledge, realised knowledge, dispassion, yoga, my deeds, their secrets and their divisions:
you will know the distinctions of them all, by my grace, without the toil of spiritual practice. ॥4॥
uttar.85.do85क: None of the delusions born of māyā will touch you now.
Know me to be Brahman, who has no beginning and no birth, who is free of the guṇas, and in whom all virtues are stored. ॥85 (क)॥
uttar.85.do85ख: Devotees are always dear to me. Listen, crow: bearing this in mind,
keep an unshakable love for my feet in body, speech and mind. ॥85 (ख)॥
uttar.86.cau1: Now hear my words, supremely pure, true and easy to grasp, set forth by the Vedas and other scriptures.
I tell you my own settled truth: listen, hold it in your mind, and leaving all else, worship me. ॥1॥
uttar.86.cau2: The world springs from my māyā, and in it live beings of every kind, moving and unmoving.
All are dear to me, all are created by me; but humans please me more than all. ॥2॥
uttar.86.cau3: Among them, the twice-born; among the twice-born, those who hold the Vedas; among those, the ones who follow the dharma of the Vedas;
among them the dispassionate are dear to me, then the wise, and dearer still than the wise are those of realised knowledge. ॥3॥
uttar.86.cau4: Dearer to me than them is my own servant, whose refuge is in me alone, with no other hope.
I tell you the truth again and again: no one is as dear to me as my servant. ॥4॥
uttar.86.cau5: One without devotion, be he Brahmā himself, is only as dear to me as any other being.
But a creature with devotion, even the lowliest, is dear to me as life: this is my word. ॥5॥
uttar.86.do86: Tell me, to whom is a servant who is pure, good-natured and right-minded not dear?
The Vedas and Purāṇas state this rule; listen carefully, crow. ॥86॥
uttar.87.cau1: A father may have many sons, each of a different nature, temperament and conduct.
One is learned, one an ascetic, one a knower; one wealthy, one brave, one generous; ॥1॥
uttar.87.cau2: one knows everything, one is devoted to dharma; the father's love for all of them is the same.
But one son is devoted to his father in word, thought and deed, and knows no other duty even in a dream. ॥2॥
uttar.87.cau3: That son is as dear to his father as his own life, though he may be ignorant in every way.
In the same way, all beings, moving and unmoving, with the animals, gods, humans and asuras among them, ॥3॥
uttar.87.cau4: this whole universe is my making, and my mercy rests equally on all.
But whoever among them gives up pride and māyā and worships me in mind, speech and body, ॥4॥
uttar.87.do87क: be it a man, one who is neither man nor woman, a woman, or any being, moving or unmoving,
whoever worships me with their whole being, free of deceit, is supremely dear to me. ॥87 (क)॥
uttar.87.so87ख: I tell you the truth, bird: a pure servant is as dear to me as life.
Bearing this in mind, give up every other hope and reliance, and worship me. ॥87 (ख)॥
uttar.88.cau1: Time will never have power over you; remember me and worship me without ceasing.
I could not have enough of hearing the Lord's nectar-like words; my body thrilled and my heart was overjoyed. ॥1॥
uttar.88.cau2: That joy only the mind and the ears know; the tongue cannot describe it.
The joy of the Lord's beauty the eyes know, but how could they tell it? They have no speech. ॥2॥
uttar.88.cau3: Having taught me in many ways and given me joy, the Lord began again the same childish play.
With tears in his eyes and a somewhat sulky face, he looked at his mother, as though very hungry. ॥3॥
uttar.88.cau4: Seeing it, the mother rose anxiously and ran to him, and with tender words held him to her breast.
Keeping him in her lap she gave him milk to drink, singing the charming deeds of Śrī Rāma. ॥4॥
uttar.88.so88क: The joy for which Śiva, the enemy of Tripura, auspicious and the giver of joy, took on an inauspicious guise
is the joy in which the men and women of Ayodhyā are ever immersed. ॥88 (क)॥
uttar.88.so88ख: Those who have once, even in a dream, tasted the merest trace of that joy,
good and wise souls, Garuḍa, count even the bliss of Brahman as nothing. ॥88 (ख)॥
uttar.89.cau1: Then I stayed in Ayodhyā for some time and watched the Lord's delightful childhood play.
By Śrī Rāma's grace I received the boon of devotion, and bowing at the Lord's feet I came back to my own hermitage. ॥1॥
uttar.89.cau2: Māyā has had no hold on me ever since Śrī Rāma made me his own.
I have sung to you this whole secret story of how Śrī Hari's māyā made me dance. ॥2॥
uttar.89.cau3: Now, Garuḍa, I tell you what I have known myself: without worship of Śrī Hari, afflictions do not go.
Listen, king of birds: Śrī Rāma's greatness cannot be known without his grace. ॥3॥
uttar.89.cau4: Without knowing it there is no faith, and without faith there is no love.
Without love, Garuḍa, devotion never grows firm, just as water leaves no smoothness that stays. ॥4॥
uttar.89.so89क: Can there be knowledge without a guru? Can there be knowledge without dispassion?
The Vedas and Purāṇas proclaim it: can joy be found without devotion to Śrī Hari? ॥89 (क)॥
uttar.89.so89ख: Dear one, can anyone find rest without a natural contentment?
Try millions of means and wear yourself out to the point of death: will a boat ever move without water? ॥89 (ख)॥
uttar.90.cau1: Without contentment desires do not perish, and while desire remains there is no happiness, not even in a dream.
Can desires be ended without the worship of Śrī Rāma? Does a tree ever grow where there is no ground? ॥1॥
uttar.90.cau2: Does evenness of mind come without realised knowledge? Can anyone find room without the sky?
Without faith there is no dharma; can anyone find scent without the earth? ॥2॥
uttar.90.cau3: Does splendour spread without austerity? Without water, could the world have any taste?
Is good conduct found without serving the wise? No more, master, than there is form without light. ॥3॥
uttar.90.cau4: Does the mind grow steady without the joy of the self? Can there be touch without air?
Is any accomplishment won without faith? Just so, without the worship of Śrī Hari the fear of worldly existence does not end. ॥4॥
uttar.90.do90क: Without faith there is no devotion, and without devotion Śrī Rāma's heart does not melt.
Without Śrī Rāma's grace a living being finds no rest, not even in a dream. ॥90 (क)॥
uttar.90.so90ख: Considering this, O steady of mind, cast off all sophistry and doubt,
and worship Śrī Rāma, a mine of compassion, beautiful, the giver of joy. ॥90 (ख)॥
uttar.91.cau1: My lord Garuḍa, I have sung the majesty and glory of the Lord as far as my understanding goes.
I have said nothing by way of any special contrivance; all this I have seen with my own eyes. ॥1॥
uttar.91.cau2: Glory, name, form and the tale of virtues: all are boundless, and Śrī Rāma himself is without end.
The sages sing Śrī Hari's virtues each as far as his mind reaches; the Vedas, Śeṣa and Śiva do not find their end. ॥2॥
uttar.91.cau3: Every winged creature, from you down to the mosquito, flies through the sky, yet none reaches its end.
So too, dear one, the glory of Śrī Rāma is fathomless: has anyone ever touched its bottom? ॥3॥
uttar.91.cau4: Śrī Rāma's body is as lovely as a thousand million Kāmadevas; like countless millions of Durgās he crushes his foes.
His pomp and pleasure equal those of a thousand million Indras; his expanse is boundless as a thousand million skies. ॥4॥
uttar.91.do91क: He has the vast strength of a thousand million winds and the light of a thousand million suns.
He is cool as a thousand million moons, and he stills every terror of worldly existence. ॥91 (क)॥
uttar.91.do91ख: Like a thousand million Deaths he is exceedingly hard to overcome, hard to approach, without end.
Like a thousand million comets the Lord is not to be withstood. ॥91 (ख)॥
uttar.92.cau1: The Lord is fathomless as a thousand million nether worlds, and fearsome as a thousand million Yamas.
He purifies like countless millions of holy places; his name destroys the whole heap of sins. ॥1॥
uttar.92.cau2: Śrī Rāma is unshakeable as ten million Himālayas and deep as a thousand million oceans.
Like a thousand million wish-fulfilling cows, the Lord grants every desire. ॥2॥
uttar.92.cau3: His skill is that of countless millions of Sarasvatīs, his craft in creation that of a thousand million Brahmās.
He sustains like ten million Viṣṇus and destroys like a thousand million Rudras. ॥3॥
uttar.92.cau4: He is wealthy as a thousand million Kuberas, and like ten million Māyās a storehouse of the world's display.
In bearing the load he is like a thousand million Śeṣas; the Lord of the world is limitless and beyond compare. ॥4॥
uttar.92.cha1: He is beyond compare; there is no other to liken him to; Śrī Rāma is like Śrī Rāma alone, the Vedas say.
Just as the sun, when called the equal of a thousand million fireflies, is only made very small,
so the great sages extol Śrī Hari each by the play of his own mind;
and the Lord, who values the feeling and is most merciful, hears it with love and is pleased. ॥1॥
uttar.92.do92क: Śrī Rāma is an ocean of boundless virtues; can anyone find its bottom?
What I heard from the saints, just as I heard it, I have told you. ॥92 (क)॥
uttar.92.so92ख: The Lord is won by heartfelt feeling; he is a treasury of joy, a home of compassion.
Casting off attachment, pride and self-regard, one should always worship the beloved of Sītā. ॥92 (ख)॥
uttar.93.cau1: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's lovely words, Garuḍa rejoiced and fluffed out his wings.
Tears filled his eyes, his heart was overjoyed, and he took Śrī Rāma's majesty into his heart. ॥1॥
uttar.93.cau2: Understanding his earlier delusion, he repented that he had taken the beginningless Brahman for a man.
Over and over he laid his head at the feet of the crow, whom he now knew to be like Śrī Rāma, and his love for him grew. ॥2॥
uttar.93.cau3: Without a guru no one crosses the ocean of worldly existence, not even one as great as Brahmā and Śiva.
Garuḍa said: Dear one, the snake of doubt had bitten me, and waves of sophistry rose upon me in painful throngs. ॥3॥
uttar.93.cau4: Śrī Rāma, giver of joy to his own, became the snake-charmer in your form and brought me back to life.
By your grace my delusion has perished, and I have come to know the peerless secret of Śrī Rāma. ॥4॥
uttar.93.do93क: Having praised him in many ways, bowing his head with folded hands,
Garuḍa spoke again in humble, loving and gentle words: ॥93 (क)॥
uttar.93.do93ख: My lord and master, it is from my own want of discernment that I ask you.
Ocean of mercy, think of me as your own servant and tell me with kindly care. ॥93 (ख)॥
uttar.94.cau1: You know all things and know the truth; you are beyond darkness, wise, gentle and simple in conduct.
You are the dwelling of knowledge, dispassion and realised knowledge, and a dear servant of Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
uttar.94.cau2: For what reason did you receive this body? Dear one, explain it all to me.
Master, you who range the sky, tell me where you found this lovely lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds. ॥2॥
uttar.94.cau3: My lord, I heard from Śiva that even in the great dissolution you do not perish.
Śiva, the Lord, never speaks idle words; and this too is a doubt in my mind. ॥3॥
uttar.94.cau4: Beings moving and unmoving, nāgas, men and gods: my lord, the whole world is a morning meal for Kāla, Time.
Kāla, who dissolves countless universes, is always mighty, and no one can pass beyond him. ॥4॥
uttar.94.so94क: What is the reason that Kāla, so very terrible, has no hold on you?
Tell me that, compassionate one: is it the power of knowledge or the strength of yoga? ॥94 (क)॥
uttar.94.do94ख: My lord, the moment I came to your hermitage my delusion and error fled.
What is the reason for that, my lord? Tell me all of it with love. ॥94 (ख)॥
uttar.95.cau1: Umā, hearing Garuḍa's words Kākabhuśuṇḍi rejoiced and spoke with the deepest love:
Blessed, blessed is your understanding, Garuḍa. Your question is very dear to me. ॥1॥
uttar.95.cau2: Hearing your loving, lovely question, the memory of many births has come back to me.
I will tell you my whole story in song; dear one, listen with reverence and with your mind on it. ॥2॥
uttar.95.cau3: Repetition of the Name, austerity, sacrifice, calm of mind, restraint of the senses, vows, gifts, dispassion, discernment, yoga and realised knowledge:
the fruit of them all is love for the feet of Śrī Rāma, and without it no one finds well-being. ॥3॥
uttar.95.cau4: In this very body I gained devotion to Śrī Rāma, and so I feel great attachment to it.
Everyone feels attachment for that which serves some purpose of his own. ॥4॥
uttar.95.so95क: Garuḍa, this is a rule of conduct approved by the Veda, and the good say it too:
love even the very lowly when you know them to be for your highest good. ॥95 (क)॥
uttar.95.so95ख: Silk comes from a worm, and from silk comes beautiful silken cloth;
so everyone tends that worm as dearly as life, though it is utterly impure. ॥95 (ख)॥
uttar.96.cau1: This is the true self-interest of a living being: love for Śrī Rāma's feet in thought, deed and word.
Holy and fair is that body alone which, once received, is spent in the worship of Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
uttar.96.cau2: One turned away from Śrī Rāma may gain a body like Brahmā's, yet poets and the learned do not praise him.
In this body devotion to Śrī Rāma sprang up in my heart; therefore, master, it is supremely dear to me. ॥2॥
uttar.96.cau3: I do not leave this body, though my death is at my own will, for the Vedas tell of no worship without a body.
Delusion first brought me to great ruin; turned away from Śrī Rāma, I never once slept in peace. ॥3॥
uttar.96.cau4: Through many births I did many kinds of works besides: yoga, repetition of the Name, austerity, sacrifice and gifts.
What womb is there in which I was not born, Garuḍa, as I wandered and wandered through the world? ॥4॥
uttar.96.cau5: Master, I tried every kind of work and saw what came of it, but I was never as happy as I am now.
My lord, I remember many births; by Śiva's grace delusion did not close round my mind. ॥5॥
uttar.96.do96क: Now I will tell the story of my first birth; listen, Garuḍa.
Hearing it, love for the Lord's feet springs up, and by that every affliction is ended. ॥96 (क)॥
uttar.96.do96ख: My lord, in a former kalpa there was an age, the Kali age, the root of all impurity.
Men and women alike were bent on unrighteousness, and all of them went against the Veda. ॥96 (ख)॥
uttar.97.cau1: In that Kali age I went to the city of Kosala and was born there, taking the body of a śūdra.
I served Śiva in thought, deed and word, reviled the other gods, and was proud. ॥1॥
uttar.97.cau2: Drunk with the pride of wealth, I was a great talker, harsh of mind, with vast hypocrisy in my heart.
Though I lived in the capital of Śrī Rāma, I knew nothing then of its glory. ॥2॥
uttar.97.cau3: Now I know the power of Avadh. The Vedas, the Āgamas and the Purāṇas sing that
whoever lives in Avadh, in any birth, is bound to become devoted to Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
uttar.97.cau4: A living being knows the power of Avadh only when Śrī Rāma, bow in hand, dwells in his heart.
That Kali age was a hard one, Garuḍa; all men and women were given over to sin. ॥4॥
uttar.97.do97क: The impurity of Kali had swallowed every dharma, and the true scriptures had vanished.
Hypocrites, inventing out of their own minds, had brought forth many sects. ॥97 (क)॥
uttar.97.do97ख: All the people had fallen under delusion, and greed had swallowed good works.
Listen, mount of Hari, treasury of knowledge: I will tell you a little of the ways of the Kali age. ॥97 (ख)॥
uttar.98.cau1: The dharma of the varṇas is gone, and so are the four stages of life; all men and women are bent on opposing the Vedas.
Brahmins sell the Vedas, kings devour their subjects, and no one heeds the command of the Vedas. ॥1॥
uttar.98.cau2: The path is whatever pleases each one; the learned man is he who brags.
Whoever is given to false show and hypocrisy is called a saint by all. ॥2॥
uttar.98.cau3: The clever man is he who seizes another's wealth; the one who practises hypocrisy is the great observer of right conduct.
Whoever tells lies and knows how to jest is praised as gifted in the Kali age. ॥3॥
uttar.98.cau4: One who has no right conduct and has left the path of the Vedas is, in the Kali age, both the wise man and the man of dispassion.
The famous ascetic of the Kali age is the one whose nails and matted locks have grown long. ॥4॥
uttar.98.do98क: Those who wear inauspicious garb and ornaments and eat whatever is fit or unfit to be eaten,
they are the yogis, they the siddhas, they the people worshipped in the Kali age. ॥98 (क)॥
uttar.98.so98ख: Those whose conduct does harm are the ones held in esteem and honoured;
those who are false in thought, deed and word are the speakers of the Kali age. ॥98 (ख)॥
uttar.99.cau1: My lord, all men are in the power of women and dance like a juggler's monkey.
Śūdras teach knowledge to Brahmins and, putting on the sacred thread, accept improper gifts. ॥1॥
uttar.99.cau2: All men are given to desire and greed and are quick to anger; they are hostile to the gods, Brahmins, the Vedas and the saints.
Ill-fated women leave a handsome husband who is a home of virtues and court another man. ॥2॥
uttar.99.cau3: Wives whose husbands live go without ornaments, while widows adorn themselves anew.
Guru and disciple are like the deaf and the blind: one does not hear, the other does not see. ॥3॥
uttar.99.cau4: The guru who takes his disciple's wealth but does not take away his grief falls into a terrible hell.
Mothers and fathers summon their children and teach them whatever dharma will fill the stomach. ॥4॥
uttar.99.do99क: Women and men talk of nothing but the knowledge of Brahman,
and these same people, ruled by greed, kill a Brahmin or a guru for a cowrie's worth. ॥99 (क)॥
uttar.99.do99ख: Śūdras argue with Brahmins: Are we in any way less than you?
He who knows Brahman is the best of Brahmins. And they glare at them and rebuke them. ॥99 (ख)॥
uttar.100.cau1: Those who lust after other men's wives, are clever at deceit and are wrapped in delusion, malice and possessiveness,
these are the wise men who preach non-duality: such were the ways of the Kali age that I saw. ॥1॥
uttar.100.cau2: They are lost themselves, and they bring ruin on those too who anywhere keep to the true path.
Those who find fault with the Vedas by argument lie in one hell after another, each for a whole kalpa (aeon). ॥2॥
uttar.100.cau3: Those counted lowest among the varṇas, such as oil-pressers, potters, śvapacas (outcastes), Kirātas, Kols and liquor-sellers,
when a wife dies or the household's wealth is lost, shave their heads and become sannyāsīs. ॥3॥
uttar.100.cau4: They have Brahmins worship them, and with their own hands they ruin both worlds.
Brahmins are unlettered, greedy and lustful, without right conduct, foolish, and husbands of low-born women. ॥4॥
uttar.100.cau5: Śūdras perform japa, austerities and vows of many kinds, and sit on the seat of honour to recite the Purāṇas.
All people follow ways of their own invention; the boundless wrong cannot be described. ॥5॥
uttar.100.do100क: In the Kali age the varṇas became mixed, and all people broke through the bounds.
They commit sins and reap sorrow, fear, sickness, grief and separation. ॥100 (क)॥
uttar.100.do100ख: The path of devotion to Śrī Hari, approved by the Vedas and joined with dispassion and discernment,
men, in their delusion, do not walk in it, and invent many paths of their own. ॥100 (ख)॥
uttar.101.cha1: Ascetics spend great sums to adorn their houses; sense-pleasures have stolen their dispassion and none is left.
The austere are rich and householders poor; dear one, the wonders of the Kali age cannot be told. ॥1॥
uttar.101.cau2: Men turn out a faithful wife of good family and, casting aside propriety, bring a maidservant into the house.
Sons honour mother and father only until they have looked on a wife's face. ॥2॥
uttar.101.cau3: From the time the in-laws' house grew dear, their own family became like enemies.
Kings are given to sin and have no dharma; they constantly torment their subjects with punishments. ॥3॥
uttar.101.cau4: The rich, though base, count as well-born; the mark of a Brahmin is his sacred thread, of an ascetic his bare body.
He who respects neither the Purāṇas nor the Vedas is, in the Kali age, the true servant of Śrī Hari and saint. ॥4॥
uttar.101.cau5: Poets come in throngs, but no generous patron is heard of in the world; fault-finders of merit are many, but not one person of merit.
In the Kali age famine falls again and again, and without food all people die in misery. ॥5॥
uttar.101.do101क: Listen, Garuḍa: in the Kali age deceit, obstinacy, hypocrisy, hatred, false creeds,
vanity, delusion, desire and the rest, and arrogance have spread over the whole universe. ॥101 (क)॥
uttar.101.do101ख: Men practise their dharma of japa, austerity, vows, sacrifice and charity in a spirit of darkness (tamas).
The gods send no rain on the earth, and the rice that is sown does not sprout. ॥101 (ख)॥
uttar.102.cha1: Women have only their hair for ornament, and great hunger; they are poor and sorrowful, with attachments of many kinds.
Foolish, they want happiness but have no love for dharma; their minds are small and hard, with no gentleness. ॥1॥
uttar.102.cau2: Men are afflicted with disease and find enjoyment nowhere; they are proud and quarrel without cause.
Life is short, five or ten years, yet their vanity is as if they would not perish even at the end of the aeon. ॥2॥
uttar.102.cau3: The Kali age has brought men to ruin; no one respects even a younger sister or a daughter.
There is no contentment, no reflection, no calm; people of every caste, high or low, have become beggars. ॥3॥
uttar.102.cau4: Envy, harsh words and greed fill everything to the brim; evenness of mind is gone.
All people are struck down by separation and deep grief; the dharma and conduct of varṇa and āśrama have vanished. ॥4॥
uttar.102.cau5: Self-restraint, charity, compassion and good sense are gone; dullness and the cheating of others abound.
Women and men alike care only to feed the body; slanderers of others are spread across the world. ॥5॥
uttar.102.do102क: Listen, Garuḍa: the Kali age is a home of sins and vices;
yet the Kali age has great merit too: in it deliverance comes without effort. ॥102 (क)॥
uttar.102.do102ख: In the Kṛta, Tretā and Dvāpara ages there are worship, sacrifice and yoga;
the state these win, people reach in the Kali age by the name of Śrī Hari. ॥102 (ख)॥
uttar.103.cau1: In the Kṛta age all are yogis and men of realised knowledge; by meditating on Śrī Hari, beings cross worldly existence.
In the Tretā age people perform sacrifices of many kinds and, offering their actions to the Lord, get across worldly existence. ॥1॥
uttar.103.cau2: In the Dvāpara age, worshipping the feet of Śrī Rāma, men cross worldly existence; there is no other way.
In the Kali age, simply by singing the tale of Śrī Hari's virtues, men find a footing in the ocean of existence. ॥2॥
uttar.103.cau3: In the Kali age there is no yoga, no sacrifice, no knowledge; the one support is singing Śrī Rāma's virtues.
Whoever gives up every other reliance, worships Śrī Rāma and sings his host of virtues with love, ॥3॥
uttar.103.cau4: he and no other crosses worldly existence, without any doubt; the power of the Name is plain to see in the Kali age.
The Kali age has one holy power: merit in the mind bears fruit, but sin in the mind does not count. ॥4॥
uttar.103.do103क: If one has faith, there is no age like the Kali age;
singing the spotless host of Śrī Rāma's virtues, one crosses worldly existence without effort. ॥103 (क)॥
uttar.103.do103ख: Dharma plainly has four feet, and in the Kali age one of them is chief;
that is giving: a gift, made by any means at all, does good. ॥103 (ख)॥
uttar.104.cau1: Moved by Śrī Rāma's māyā, the dharmas of all the ages arise in every heart day after day.
Pure sattva, evenness, realised knowledge and a cheerful mind: know these as the working of the Kṛta age. ॥1॥
uttar.104.cau2: Much sattva, a little rajas, a love of action and happiness of every kind: this is the dharma of the Tretā age.
Much rajas, very little sattva, some tamas, and joy and fear in the mind: this is the dharma of the Dvāpara age. ॥2॥
uttar.104.cau3: Much tamas, little rajas and strife on every side: this is the working of the Kali age.
The wise, understanding in their minds the dharma of the ages, give up unrighteousness and love dharma. ॥3॥
uttar.104.cau4: The ways of the age do not touch one whose love for the feet of Śrī Rāma is great.
King of the birds, the trickery a juggler works is hard to see through, but the juggler's own servant is not taken in by that illusion. ॥4॥
uttar.104.do104क: The faults and merits wrought by Śrī Hari's māyā do not go without worship of Śrī Hari;
considering this in the mind, one should give up all desires and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥104 (क)॥
uttar.104.do104ख: Lord of birds, in that Kali age I lived many years in Ayodhyā;
then famine came, and driven by hardship I went to a foreign land. ॥104 (ख)॥
uttar.105.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: I went to Ujjain, wretched, dejected, poor and unhappy.
After some time I came by a little wealth, and there I took to the service of Śiva. ॥1॥
uttar.105.cau2: There was a Vedic Brahmin who always worshipped Śiva and had no other work.
He was a true saint and knew the highest truth; a worshipper of Śiva, he never reviled Śrī Hari. ॥2॥
uttar.105.cau3: I served him with deceit in my heart; the Brahmin was most kind and a home of right conduct.
My lord, the Brahmin saw how humble I seemed outwardly and taught me like a son. ॥3॥
uttar.105.cau4: The noble Brahmin gave me Śiva's mantra and taught me what was good in many ways.
I would go to Śiva's temple and repeat the mantra, while hypocrisy and egoism grew great in my heart. ॥4॥
uttar.105.do105क: I was wicked, my mind full of filth, of low birth and in the grip of delusion;
at the sight of Śrī Hari's devotees and Brahmins I burned, and I bore enmity to Viṣṇu. ॥105 (क)॥
uttar.105.so105ख: My guru counselled me daily, pained at what he saw of my conduct;
but great anger arose in me: does right counsel ever please a hypocrite? ॥105 (ख)॥
uttar.106.cau1: Once my guru called me and taught me right conduct in many ways.
He said: Son, the fruit of serving Śiva is just this: unbroken devotion to Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥1॥
uttar.106.cau2: Dear one, Śiva and Brahmā themselves worship Śrī Rāma; what need, then, to speak of a lowly man?
Unlucky one, you hope to find happiness by hostility to him whose feet Brahmā and Śiva love? ॥2॥
uttar.106.cau3: My guru called Hara a servant of Hari, and hearing it, Garuḍa, my heart burned.
I was of low birth, and on gaining learning I became like a snake that has been fed milk. ॥3॥
uttar.106.cau4: Proud, crooked, ill-starred and low-born, I bore ill will to my guru day and night.
He was most compassionate, without the least anger, and again and again he gave me good counsel. ॥4॥
uttar.106.cau5: A base man strikes down and ruins first of all the very one through whom he gained his greatness.
Listen, brother: smoke, born of fire, rises to the rank of a cloud and puts that fire out. ॥5॥
uttar.106.cau6: Dust lies scorned on the road and bears the kicks of everyone, every day.
But when the wind lifts it, it first fills the wind itself, and then settles in the eyes of kings and on their crowns. ॥6॥
uttar.106.cau7: Listen, Garuḍa: understanding this, the wise keep no company with the base.
Poets and the learned sing this rule of conduct: with the wicked, neither quarrel nor friendship is good. ॥7॥
uttar.106.cau8: My master, one should always stay aloof, and shun the wicked as one would a dog.
I was wicked, with deceit and crookedness in my heart; my guru spoke for my good, but it did not please me. ॥8॥
uttar.106.do106क: Once I was in Śiva's temple, repeating the name of Śiva.
My guru came in, and in my pride I did not rise and bow to him. ॥106 (क)॥
uttar.106.do106ख: Compassionate as he was, he said nothing, and there was not a trace of anger in his heart.
But Maheśa could not bear the grave sin of slighting the guru. ॥106 (ख)॥
uttar.107.cau1: A voice from the sky sounded in the temple: Wretch, ignorant and proud!
Though your guru feels no anger, being most merciful and of perfect understanding, ॥1॥
uttar.107.cau2: still, fool, I shall curse you, for I cannot abide a breach of right conduct.
Wicked one, if I do not punish you, my path of the Veda will be broken. ॥2॥
uttar.107.cau3: Fools who envy their guru lie in the Raurava hell for ten million ages.
Then they take bodies among the lower creatures and suffer pain for ten thousand births. ॥3॥
uttar.107.cau4: Sinner, you sat on like a python; wicked one, your mind steeped in filth, become a snake.
Go into the hollow of some great tree and stay there, lowest of the low, sunk to this base state. ॥4॥
uttar.107.do107क: Hearing Śiva's dreadful curse, my guru cried out in dismay.
Seeing me tremble violently, he felt anguish rise in his heart. ॥107 (क)॥
uttar.107.do107ख: The Brahmin prostrated himself with love and, facing Śiva, joined his palms.
Then, thinking of the terrible fate that awaited me, he began to pray in a voice choked with feeling. ॥107 (ख)॥
uttar.108.cau1: O Īśāna, I bow to the Lord whose form is liberation, the mighty, the all-pervading, Brahman, the Veda itself.
Abiding in his own being, beyond attributes and all distinctions, free of desire, the sky of consciousness, dwelling in the sky: you I worship. ॥1॥
uttar.108.cau2: Formless, the root of Oṃ, the fourth state beyond the three, beyond speech, knowledge and the senses, the Lord, lord of the mountain,
terrible, the death even of Mahākāla, compassionate, the home of virtues, beyond the world: to him I bow. ॥2॥
uttar.108.cau3: Fair as the snowy mountain and deep, his body bright with the radiance and beauty of ten million Kāmas;
on his head the lovely Gaṅgā shimmers in waves, the young moon gleams on his brow, and serpents lie at his throat; ॥3॥
uttar.108.cau4: his earrings swaying, his brows fair and his eyes large and lovely, his face serene, his throat blue, full of compassion;
clad in the skin of the lion, garlanded with skulls: Śaṅkara, the beloved, the Lord of all, I worship. ॥4॥
uttar.108.cau5: The fierce, the supreme, the bold, the highest Lord, the undivided, the unborn, shining like ten million suns,
who uproots the three kinds of pain, trident in hand, reached through loving feeling: the lord of Bhavānī I worship. ॥5॥
uttar.108.cau6: You who are beyond all parts, the auspicious, who bring the aeon to its end, ever the giver of joy to the good, enemy of Tripura,
mass of consciousness and bliss, dispeller of delusion, enemy of Kāma: my Lord, be gracious, be gracious. ॥6॥
uttar.108.cau7: Lord of Umā, as long as men, in this world or the next, do not worship your lotus feet,
they find no happiness, no peace, no end to their torment. Be gracious, my Lord, who dwell in all beings. ॥7॥
uttar.108.cau8: I know neither yoga nor japa nor worship; Śambhu, at every moment and always, I bow to you.
My Lord, I am scorched by the flood of the sorrows of age and birth and have fallen into distress: protect me, O Īśa, O Śambhu. ॥8॥
uttar.108.shloka9: This Rudrāṣṭaka was spoken by the Brahmin to please Hara.
Śiva is gracious to those who recite it with devotion. ॥9॥
uttar.108.do108क: Śiva, who knows all, heard the prayer and saw the Brahmin's love.
Then again a voice from the sky sounded in the temple: Best of Brahmins, ask for a boon. ॥108 (क)॥
uttar.108.do108ख: The Brahmin said: Lord, if you are pleased with me, and, master, if you love the lowly,
then, Lord, grant me first devotion to your own feet, and after that a second boon. ॥108 (ख)॥
uttar.108.do108ग: The soul is dull; in the power of your māyā it wanders, always astray.
Lord, ocean of mercy, Bhagavān, do not be angry with it. ॥108 (ग)॥
uttar.108.do108घ: Śiva, kind to the lowly, be merciful to him now,
so that, my Lord, before long the curse may give way to grace. ॥108 (घ)॥
uttar.109.cau1: Treasury of mercy, now do that which will bring him the highest good.
Hearing the Brahmin's words, steeped in the good of another, the voice from the sky said: So be it. ॥1॥
uttar.109.cau2: Though he has committed a dreadful sin, and I in my anger have cursed him,
yet, seeing your goodness, I shall show him special grace. ॥2॥
uttar.109.cau3: Brahmins who are forgiving and do good to others are as dear to me as Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara.
Brahmin, my curse will not go for nothing; he will surely pass through a thousand births. ॥3॥
uttar.109.cau4: But the unbearable pain that comes with being born and dying will not touch him in the least.
In no birth will his knowledge fade. Śūdra, listen: my word holds true. ॥4॥
uttar.109.cau5: You were born in Śrī Rāma's city, and then you set your mind on serving me.
Through the power of that city and through my grace, devotion to Śrī Rāma will arise in your heart. ॥5॥
uttar.109.cau6: Now hear my true words, brother: serving the Brahmins is the vow that pleases Śrī Hari.
Never again insult a Brahmin; know the saints to be equal to the infinite Lord. ॥6॥
uttar.109.cau7: Indra's thunderbolt, my great trident, the rod of Death and the dreadful discus of Śrī Hari:
one whom these cannot kill is burnt up in the fire of hostility to Brahmins. ॥7॥
uttar.109.cau8: Keep this discernment in your mind, and nothing in the world will be beyond your reach.
And I give you one more blessing: your going will be unhindered everywhere. ॥8॥
uttar.109.do109क: Hearing Śiva's words, my guru rejoiced and said: So be it.
Then he counselled me and went home, keeping Śiva's feet in his heart. ॥109 (क)॥
uttar.109.do109ख: Driven by time, I went to the Vindhya mountains and became a serpent.
Then, when some time had passed, I left that body without any struggle. ॥109 (ख)॥
uttar.109.do109ग: Garuḍa, mount of Hari, whatever body I took I would lay down again with ease,
as a man puts on new clothes and casts off the old. ॥109 (ग)॥
uttar.109.do109घ: Śiva kept the rule of the Veda, and I did not suffer.
In this way, Garuḍa, I took many bodies, yet my knowledge never left me. ॥109 (घ)॥
uttar.110.cau1: Whatever body I took, beast or bird, god or man, in each I kept up the worship of Śrī Rāma.
One pain I can never forget: the gentle, gracious nature of my guru. ॥1॥
uttar.110.cau2: My last body was that of a Brahmin, which the Purāṇas and the Vedas declare hard even for the gods to win.
There too I played among the boys, acting out all the deeds of Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.110.cau3: When I grew up, my father taught me; I understood, listened and pondered, but none of it appealed to me.
Every desire had fled my mind; I was absorbed in Śrī Rāma's feet alone. ॥3॥
uttar.110.cau4: Tell me, Garuḍa, who would be so unlucky as to leave the cow of plenty of the gods and tend a she-ass?
Lost in love, I cared for nothing else; my father wore himself out teaching me. ॥4॥
uttar.110.cau5: When my father and mother were taken by death, I went to the forest to worship the protector of his people.
Wherever in the woods I came upon great sages, I would go to their hermitages, one after another, and bow my head. ॥5॥
uttar.110.cau6: I would ask them the tales of Śrī Rāma's virtues; they would tell them, Garuḍa, and I would listen in delight.
So I roamed, hearing the virtues of Śrī Hari recounted, and by Śiva's grace nothing stopped my way. ॥6॥
uttar.110.cau7: The three deep-rooted cravings fell away from me, and one longing grew strong in my heart:
only when I see the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma shall I count my birth fulfilled. ॥7॥
uttar.110.cau8: Every sage I asked would tell me that God is made up of all beings.
The doctrine of the attributeless did not please me; love for Brahman with attributes grew ever stronger in my heart. ॥8॥
uttar.110.do110क: Remembering my guru's words, my mind was fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet.
I roamed singing the glory of Śrī Rāma, my love new at every moment. ॥110 (क)॥
uttar.110.do110ख: The sage Lomaśa was seated under a banyan, in its shade, on the summit of Meru.
When I saw him I bowed my head at his feet and spoke very humbly. ॥110 (ख)॥
uttar.110.do110ग: King of birds, the kind sage heard my humble, gentle words,
and asked me courteously: Brahmin, what brings you here? ॥110 (ग)॥
uttar.110.do110घ: Then I said: Treasury of mercy, you know all things and are wise.
Revered one, teach me the worship of Brahman with attributes. ॥110 (घ)॥
uttar.111.cau1: Then, Garuḍa, the great sage told me with reverence something of the story of Śrī Rāma's virtues.
And that sage of realised knowledge, absorbed in the knowledge of Brahman, judging me a most fit recipient, ॥1॥
uttar.111.cau2: began to teach me about Brahman: it is unborn, one without a second, without attributes, the lord of the heart;
without parts, without desire, without name and without form; it is known only by experience, it is undivided, and nothing compares with it. ॥2॥
uttar.111.cau3: It is beyond the reach of mind and senses, stainless, imperishable, changeless, boundless, a mass of joy.
You are That, the Vedas sing; between it and you there is no difference, as there is none between water and its wave. ॥3॥
uttar.111.cau4: The sage explained it to me in many ways, but the doctrine of the attributeless would not enter my heart.
Once more I spoke, my head bowed at his feet: Great sage, teach me the worship of the Lord with attributes. ॥4॥
uttar.111.cau5: My mind is a fish in the water of devotion to Śrī Rāma; how could it live apart from it, wise and great sage?
Be kind and give me that teaching by which, with my own eyes, I may see Śrī Rāma. ॥5॥
uttar.111.cau6: When I have seen the Lord of Avadh to my eyes' content, then I will hear the teaching on the attributeless.
The sage, after telling once more the peerless story of Śrī Hari, refuted the view of the Lord with attributes and set forth the attributeless. ॥6॥
uttar.111.cau7: Then I would push aside the view of the attributeless and argue, stubborn beyond measure, for the Lord with attributes.
I answered him and answered back, and signs of anger showed in the sage's body. ॥7॥
uttar.111.cau8: Listen, my lord: when much disrespect is shown, anger springs up even in the hearts of the wise.
If someone rubs sandalwood too hard, even from it fire breaks out. ॥8॥
uttar.111.do111क: Again and again the sage, in anger, expounded knowledge,
while I sat there and turned over many thoughts in my own mind: ॥111 (क)॥
uttar.111.do111ख: Can anger arise where there is no sense of duality? Can duality exist without ignorance?
Can the soul, in the grip of māyā, limited and inert, be the equal of God? ॥111 (ख)॥
uttar.112.cau1: Does sorrow ever come to one who looks to the good of all? Can poverty touch one who owns the touchstone?
Can those who wrong others live free of fear? And do the lustful stay without a stain? ॥1॥
uttar.112.cau2: Does anyone's line survive harm done to a Brahmin? Once one has known one's own true nature, is there still karma?
Has good sense ever sprung up in anyone in the company of the wicked? Does one who goes to another's wife reach a good end? ॥2॥
uttar.112.cau3: Do those who know the Supreme Self fall into worldly existence? Are those who revile Śrī Hari ever happy?
Does a kingdom last without knowledge of right policy? Do sins remain when the deeds of Śrī Hari are told? ॥3॥
uttar.112.cau4: Is holy fame won without merit? Does anyone earn ill fame without sin?
Is there any gain equal to devotion to Śrī Hari, which the Vedas, the saints and the Purāṇas sing? ॥4॥
uttar.112.cau5: Brother, to gain a human body and not worship Śrī Rāma: what loss in the world could equal this?
Is there any other sin like backbiting, Garuḍa, or any dharma like compassion? ॥5॥
uttar.112.cau6: In this way I kept weighing countless arguments in my mind, and did not hear the sage's teaching with respect.
When again and again I planted myself on the side of the Lord with attributes, the sage spoke in anger: ॥6॥
uttar.112.cau7: Fool, I give you the highest teaching and you will not accept it; you keep bringing answer upon answer.
You put no faith in words of truth; like a crow you are afraid of everything. ॥7॥
uttar.112.cau8: Wretch, your heart clings hard to your own side: become at once the lowest of birds.
I took the curse upon my head; I felt no fear, and no dejection came over me. ॥8॥
uttar.112.do112क: At once I became a crow; then, bowing my head again at the sage's feet
and remembering Śrī Rāma, the jewel of the Raghu line, I flew away in gladness. ॥112 (क)॥
uttar.112.do112ख: Umā, those whose love is fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet, who have left desire, pride and anger behind,
see the whole world as full of their own Lord: with whom, then, should they quarrel? ॥112 (ख)॥
uttar.113.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, Garuḍa: no blame at all lies with the sage; the one who stirs the heart is Śrī Rāma, the ornament of the Raghu line.
To try my love, the ocean of mercy made the sage's mind simple and unwary. ॥1॥
uttar.113.cau2: The Lord saw that in thought, word and deed I was his own; then he turned the sage's mind back again.
The sage saw my great gentleness of nature and my special faith in Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥2॥
uttar.113.cau3: Deeply astonished, he repented again and again, and the sage called me back with respect.
He comforted me in many ways, and then, glad at heart, gave me the mantra of Rāma. ॥3॥
uttar.113.cau4: The sage, a treasury of compassion, taught me the meditation on Śrī Rāma in the form of a child.
That lovely, joy-giving meditation delighted me greatly; I have already told it to you. ॥4॥
uttar.113.cau5: The sage kept me there with him for some time, and then he told the Rāmacaritamānasa.
When he had told me this story with reverence, the sage spoke again in gracious words: ॥5॥
uttar.113.cau6: Dear one, I received this lovely and hidden lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds by the grace of Śiva.
It is because I know you to be Śrī Rāma's own devotee that I have told you all of it in full. ॥6॥
uttar.113.cau7: Dear one, never tell it to those who have no devotion to Śrī Rāma in their hearts.
In many ways the sage instructed me, and I bowed my head at his feet with love. ॥7॥
uttar.113.cau8: Touching my head with his lotus hand, the great sage blessed me with joy:
Unbroken devotion to Śrī Rāma will dwell in your heart for ever; this, from now on, is my grace upon you. ॥8॥
uttar.113.do113क: May you always be dear to Śrī Rāma, a home of good qualities, free of pride;
able to take any form at will, dying only when you choose, a treasury of knowledge and dispassion. ॥113 (क)॥
uttar.113.do113ख: Moreover, in whatever hermitage you dwell, remembering the Blessed Lord,
there ignorance will not spread for a yojana around. ॥113 (ख)॥
uttar.114.cau1: No sorrow born of time, karma, the guṇas, faults or one's own nature will ever touch you.
The many lovely secrets of Śrī Rāma, hidden and open, in the epics and the Purāṇas, ॥1॥
uttar.114.cau2: all of them too you will know without effort; may your love for Śrī Rāma's feet be new every day.
Whatever you wish for in your mind, by the grace of Śrī Hari nothing will be beyond your reach. ॥2॥
uttar.114.cau3: Listen, Garuḍa, steady of mind: when the sage's blessing had been heard, a deep voice of Brahman sounded from the sky:
So be it, wise sage, as you have spoken; he is my devotee in deed, mind and speech. ॥3॥
uttar.114.cau4: Hearing the voice from the sky, I was filled with joy; I was lost in love, and all my doubt was gone.
I made my entreaty to the sage and, receiving his leave, bowed my head again and again at his lotus feet; ॥4॥
uttar.114.cau5: then I came joyfully to this hermitage, having gained by the Lord's grace a boon that is hard to win.
Listen, Garuḍa: since I came to live here, twenty-seven kalpas have gone by. ॥5॥
uttar.114.cau6: I am always singing the virtues of Śrī Rāma, and wise birds listen with reverence.
Each time Śrī Rāma, for his devotees' sake, takes a human body in Ayodhyā, ॥6॥
uttar.114.cau7: each time I go and live in Śrī Rāma's city, and find my joy in watching his play as a child.
Then, Garuḍa, keeping Śrī Rāma's child form in my heart, I come back to my own hermitage. ॥7॥
uttar.114.cau8: I have told you the whole story of how I came to have a crow's body.
Dear one, I have answered all your questions; immense is the glory of devotion to Śrī Rāma. ॥8॥
uttar.114.do114क: This body is dear to me for this reason: in it love for Śrī Rāma's feet was born in me.
In it I had the sight of my own Lord, and all my doubts were gone. ॥114 (क)॥
uttar.114.do114ख: I held stubbornly to the side of devotion, and the great sage laid a curse on me;
yet I gained a boon that even sages rarely win: see the power of worship. ॥114 (ख)॥
uttar.115.cau1: Those who know such devotion and yet forsake it, and labour for knowledge alone,
are dullards: they abandon the wish-fulfilling cow at home and wander, searching the milkweed for milk. ॥1॥
uttar.115.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: those who turn from devotion to Śrī Hari and seek happiness by some other means
are fools of foolish deeds who would swim across the vast ocean without a boat. ॥2॥
uttar.115.cau3: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's words, Bhavānī, Garuḍa spoke joyfully and gently:
By your grace, my lord, there is now no doubt in my heart, no grief, no delusion, no error. ॥3॥
uttar.115.cau4: I have heard the many holy virtues of Śrī Rāma, and by your grace I have found rest.
One thing I ask you, my lord; explain it to me clearly, treasury of mercy. ॥4॥
uttar.115.cau5: The saints, the sages, the Vedas and the Purāṇas say that nothing is as hard to gain as knowledge.
That very knowledge, master, the sage taught you, yet you did not honour it as you honour devotion. ॥5॥
uttar.115.cau6: How great is the difference between knowledge and devotion? Tell me all of it, my lord, home of grace.
The wise crow was pleased to hear Garuḍa's words, and replied with respect: ॥6॥
uttar.115.cau7: Between devotion and knowledge there is no difference at all; both take away the suffering born of worldly existence.
My lord, the great sages do name some difference; hear it carefully, best of birds. ॥7॥
uttar.115.cau8: Knowledge, dispassion, yoga and realised knowledge, listen, Garuḍa: all these are male.
The power of the male is strong in every way; the female is by nature weak and of an inert kind. ॥8॥
uttar.115.do115क: Only the man who is free of attachment and steady of mind can give up woman;
not the man of desire, ruled by the senses, who has turned away from Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥115 (क)॥
uttar.115.so115ख: Even such a sage, a treasury of knowledge, gazing on the moonlike face of a doe-eyed woman,
falls under her sway, Garuḍa: woman is the māyā of Viṣṇu made manifest. ॥115 (ख)॥
uttar.116.cau1: Here I take no side; I state the view of the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the saints.
Delusion does not come to a woman from a woman's beauty; this, Garuḍa, is a matchless rule. ॥1॥
uttar.116.cau2: Listen: māyā and devotion are both of the feminine kind, as everyone knows.
Then too, devotion is dear to Śrī Rāma, and māyā, poor thing, is no more than a dancer. ॥2॥
uttar.116.cau3: Śrī Rāma favours devotion; that is why māyā fears her so.
The one in whose heart devotion to Śrī Rāma dwells always and unhindered, peerless and free of all adjuncts: ॥3॥
uttar.116.cau4: seeing him, māyā shrinks back and can exert none of her power over him.
Considering this, sages of realised knowledge ask for devotion, the mine of every joy. ॥4॥
uttar.116.do116क: This secret of Śrī Rāma no one comes to know quickly.
Whoever knows it by Śrī Rāma's grace is never deluded, not even in a dream. ॥116 (क)॥
uttar.116.do116ख: Hear, most skilful Garuḍa, a further difference between knowledge and devotion,
hearing which one comes to have unbroken love for Śrī Rāma's feet for ever. ॥116 (ख)॥
uttar.117.cau1: Listen, dear one, to this story beyond telling: it can be understood, but not described.
The soul is a part of the Lord, imperishable, conscious, stainless, by its nature a mass of joy. ॥1॥
uttar.117.cau2: That soul, my lord, fell under the sway of māyā and was caught like a parrot or a monkey.
A knot was tied between the inert and the conscious; though it is false, it is hard to undo. ॥2॥
uttar.117.cau3: From then on the soul has been bound to worldly existence; the knot does not loosen, nor does the soul find happiness.
The Vedas and Purāṇas have told many remedies, but it does not come loose; it only tangles more and more. ॥3॥
uttar.117.cau4: In the soul's heart the darkness of delusion is thick; the knot cannot even be seen, so how can it come loose?
Even when the Lord brings about such a circumstance, it may only now and then be undone. ॥4॥
uttar.117.cau5: Suppose that by Śrī Hari's grace the lovely cow of sāttvika faith comes to dwell in the heart;
the countless prayers, austerities, vows, restraints and observances, and the good dharma and conduct that the Vedas speak of, ॥5॥
uttar.117.cau6: are the green grass; when that cow grazes on it and, finding her young calf of devout feeling, lets down her milk;
with withdrawal from the world as the milking tether, faith as the pail, and the pure mind, one's own servant, as the cowherd; ॥6॥
uttar.117.cau7: having milked, brother, the milk that is supreme dharma, let him boil it well on the fire of desirelessness;
then cool it in the breeze of contentment and forbearance, and set it into curd with the starter of fortitude and calm. ॥7॥
uttar.117.cau8: With gladness let him churn it with the churning-stick of reflection, on the post of self-control, with the rope of truth and kind speech;
then by churning draw out the butter of dispassion, stainless, lovely and wholly pure. ॥8॥
uttar.117.do117क: Then let him kindle the fire of yoga and feed it with deeds good and bad;
when the dross of attachment has burnt away, let the intellect cool the ghee of knowledge. ॥117 (क)॥
uttar.117.do117ख: Then the intellect, which is realised knowledge itself, having gained that clear ghee,
should fill the lamp of the mind and set it firm on a stand made of evenness. ॥117 (ख)॥
uttar.117.do117ग: From the cotton of the three states and the three guṇas let the intellect draw out the fibre of turīya, the fourth state,
then card it and twist it into a firm, tight wick. ॥117 (ग)॥
uttar.117.so117घ: In this way let the lamp of realised knowledge be lit, a mass of radiance,
on coming near which pride and all the other moths are burnt up. ॥117 (घ)॥
uttar.118.cau1: The unbroken awareness so'ham asmi (I am That) is the lamp's most brilliant flame.
The joy of knowing the Self gives a clear light; then the delusion of difference that worldly existence grows from is destroyed, ॥1॥
uttar.118.cau2: and the boundless darkness of delusion and the rest, the household of mighty ignorance, is dispelled.
Then that same intellect, gaining light, sits in the house of the heart and unties the knot. ॥2॥
uttar.118.cau3: If it can untie the knot, the soul attains its end.
But knowing that the knot is being untied, king of birds, māyā then raises many obstacles. ॥3॥
uttar.118.cau4: She urges on many ṛddhis and siddhis (riches and powers), brother, who come and tempt the intellect with greed.
By charm, force and trickery they draw near and blow out the lamp with the breeze of their garments. ॥4॥
uttar.118.cau5: If the intellect is truly wise, it knows them for its harm and will not even look at them.
If that obstacle does not stop the intellect, then the gods make trouble. ॥5॥
uttar.118.cau6: The doors of the senses are the many windows of that house, and at each of them gods have taken their post.
As soon as they see the wind of the sense-objects coming, they force the shutters open. ॥6॥
uttar.118.cau7: When that gale enters the house of the heart, the lamp of realised knowledge goes out.
The knot was not undone, the light was gone, and the intellect was thrown into confusion by the wind of the sense-objects. ॥7॥
uttar.118.cau8: Knowledge does not please the senses or their gods; their love is always for the enjoyment of sense-objects.
The wind of the sense-objects has bewildered the intellect; who then will light the lamp again in the same way? ॥8॥
uttar.118.do118क: Then the soul suffers once more the many pains of the round of birth and death.
Śrī Hari's māyā is very hard to cross, lord of birds; it cannot be crossed. ॥118 (क)॥
uttar.118.do118ख: Discernment is hard to tell, hard to understand and hard to practise.
If by pure chance, as a woodworm happens to carve a letter, one gains it, even then obstacles are many. ॥118 (ख)॥
uttar.119.cau1: The path of knowledge is a sword's edge; one falls from it in no time, king of birds.
He who keeps to that path without a hindrance attains kaivalya, the supreme state. ॥1॥
uttar.119.cau2: Kaivalya, the supreme state, is very hard to reach, say the saints, the Purāṇas, the Vedas and the Āgamas.
Yet, my lord, when one worships Śrī Rāma, that same liberation forces its way to him unbidden. ॥2॥
uttar.119.cau3: As water cannot stay without ground, whatever ten million means one tries,
so, listen, king of birds, the joy of liberation cannot remain without devotion to Śrī Hari. ॥3॥
uttar.119.cau4: Considering this, wise devotees of Śrī Hari disdain liberation and are drawn to devotion.
Through devotion, without effort or labour, ignorance, the root of worldly existence, is destroyed, ॥4॥
uttar.119.cau5: as one eats for the sake of being satisfied, and the fire of the stomach digests the food.
Such is devotion to Śrī Hari, easy and joy-giving; who is so foolish as not to love it? ॥5॥
uttar.119.do119क: Without the feeling of servant and served, Garuḍa, one cannot cross worldly existence.
Weigh this settled truth and worship Śrī Rāma's lotus feet. ॥119 (क)॥
uttar.119.do119ख: He makes the conscious inert and the inert conscious:
blessed are the souls who worship Śrī Rāma, so mighty. ॥119 (ख)॥
uttar.120.cau1: I have explained the doctrine of knowledge; now hear the power of the jewel of devotion.
Devotion to Śrī Rāma is a lovely wish-fulfilling gem; in whoever's heart it dwells, Garuḍa, ॥1॥
uttar.120.cau2: it is supreme light day and night, needing no lamp, no ghee, no wick.
The poverty of delusion does not come near, and the wind of greed does not put it out. ॥2॥
uttar.120.cau3: The darkness of mighty ignorance is dispelled, and the swarms of moths are all defeated.
Desire and the other villains do not come near one in whose heart devotion dwells. ॥3॥
uttar.120.cau4: For him poison becomes like nectar and a foe a friend; without that gem no one finds happiness.
The grave ailments of the mind, which hold all creatures in misery, do not seize him. ॥4॥
uttar.120.cau5: If the gem of devotion to Śrī Rāma lives in someone's heart, not a trace of sorrow touches him even in dreams.
In this world those are the crown of the wise who strive well to gain that gem. ॥5॥
uttar.120.cau6: Though that gem is there for all the world to see, no one gains it without Śrī Rāma's grace.
The means of finding it are easy, but luckless men spurn them. ॥6॥
uttar.120.cau7: The Vedas and Purāṇas are holy mountains, and the many stories of Śrī Rāma are the fine mines in them.
The good who know their secrets are the prospectors, a sound mind the pick, and knowledge and dispassion the eyes, Garuḍa. ॥7॥
uttar.120.cau8: Whoever searches for it with love finds the gem of devotion, mine of every joy.
My lord, this is the faith of my heart: greater than Śrī Rāma is the servant of Śrī Rāma. ॥8॥
uttar.120.cau9: Śrī Rāma is the ocean and the steadfast good are the clouds; Śrī Hari is the sandal tree and the saints the breeze.
The fruit of all is lovely devotion to Śrī Hari, and no one has gained it without a saint. ॥9॥
uttar.120.cau10: Considering this, whoever keeps the company of the good finds devotion to Śrī Rāma within easy reach, Garuḍa. ॥10॥
uttar.120.do120क: Brahman, the Veda, is the ocean, knowledge is Mount Mandara, and the saints are the gods
who churn it and draw out the nectar of the story, whose sweetness is devotion. ॥120 (क)॥
uttar.120.do120ख: With dispassion as shield and knowledge as sword, slaying the foes pride, greed and delusion,
the one who wins the victory is devotion to Śrī Hari; think it over and see, lord of birds. ॥120 (ख)॥
uttar.121.cau1: Then Garuḍa, king of birds, spoke lovingly: Gracious one, if you have affection for me,
my lord, regard me as your own servant and answer my seven questions in full. ॥1॥
uttar.121.cau2: First tell me, my lord of steady mind, which body is the hardest of all to gain.
What is the great sorrow, and what the great joy? Consider this too and tell it briefly. ॥2॥
uttar.121.cau3: You know the inner nature of the good and the wicked; describe their innate ways.
What merit, renowned in the Vedas, is greatest? And tell me which sin is the most terrible. ॥3॥
uttar.121.cau4: Explain to me the diseases of the mind; you know all things, and your kindness to me is great.
Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, dear one, with respect and deep love; I will tell this teaching briefly. ॥4॥
uttar.121.cau5: No body equals the human body; all creatures, moving and unmoving, long for it.
It is the ladder to hell, to heaven and to liberation, and it gives the blessings of knowledge, dispassion and devotion. ॥5॥
uttar.121.cau6: Those men who take that body and do not worship Śrī Hari, but cling to the senses, grow base and baser;
they take bits of broken glass in exchange, casting the philosopher's stone from their hand. ॥6॥
uttar.121.cau7: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy in the world like meeting the saints.
To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the very nature of the saints, king of birds. ॥7॥
uttar.121.cau8: The saints bear suffering for the good of others; the wretched wicked, to bring others suffering.
Like the birch tree, the kindly saints always endure great hardship for others' good. ॥8॥
uttar.121.cau9: The wicked, like hemp, bind others, and have their skin stripped and die in torment for it.
The wicked do others harm though nothing is in it for them, like the snake and the rat; listen, Garuḍa. ॥9॥
uttar.121.cau10: They ruin others' wealth and are ruined themselves, as hailstones beat down the crops and melt away.
The rise of the wicked brings the world distress, as does that of Ketu, the notorious evil planet. ॥10॥
uttar.121.cau11: The rise of the saints always brings happiness, as the moon and the sun bring joy to the whole world.
The highest dharma, known from the Vedas, is non-violence, and no sin is as heavy as speaking ill of others. ॥11॥
uttar.121.cau12: One who reviles Śiva or the guru becomes a frog, and keeps that body for a thousand births.
One who reviles the brāhmaṇas suffers many hells and is then born in the world in the body of a crow. ॥12॥
uttar.121.cau13: Proud creatures who revile the gods and the Vedas fall into the Raurava hell.
Those given to reviling the saints become owls, lovers of the night of delusion, the sun of knowledge gone from them. ॥13॥
uttar.121.cau14: The dull who revile everyone are born as bats.
Now hear, dear one, of the diseases of the mind, from which all people suffer. ॥14॥
uttar.121.cau15: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from them in turn spring many pains.
Desire is wind, boundless greed is phlegm, and anger is bile, which always burns the breast. ॥15॥
uttar.121.cau16: If these three brothers make friends, the painful sannipāta (a fever of all three humours) arises.
The many cravings for sense-objects, hard to fulfil, are all those pains; who knows their names? ॥16॥
