uttar.121.cau17: Attachment is ringworm, envy is the itch, and joy and grief are a host of throat diseases.
The burning at seeing another's happiness is consumption; wickedness and crookedness of mind are leprosy. ॥17॥
uttar.121.cau18: Egotism is a most painful gout; hypocrisy, deceit, pride and vanity are the guinea-worm.
Craving is a severe dropsy, and the three kinds of longing are a raging tertian fever. ॥18॥
uttar.121.cau19: Envy and lack of discernment are two kinds of fever. How far can I go on naming the many evil diseases? ॥19॥
uttar.121.do121क: Men die in the grip of a single disease, and these are many diseases, past all cure.
They torment the soul without end; how then can it find samādhi, inner stillness? ॥121 (क)॥
uttar.121.do121ख: Observances, dharma, good conduct, austerity, knowledge, sacrifice, prayer and charity,
and remedies by the million besides: yet with them, Garuḍa, these diseases do not go. ॥121 (ख)॥
uttar.122.cau1: In this way all creatures in the world are sick, suffering from sorrow, delight, fear, attachment and separation.
These few ailments of the mind I have sung of; they are in everyone, yet rare are those who have perceived them. ॥1॥
uttar.122.cau2: Once recognised, these wicked ailments dwindle a little, but these tormentors of people are not destroyed.
Once they get the wrong food of sense-objects, they sprout even in the hearts of sages; what chance, then, for poor men? ॥2॥
uttar.122.cau3: By Śrī Rāma's grace all these diseases perish, if the means come together in this way:
faith in the words of the true guru, the physician, and for restraint, no longing for the objects of sense. ॥3॥
uttar.122.cau4: Devotion to Śrī Rāma is the life-giving herb, and a mind full of faith is what it is taken with.
Taken in this way, those diseases are surely cured; otherwise they do not go, though ten million remedies be tried. ॥4॥
uttar.122.cau5: Know the mind to be free of disease, my lord, when the strength of dispassion grows in the heart,
when the hunger for right understanding increases, new every day, and the weakness of longing for the senses has gone. ॥5॥
uttar.122.cau6: When the mind has bathed in the water of pure knowledge, devotion to Śrī Rāma fills the heart and stays there.
Śiva, Brahmā, Śuka, Sanaka and his brothers, and Nārada, sages skilled in reflection on Brahman, ॥6॥
uttar.122.cau7: are all of this one view, lord of birds: love should be given to Śrī Rāma's lotus feet.
The Vedas, the Purāṇas and every scripture say that without devotion to Śrī Rāma there is no happiness. ॥7॥
uttar.122.cau8: Hair may grow on a tortoise's back, a barren woman's son may kill a man,
flowers of every kind may blossom in the sky; still no being hostile to Śrī Hari finds happiness. ॥8॥
uttar.122.cau9: A mirage's water may quench thirst, horns may spring from a hare's head,
darkness may put out the sun; still no being turned from Śrī Rāma finds happiness. ॥9॥
uttar.122.cau10: Fire may even spring out of ice, yet no one turned away from Śrī Rāma finds happiness. ॥10॥
uttar.122.do122क: Ghee may come from churning water, oil may be pressed from sand,
but without the worship of Śrī Hari the ocean of worldly existence is not crossed: this truth is unshakable. ॥122 (क)॥
uttar.122.do122ख: The Lord can make a mosquito into Brahmā, and make Brahmā lower than a mosquito.
Seeing this, the wise give up doubt and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥122 (ख)॥
uttar.123.shloka122ग: I tell you what is firmly settled, and my words are not false:
those who worship Śrī Hari cross over what is most hard to cross. ॥122 (ग)॥
uttar.123.cau1: My lord, I have told the incomparable deeds of Śrī Hari, at length and in brief, as far as my understanding goes.
Garuḍa, this is the settled teaching of the Vedas: worship Śrī Rāma, setting every other task aside. ॥1॥
uttar.123.cau2: Leaving the Lord Śrī Rāma, whom else should one serve, who claims even a fool like me for his own?
You are realised knowledge itself, with no delusion in you; yet, my lord, you have shown me great kindness, ॥2॥
uttar.123.cau3: in that you asked me for the most holy story of Śrī Rāma, which delights the minds of Śuka, Sanaka and his brothers, and Śiva.
In this world the company of the good is hard to find even once, for a moment or for a short while. ॥3॥
uttar.123.cau4: Garuḍa, think it over in your own heart: was I fit to worship Śrī Rāma?
I, the lowest of birds and impure in every way, have been made by the Lord holy and known throughout the world. ॥4॥
uttar.123.do123क: Today I am blessed, deeply blessed, though lacking in every way,
for Śrī Rāma, knowing me as his own, has granted me the meeting with a saint. ॥123 (क)॥
uttar.123.do123ख: My lord, I have spoken as my understanding allows, and have kept nothing back.
The deeds of Śrī Rāma are an ocean: can anyone touch its bottom? ॥123 (ख)॥
uttar.124.cau1: Remembering Śrī Rāma's many virtues, the wise Kākabhuśuṇḍi rejoiced again and again.
Then he said: He whose glory the Vedas have sung as neti, not this, whose might, majesty and lordship are beyond compare, ॥1॥
uttar.124.cau2: whose feet are worshipped by Śiva and Brahmā: his grace on me is his utmost tenderness.
Such a nature I neither hear of nor see anywhere; whom, Garuḍa, could I count equal to Śrī Rāma? ॥2॥
uttar.124.cau3: Seekers, adepts, the liberated, the detached, poets, the learned, the grateful, renunciants,
yogis, heroes, great ascetics, the wise, those intent on dharma, scholars and those of realised knowledge: ॥3॥
uttar.124.cau4: none of them crosses over without serving my Lord. To Śrī Rāma I bow, I bow, I bow.
Going to his refuge, even heaps of sin like me are made pure: I bow to the Imperishable. ॥4॥
uttar.124.do124क: His name is the cure for the sickness of worldly life and removes the three terrible torments;
may he, the compassionate one, be ever kind to me and to you. ॥124 (क)॥
uttar.124.do124ख: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's auspicious words and seeing his love for Śrī Rāma's feet,
Garuḍa spoke words full of love, all his doubt gone: ॥124 (ख)॥
uttar.125.cau1: Hearing your words, steeped in the delight of devotion to Śrī Rāma, I have reached life's fulfilment.
A new love for Śrī Rāma's feet has arisen in me, and all the trouble born of māyā has gone. ॥1॥
uttar.125.cau2: In the ocean of delusion you became my ship; my lord, you have given me joys of many kinds.
I have nothing to give in return; again and again I bow to your feet. ॥2॥
uttar.125.cau3: Your every wish is fulfilled and you love Śrī Rāma; dear sir, no one is as fortunate as you.
Saints, trees, rivers, mountains and the earth: everything they do is for the good of others. ॥3॥
uttar.125.cau4: Poets have called a saint's heart like butter, but they did not know how to put it rightly.
Butter melts when it is itself heated; the holy saints melt at the sorrow of others. ॥4॥
uttar.125.cau5: My life and my birth have borne fruit; by your grace all my doubt is gone.
Always know me as your own servant. So, Umā, the best of birds said again and again. ॥5॥
uttar.125.do125क: Then Garuḍa, steady of mind, bowed his head at his feet with love,
and went to Vaikuṇṭha, keeping Śrī Rāma in his heart. ॥125 (क)॥
uttar.125.do125ख: Girijā, there is no gain to equal the meeting with saints,
yet it does not come without the grace of Śrī Hari: so the Vedas and Purāṇas sing. ॥125 (ख)॥
uttar.126.cau1: I have told this most holy history; as soon as the ears hear it, the snares of worldly existence fall away,
and love arises for the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma, the wish-fulfilling tree of those who bow to him, the treasury of compassion. ॥1॥
uttar.126.cau2: Sins born of thought, deed and word leave those who listen to this story with ears and mind intent.
Pilgrimage and the whole range of spiritual practices, mastery in yoga, dispassion and knowledge, ॥2॥
uttar.126.cau3: rites of many kinds, dharma, vows and gifts, restraint, self-control, japa, austerity and many sacrifices,
compassion for living beings, service of Brahmins and of the guru, and the excellence of learning, humility and discernment: ॥3॥
uttar.126.cau4: of every practice the Vedas describe, Bhavānī, the fruit is devotion to Śrī Hari.
That devotion to Śrī Rāma, sung in the Vedas, few have won, and those few only by his grace. ॥4॥
uttar.126.do126: Devotion to Śrī Hari, hard even for sages to win, is gained without effort by those men
who hear this story continually, with faith. ॥126॥
uttar.127.cau1: He alone knows all, he alone has true worth, he alone is the knower; he alone is the ornament of the earth, a scholar and a giver.
He alone is devoted to dharma and the protector of his family, whose mind is given to Śrī Rāma's feet. ॥1॥
uttar.127.cau2: He alone is skilled in right conduct and truly wise; he alone has rightly understood the teaching of the Vedas.
He alone is a poet, a scholar and steadfast in battle, who leaves guile behind and worships Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
uttar.127.cau3: Blessed the land where the Gaṅgā flows; blessed the woman who keeps faith with her husband.
Blessed the king who rules by right policy; blessed the Brahmin who does not stray from his dharma. ॥3॥
uttar.127.cau4: Blessed the wealth that takes the first course, giving; blessed and ripe the mind that is set on merit.
Blessed the hour spent in the company of the good; blessed the birth with unbroken devotion to Brahmins. ॥4॥
uttar.127.do127: Blessed is that family, Umā, listen: the world reveres it and it is supremely pure,
the family that brings forth a humble man wholly given to Śrī Rāma. ॥127॥
uttar.128.cau1: I have told this story as my understanding allows, though at first I kept it hidden.
Seeing the great love in your mind, I then told you the story of Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
uttar.128.cau2: This should not be told to the deceitful and the stubborn, nor to one who does not listen with his mind to Śrī Hari's play.
Nor should it be told to the greedy, the angry or the lustful, nor to one who does not worship the Lord of all that moves and does not move. ॥2॥
uttar.128.cau3: Never tell it to one hostile to Brahmins, even if he is a king equal to Indra.
Those fit for Śrī Rāma's story are the ones to whom the company of the good is very dear. ॥3॥
uttar.128.cau4: Those who love the guru's feet, hold to right conduct and serve Brahmins: they too are fit for it.
And to one who holds Śrī Rāma dear as life, it gives a joy beyond all others. ॥4॥
uttar.128.do128: Whoever longs for love of Śrī Rāma's feet, or for the state of liberation,
let him drink this story with feeling from the cups of his ears. ॥128॥
uttar.129.cau1: Girijā, I have told you Śrī Rāma's story, which quells the sins of the Kali age and cleans the mind of its stains.
It is the reviving herb for the sickness of the round of rebirth; so the Vedas and the wise sing of Śrī Rāma's story. ॥1॥
uttar.129.cau2: In it are seven lovely steps, the paths to devotion to Śrī Rāma.
Only he on whom Śrī Hari's grace is very great sets foot upon this path. ॥2॥
uttar.129.cau3: Those who sing this story without guile find the wishes of their heart fulfilled.
For those who tell it, hear it and approve it, the ocean of worldly existence is no wider than a cow's hoofprint, and they step across. ॥3॥
uttar.129.cau4: Having heard the whole story, which delighted her heart, Girijā spoke in gentle words:
My lord, by your grace my doubt is gone, and a new love for Śrī Rāma's feet has arisen. ॥4॥
uttar.129.do129: Lord of the universe, by your grace I am now fulfilled.
Firm devotion to Śrī Rāma has arisen in me, and all my sorrows are past. ॥129॥
uttar.130.cau1: This auspicious dialogue of Śiva and Umā brings happiness and allays sorrow.
It breaks the bonds of worldly existence, destroys doubt, brings joy to the devotees and is beloved of the good. ॥1॥
uttar.130.cau2: Those in the world who worship Śrī Rāma hold nothing as dear as this.
Through Śrī Rāma's grace I have sung, as my understanding allows, this pure and lovely story. ॥2॥
uttar.130.cau3: In this age of Kali there is no other means: not yoga, nor sacrifice, nor japa, austerity, vows or worship.
Remember Śrī Rāma, sing of Śrī Rāma, and hear the host of Śrī Rāma's virtues always. ॥3॥
uttar.130.cau4: Poets, the Vedas, saints and the Purāṇas sing of him whose great vow is to make the fallen pure.
Mind, give up crookedness and worship him; who has ever worshipped Śrī Rāma and not found salvation? ॥4॥
uttar.130.cha1: Listen, foolish mind: who has worshipped Śrī Rāma, purifier of the fallen, and not found salvation?
He delivered many wicked ones: the courtesan, Ajāmila, the hunter, the vulture, the elephant and others.
Even those among the Ābhīras, Yavanas, Kirātas, Khasas, Śvapacas and others who are sin itself
become pure by uttering the Name but once; Rāma, I bow to you. ॥1॥
uttar.130.cha2: Those who tell, hear and sing this story of Śrī Rāma, the ornament of Raghu's line,
wash away the impurity of the Kali age and of the mind, and reach Śrī Rāma's abode without toil.
Whoever finds five or seven of its caupāīs charming and keeps them in his heart,
from him Śrī Rāma takes away the faults born of the five dreadful forms of ignorance. ॥2॥
uttar.130.cha3: He who is beautiful and wise, a treasury of grace, and loves the helpless,
is Śrī Rāma alone; who else equals him in doing good for no gain of his own and in granting liberation?
By the merest trace of his grace even dull-witted Tulasīdāsa has found supreme rest;
there is no lord anywhere like Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
uttar.130.do130क: O hero of the Raghus, there is none as lowly as I, and none who befriends the lowly as you do.
Bearing this in mind, O jewel of Raghu's line, take away the harsh distress of my worldly existence. ॥130 (क)॥
uttar.130.do130ख: Just as a man of desire holds a woman dear, and the greedy hold money dear,
so, O Lord of the Raghus, O Rāma, may you be dear to me without cease. ॥130 (ख)॥
uttar.end.shloka1: The Rāmāyaṇa, hard to fathom, which the Lord Śrī Śambhu, the great poet, composed long ago
so that ceaseless devotion to the lotus feet of glorious Śrī Rāma might be gained,
Tulasīdāsa, holding it to be absorbed in the name of Śrī Rāma, and to still the darkness within his own heart,
has likewise set it in the common tongue as this Mānasa. ॥1॥
uttar.end.shloka2: Holy, taking away sin, ever bringing good, bestowing realised knowledge and devotion,
removing the stain of māyā and delusion, utterly pure, brimming with the water of love, auspicious:
those who bathe with devotion in this Mānasa of Śrī Rāma's deeds
are not scorched by the fierce rays of the sun of worldly existence. ॥2॥
